title: 敢えて
meaning: daringly; deliberately; going out of one's way (to do something difficult or usually avoided)
summary: 敢えて marks that the speaker knowingly does something difficult, risky, or normally avoided, choosing it on purpose despite reasons not to. あえて言う = dare to say it (even if unwelcome), あえて反対する = deliberately raise an objection. Paired with a negative, あえて〜ない means 'not go out of one's way to ~ / not bother': あえて口を出さない = choose not to interfere. The core nuance is a conscious decision against the easier or expected course.
structure: 敢えて＋Verb［plain negative］［choose not to; not bother to ~］
pitfalls: あえて is 'daring to' do something difficult or unwelcome despite reasons not to; わざと is 'on purpose', often with intent to affect someone.
With a negative, あえて〜ない means 'not go out of one's way to ~', not a plain 'don't ~'.

examples.ja: 彼の考えには賛成できなかったが、あえて反論はしなかった。
examples.en: I couldn't agree with his idea, but I chose not to bother voicing an objection.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜考[かんが]えには｜賛成[さんせい]できなかったが、あえて｜反論[はんろん]はしなかった。

examples.ja: 厳しい言い方になるが、あえて忠告させてもらう。
examples.en: This may sound harsh, but I'll dare to offer you a word of advice.
examples.f: ｜厳[きび]しい｜言い方[いいかた]になるが、あえて｜忠告[ちゅうこく]させてもらう。

synonyms.note: わざと is 'deliberately, on purpose' (often to produce an effect on someone); あえて is 'daring to' do something difficult or normally avoided.

title: あくまでも
meaning: to the very end; persistently; strictly / merely (nothing more than)
summary: あくまでも has two linked uses. With a stance or effort it means 'thoroughly, to the bitter end, without giving way': あくまでも戦う = fight to the last, あくまでも自分の意見を通す = insist on one's view no matter what. Framing a statement, it means 'strictly / merely', limiting the claim: あくまでも個人的な意見 = purely a personal opinion, あくまでも一例 = just one example. In both, it stresses that the point holds firmly and without exception.
structure: あくまでも＋Verb／Sentence［persist to the end］
pitfalls: Two senses: with a stance it is 'to the bitter end, persistently'; framing a statement it is 'strictly / merely'. Context decides which.
It is often used to pre-empt misunderstanding — あくまでも〜 signals 'take this as nothing more than ~'.

examples.ja: これはあくまでも仮の数字であって、確定したものではありません。
examples.en: These are strictly provisional figures, not anything finalized.
examples.f: これはあくまでも｜仮[かり]の｜数字[すうじ]であって、｜確定[かくてい]したものではありません。

examples.ja: 彼はあくまでも自分の主張を曲げなかった。
examples.en: He stubbornly refused to bend his position to the very end.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]はあくまでも｜自分[じぶん]の｜主張[しゅちょう]を｜曲[ま]げなかった。

title: 〜あっての
meaning: which exists only thanks to; made possible only by
summary: 〜あっての joins two nouns: 'A あっての B' means B exists or holds true only because A is there — take A away and B collapses. 客あっての商売 = a business is nothing without its customers, 健康あっての仕事 = work only matters if you have your health. It stresses that the first noun is the indispensable foundation for the second. The pattern is emphatic and set in feel.
structure: Noun［essential thing］＋あっての＋Noun［what depends on it］
pitfalls: Order matters: 'A あっての B' means B depends on A, not the other way round.
Both slots are nouns and あっての links them directly — no の or な in between.

examples.ja: 読者あっての雑誌なのだから、読者の声を第一に考えるべきだ。
examples.en: A magazine is nothing without its readers, so their voices should come first.
examples.f: ｜読者[どくしゃ]あっての｜雑誌[ざっし]なのだから、｜読者[どくしゃ]の｜声[こえ]を｜第[だい]｜一[いち]に｜考[かんが]えるべきだ。

examples.ja: 日々の努力あっての結果であり、決して偶然ではない。
examples.en: This result came about only through daily effort; it was by no means luck.
examples.f: ｜日々[ひび]の｜努力[どりょく]あっての｜結果[けっか]であり、｜決[けっ]して｜偶然[ぐうぜん]ではない。

synonyms.note: 〜てこそ also says something holds true 'only through / precisely because of', but attaches to a verb clause; あっての links two nouns.

title: あらかじめ
meaning: in advance; beforehand; ahead of time
summary: あらかじめ is an adverb meaning that something is done ahead of time in preparation for what is to come: あらかじめ調べておく = look into it in advance, あらかじめ予約する = reserve beforehand. It frequently pairs with 〜ておく to mark preparatory action. It belongs to somewhat formal or written speech; 前もって is a plainer everyday equivalent.
structure: あらかじめ＋Verb［often + ておく］
pitfalls: あらかじめ leans formal/written; in casual speech 前もって or 先に is more natural.

examples.ja: 参加する人は、あらかじめ資料に目を通しておいてください。
examples.en: Those attending should look over the materials in advance.
examples.f: ｜参加[さんか]する｜人[ひと]は、あらかじめ｜資料[しりょう]に｜目[め]を｜通[とお]しておいてください。

examples.ja: 問題が起きる可能性は、あらかじめ想定してあった。
examples.en: The possibility of trouble had been anticipated ahead of time.
examples.f: ｜問題[もんだい]が｜起[お]きる｜可能[かのう]｜性[せい]は、あらかじめ｜想定[そうてい]してあった。

title: 案の定
meaning: just as expected; sure enough; as feared
summary: 案の定 marks that something turned out exactly as the speaker had anticipated — typically an unwelcome or worrying outcome. 案の定、失敗した = sure enough, it failed. It sits at the head of a clause and carries a faintly resigned 'I knew it' tone. Because the expectation is usually negative, it is not used for pleasant surprises.
pitfalls: 案の定 usually introduces a foreseen bad outcome; for a neutral or happy 'as expected', やはり is safer.

examples.ja: 準備不足のまま挑んだので、案の定うまくいかなかった。
examples.en: I took it on underprepared, so sure enough it didn't go well.
examples.f: ｜準備[じゅんび]｜不足[ふそく]のまま｜挑[いど]んだので、｜案の定[あんのじょう]うまくいかなかった。

examples.ja: 彼に任せたら、案の定また締め切りに間に合わなかった。
examples.en: I left it to him, and just as I feared, he missed the deadline again.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]に｜任[まか]せたら、｜案の定[あんのじょう]また｜締め切[しめき]りに｜間に合[まにあ]わなかった。

synonyms.note: 果たして (sure enough) also confirms an expectation, but is more neutral and literary; 案の定 leans toward a foreseen bad result.

title: いかなる
meaning: any kind of; whatever; no matter what
summary: いかなる is a formal adnominal meaning 'what kind of / whatever' — a literary equivalent of どんな. It almost always pairs with 〜も or 〜でも to form 'no matter what ~': いかなる理由があっても = whatever the reason, いかなる困難も = any hardship whatsoever. It modifies a noun directly and belongs to written, legal, or ceremonial registers.
structure: いかなる＋Noun＋（も／であっても）
pitfalls: いかなる directly modifies a noun (いかなる場合, not いかなるな場合) and is far more formal than どんな.
It nearly always combines with 〜も／〜でも to mean 'no matter what ~'.

examples.ja: いかなる理由があろうとも、暴力は決して許されない。
examples.en: Whatever the reason may be, violence can never be permitted.
examples.f: いかなる｜理由[りゆう]があろうとも、｜暴力[ぼうりょく]は｜決[けっ]して｜許[ゆる]されない。

examples.ja: 当社はいかなる個人情報も第三者に開示いたしません。
examples.en: Our company will not disclose any personal information whatsoever to third parties.
examples.f: ｜当社[とうしゃ]はいかなる｜個人[こじん]｜情報[じょうほう]も｜第三者[だいさんしゃ]に｜開示[かいじ]いたしません。

synonyms.note: どんな is the everyday 'what kind of'; いかなる is its formal, written counterpart.

related.note: どんなに〜ても stresses degree ('however much'); いかなる〜も ranges over kinds ('whatever ~').
を問わず means 'regardless of ~'; いかなる〜も makes a similar sweep adnominally before a noun.

title: いかに
meaning: how; to what extent; however (much)
summary: いかに is a literary adverb with two main uses. As 'how / to what extent' it often ends in 〜ことか or 〜か to voice a strong impression: いかに難しいことか = how difficult it is. Combined with 〜ても／〜とも it means 'however much ~': いかに急いでも = no matter how much you hurry. It is the formal, written cousin of どんなに／どれほど.
pitfalls: いかに is literary; in speech どんなに or どれほど is more natural.
Don't confuse it with いかにも ('truly; indeed'), which is a different word.

examples.ja: この一枚の写真が、当時の暮らしがいかに厳しかったかを物語っている。
examples.en: This single photograph tells of how harsh life was back then.
examples.f: この｜一[いち]｜枚[まい]の｜写真[しゃしん]が、｜当時[とうじ]の｜暮[く]らしがいかに｜厳[きび]しかったかを｜物語[ものがた]っている。

examples.ja: いかに才能があっても、努力を怠れば大成はしない。
examples.en: However much talent one has, neglecting effort means one will never achieve greatness.
examples.f: いかに｜才能[さいのう]があっても、｜努力[どりょく]を｜怠[おこた]れば｜大成[たいせい]はしない。

related.note: 〜ことか voices strong emotion ('how ~!'); いかに often supplies the 'how' that ことか completes.
どんなに〜ても is the everyday 'however much ~'; いかに〜ても is the literary equivalent.

title: いかにも
meaning: truly; indeed; just like; every bit the ~
summary: いかにも emphasizes that something looks or feels exactly as one would expect of its type — 'truly, indeed, every bit the ~'. いかにも高級そうだ = looks every bit as upscale as you'd imagine, いかにも彼らしい = so typical of him. It often pairs with 〜そう or 〜らしい and conveys that appearances strongly match a stereotype. It can also simply intensify, meaning 'truly / really'.
pitfalls: いかにも frequently teams with 〜らしい or 〜そう to say 'looks exactly like a typical ~'.
Distinct from いかに ('how; to what extent'); いかにも asserts 'truly / just like'.

examples.ja: 彼はいかにも自信ありげに、堂々と壇上に立った。
examples.en: He stepped onto the stage with poise, looking every bit as confident as could be.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]はいかにも｜自信[じしん]ありげに、｜堂々[どうどう]と｜壇上[だんじょう]に｜立[た]った。

examples.ja: その言い訳は、いかにもとってつけたようで説得力がなかった。
examples.en: The excuse sounded so obviously contrived that it carried no weight.
examples.f: その｜言い訳[いいわけ]は、いかにもとってつけたようで｜説得[せっとく]｜力[りょく]がなかった。

synonyms.note: さすが praises something for living up to its reputation; いかにも neutrally notes that appearance matches the expected type.

related.note: 〜らしい says something is typical of its kind; いかにも often reinforces it ('so very ~-like').

title: 〜いかんだ・〜いかんでは・〜いかんによっては
kana: いかんだ・いかんでは・いかんによっては
romaji: ikan da / ikan dewa / ikan ni yotte wa
meaning: depending on ~; hinging on what ~ is
summary: 〜いかんだ (from 如何) makes an outcome depend on the nature or state of the preceding noun — 'it depends on ~'. 君の努力いかんだ = it hinges on your effort; 結果いかんでは中止もありうる = depending on the results, it may even be called off. It attaches to a noun, sometimes with の (成績のいかんによっては). The register is formal and often official.
structure: Noun＋（の）＋いかんだ／いかんでは／いかんによっては
pitfalls: This いかん means 如何 ('how / what state'); it is unrelated to the いかん of 〜てはいかん ('must not').
The result clause states what varies with that factor, often a conditional consequence.

examples.ja: 計画を続けるかどうかは、今後の資金繰りいかんだ。
examples.en: Whether the project continues hinges on how the funding goes from here.
examples.f: ｜計画[けいかく]を｜続[つづ]けるかどうかは、｜今後[こんご]の｜資金繰[しきんぐ]りいかんだ。

examples.ja: 検査の結果いかんでは、手術が必要になるかもしれない。
examples.en: Depending on the results of the examination, surgery may become necessary.
examples.f: ｜検査[けんさ]の｜結果[けっか]いかんでは、｜手術[しゅじゅつ]が｜必要[ひつよう]になるかもしれない。

synonyms.note: 次第だ・次第で also means 'depending on ~' and is a touch less stiff; いかんだ is more formal and official.
〜によって marks 'depending on / according to'; いかんだ concentrates the dependence into a final 'it hinges on ~'.

title: 〜いかんにかかわらず・〜いかんによらず・〜いかんをとわず
kana: いかんにかかわらず・いかんによらず・いかんをとわず
romaji: ikan ni kakawarazu / ikan ni yorazu / ikan o towazu
meaning: regardless of (what ~ is); irrespective of ~
summary: 〜いかんにかかわらず (also いかんによらず／いかんを問わず) says that whatever the state of the preceding noun, the result is unaffected — 'regardless of ~'. 理由のいかんにかかわらず = regardless of the reason; 結果いかんによらず = whatever the outcome. It attaches to a noun, often with の, and is firmly formal, common in rules and notices.
structure: Noun＋（の）＋いかんにかかわらず／いかんによらず／いかんを問わず
pitfalls: Contrast いかんでは ('depending on ~', outcome varies) with いかんにかかわらず ('regardless of ~', outcome does not vary).

examples.ja: 理由のいかんにかかわらず、遅刻は遅刻として扱われる。
examples.en: Regardless of the reason, being late is treated as being late.
examples.f: ｜理由[りゆう]のいかんにかかわらず、｜遅刻[ちこく]は｜遅刻[ちこく]として｜扱[あつか]われる。

examples.ja: 審査の結果いかんを問わず、提出された書類は返却いたしません。
examples.en: Irrespective of the outcome of the review, submitted documents will not be returned.
examples.f: ｜審査[しんさ]の｜結果[けっか]いかんを｜問[と]わず、｜提出[ていしゅつ]された｜書類[しょるい]は｜返却[へんきゃく]いたしません。

synonyms.note: 〜にかかわらず means 'regardless of ~' broadly; いかんにかかわらず specifically sweeps over 'whatever the state of ~'.
〜を問わず ('regardless of ~') attaches to a plain noun; いかんを問わず adds the 如何 'whatever its nature' framing.

related.note: 〜にもかかわらず means 'despite ~' (contrast with an established fact); いかんにかかわらず means 'no matter what ~ is'.

title: いずれにしても・いずれにしろ・いずれにせよ
kana: いずれにしても・いずれにしろ・いずれにせよ
romaji: izure ni shitemo / izure ni shiro / izure ni seyo
meaning: in any case; either way; whichever it is
summary: いずれにしても (also いずれにしろ／いずれにせよ) sets aside which of several possibilities holds and moves to a conclusion that applies to all of them — 'either way, in any case'. 賛成でも反対でも、いずれにせよ理由を聞きたい = for or against, either way I want to hear your reasons. It works as a transition, dismissing the alternatives as not changing what follows. にせよ／にしろ are more formal than にしても.
structure: （Options）＋いずれにしても／いずれにしろ／いずれにせよ、＋Sentence
pitfalls: The three variants differ mainly in tone: にしても is neutral, にしろ／にせよ are more formal or written.

examples.ja: 行くか行かないか、いずれにせよ早めに返事をする必要がある。
examples.en: Whether I go or not, either way I need to reply soon.
examples.f: ｜行[い]くか｜行[い]かないか、いずれにせよ｜早[はや]めに｜返事[へんじ]をする｜必要[ひつよう]がある。

examples.ja: 原因はまだ特定できていないが、いずれにしても再発防止策は欠かせない。
examples.en: The cause hasn't been pinned down yet, but in any case, measures to prevent a recurrence are essential.
examples.f: ｜原因[げんいん]はまだ｜特定[とくてい]できていないが、いずれにしても｜再発[さいはつ]｜防止[ぼうし]｜策[さく]は｜欠[か]かせない。

synonyms.note: 〜にしても〜にしても lays out the specific options ('whether A or B'); いずれにしても bundles them into a single 'either way'.

related.note: 〜はともかく sets an issue aside to focus elsewhere; いずれにしても concludes that the alternatives don't change the result.

title: 〜以前
meaning: before even ~; more basic than the question of ~
summary: Beyond its plain sense of 'before (a time)', 〜以前 (often 〜以前の問題) marks that something is too basic to even reach the stated issue — 'before we even get to ~'. マナー以前の問題だ = it's a problem that comes before manners even enter into it; 好き嫌い以前に = before it's even a matter of liking or not. It attaches to a noun and frames the stated point as a later, secondary concern.
pitfalls: In this sense 以前 means 'a step more basic than ~', not simply 'before (in time)'.

examples.ja: 締め切りを守れないのは、能力以前の問題だ。
examples.en: Failing to meet deadlines is a problem that comes before ability even enters into it.
examples.f: ｜締め切[しめき]りを｜守[まも]れないのは、｜能力[のうりょく]｜以前[いぜん]の｜問題[もんだい]だ。

examples.ja: 彼とは、恋愛以前にまず信頼関係が築けていなかった。
examples.en: With him, it wasn't even a question of romance — we hadn't built any trust to begin with.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]とは、｜恋愛[れんあい]｜以前[いぜん]にまず｜信頼[しんらい]｜関係[かんけい]が｜築[きづ]けていなかった。

related.note: 〜どころか overturns an assumption ('far from ~'); 以前の問題 says the matter is too basic to even reach ~.

title: 〜うちに入らない
meaning: doesn't count as; can hardly be called (a real ~)
summary: 〜うちに入らない says that something falls short of qualifying as a full or proper example of a category — 'that doesn't count as ~'. この程度の雨なら降ったうちに入らない = a little rain like this hardly counts as rain; 一度会っただけでは知り合いのうちに入らない = meeting once doesn't make you acquaintances. It dismisses the case as too slight to bear that label.
pitfalls: This うちに入らない judges that something fails to qualify as a category; it is not the time expression 〜うちに ('while ~').

examples.ja: これくらいの荷物なら、重いうちに入らないよ。
examples.en: Luggage this light hardly counts as heavy.
examples.f: これくらいの｜荷物[にもつ]なら、｜重[おも]いうちに｜入[はい]らないよ。

examples.ja: 年に数冊読むくらいでは、読書家のうちに入らないだろう。
examples.en: Reading just a few books a year scarcely qualifies you as an avid reader.
examples.f: ｜年[とし]に｜数[すう]｜冊[さつ]｜読[よ]むくらいでは、｜読書[どくしょ]｜家[か]のうちに｜入[はい]らないだろう。

related.note: 〜にすぎない says something is 'no more than ~'; うちに入らない says it doesn't even qualify as ~.

title: 〜思いをする
meaning: to have a ~ experience; to feel ~ (an emotion) keenly
summary: 〜思いをする describes undergoing an experience colored by a particular feeling, with the feeling word placed before 思い. 悔しい思いをする = go through something galling; つらい思いをする = have a painful experience; 恥ずかしい思いをする = suffer embarrassment. It takes an い-adjective, or a な-adjective + な, before 思い and focuses on how an experience felt to the person.
pitfalls: The adjective describes how the experience felt; 思いをする centers the subjective feeling, not a mere action.

examples.ja: みんなの前で名前を間違えられ、恥ずかしい思いをした。
examples.en: Having my name gotten wrong in front of everyone, I felt thoroughly embarrassed.
examples.f: みんなの｜前[まえ]で｜名前[なまえ]を｜間違[まちが]えられ、｜恥[は]ずかしい｜思[おも]いをした。

examples.ja: あの一言で、彼女はさぞ悔しい思いをしたことだろう。
examples.en: That single remark must have made her feel deeply mortified.
examples.f: あの｜一言[ひとこと]で、｜彼女[かのじょ]はさぞ｜悔[くや]しい｜思[おも]いをしたことだろう。

title: およそ
meaning: roughly; approximately; generally; (with a negative) utterly
summary: およそ has a few uses. Before a number it means 'roughly, about': およそ千人 = about a thousand people. As a sentence adverb it means 'generally speaking, in broad terms': およそ物事には順序がある = in general, things have an order. Reinforcing a negative, it means 'utterly, not in the least': およそ現実的でない = utterly unrealistic. Context and what follows tell the senses apart.
pitfalls: With a negative, およそ means 'utterly / not in the least', not 'approximately'.

examples.ja: その計画は、およそ現実味のないものだった。
examples.en: That plan was utterly devoid of realism.
examples.f: その｜計画[けいかく]は、およそ｜現実味[げんじつみ]のないものだった。

examples.ja: 会場にはおよそ二千人が詰めかけた。
examples.en: Roughly two thousand people packed into the venue.
examples.f: ｜会場[かいじょう]にはおよそ｜二[に]｜千[せん]｜人[にん]が｜詰[つ]めかけた。

synonyms.note: おおよそ is essentially the same word in the 'roughly / approximately' sense; およそ additionally carries the emphatic 'utterly (not)' use.

title: 〜折に・〜折には
meaning: on the occasion of; when (the chance arises)
summary: 〜折に(は) marks a particular occasion or opportune moment for doing something — 'when, on the occasion of'. 上京の折には = when you come up to Tokyo; お近くにお越しの折は = should you happen to be nearby. It attaches to a noun + の or a plain-form verb and belongs to polite, somewhat formal speech, often in greetings and invitations. It tends to mark a good or fitting occasion.
pitfalls: 折に is polite and formal, typical of set greetings; for a neutral 'when', 時に is plainer.
It usually marks a fitting or welcome occasion, not just any random moment.

examples.ja: 次に上京する折には、ぜひご連絡ください。
examples.en: When you next come up to the city, do please get in touch.
examples.f: ｜次[つぎ]に｜上京[じょうきょう]する｜折[おり]には、ぜひご｜連絡[れんらく]ください。

examples.ja: 先日お会いした折に、その件は伺っております。
examples.en: I heard about the matter when we met the other day.
examples.f: ｜先日[せんじつ]お｜会[あ]いした｜折[おり]に、その｜件[けん]は｜伺[うかが]っております。

synonyms.note: 〜際に is a formal 'on the occasion of / when'; 折に is similarly polite but favors welcome, opportune occasions and set greetings.

related.note: 〜にあたって marks 'on the occasion of' a significant, one-off undertaking; 折に marks a fitting moment, often social or recurring.

title: 〜が〜なら〜も〜だ
meaning: like A, like B; both are (equally) at fault / just as bad
summary: 〜が〜なら〜も〜だ is a set pattern that criticizes two parties at once by pairing them — 'if A is like this, then B is no better either'. 親が親なら子も子だ = with parents like that, no wonder the child is the same; 客が客なら店も店だ = the customers are bad, but so is the shop. The same noun is usually repeated in each slot, and the tone is one of paired disapproval.
pitfalls: The same noun repeats in each pair (親が親なら子も子だ); the pattern blames both sides at once.
It is a critical, complaining expression, not a neutral comparison.

examples.ja: 客が客なら店も店だ。どちらも謝ろうとしない。
examples.en: The customers are impossible, but the shop is just as bad — neither will apologize.
examples.f: ｜客[きゃく]が｜客[きゃく]なら｜店[みせ]も｜店[みせ]だ。どちらも｜謝[あやま]ろうとしない。

examples.ja: 親が親なら子も子で、家族そろって時間にルーズだ。
examples.en: Like parent, like child — the whole family is equally lax about time.
examples.f: ｜親[おや]が｜親[おや]なら｜子[こ]も｜子[こ]で、｜家族[かぞく]そろって｜時間[じかん]にルーズだ。

title: 〜か否か
meaning: whether or not
summary: 〜か否か is the formal, written equivalent of 〜かどうか — 'whether or not'. 実現できるか否か = whether or not it can be realized; 事実か否かを確かめる = verify whether or not it is true. 否 (いな) is a literary 'no', so the phrase reads as stiff and is common in essays, reports, and formal speech. It follows a plain form or a noun.
pitfalls: か否か is markedly formal/written; in ordinary conversation かどうか is the natural choice.

examples.ja: この計画が実現可能か否かは、予算次第である。
examples.en: Whether or not this plan is feasible depends on the budget.
examples.f: この｜計画[けいかく]が｜実現[じつげん]｜可能[かのう]か｜否[いな]かは、｜予算[よさん]｜次第[しだい]である。

examples.ja: 提出された証言が真実か否かを、慎重に見極める必要がある。
examples.en: We must carefully determine whether or not the testimony given is true.
examples.f: ｜提出[ていしゅつ]された｜証言[しょうげん]が｜真実[しんじつ]か｜否[いな]かを、｜慎重[しんちょう]に｜見極[みきわ]める｜必要[ひつよう]がある。

synonyms.note: 〜かどうか is the everyday 'whether or not'; か否か is its formal, literary equivalent.

title: 〜甲斐もなく
meaning: to no avail; in vain, despite one's efforts
summary: 〜甲斐もなく says that despite the effort or care put in, it brought no worthwhile result — 'for all one's ~, it was in vain'. 看病の甲斐もなく = despite all the nursing, to no avail; 努力の甲斐もなく不合格だった = for all the effort, still failed. It attaches to a noun + の or a verb, and the following clause states the disappointing outcome. Its positive counterpart is 甲斐があって ('the effort paid off').
structure: Verb［plain form／た form］＋甲斐もなく
pitfalls: 甲斐もなく always leads to a disappointing result; if the effort paid off, use 甲斐があって instead.

examples.ja: 懸命な治療の甲斐もなく、祖父は静かに息を引き取った。
examples.en: Despite the devoted treatment, to no avail, my grandfather quietly passed away.
examples.f: ｜懸命[けんめい]な｜治療[ちりょう]の｜甲斐[かい]もなく、｜祖父[そふ]は｜静[しず]かに｜息[いき]を｜引き取[ひきと]った。

examples.ja: 必死に練習した甲斐もなく、本番では実力を出しきれなかった。
examples.en: For all my desperate practice, in vain, I couldn't show my full ability on the day.
examples.f: ｜必死[ひっし]に｜練習[れんしゅう]した｜甲斐[かい]もなく、｜本番[ほんばん]では｜実力[じつりょく]を｜出[だ]しきれなかった。

antonyms.note: 〜甲斐がある means the effort was worthwhile and paid off; 甲斐もなく means it was all for nothing.

title: 〜限りだ
meaning: feel utterly ~; extremely (of an emotion)
summary: 〜限りだ, after an emotion word, expresses that the speaker feels that emotion to the utmost — 'I couldn't be more ~'. 嬉しい限りだ = I couldn't be happier; 心細い限りだ = I feel utterly forlorn; 羨ましい限りだ = I'm terribly envious. It takes an い-adjective, or a な-adjective + な, of feeling and states the speaker's own emotion at its extreme. The tone is somewhat formal.
pitfalls: 限りだ attaches to emotion words and describes the speaker's own feeling at its peak; it isn't used for others' emotions or for non-emotional degrees.

examples.ja: 旧友が遠くから駆けつけてくれて、心強い限りだ。
examples.en: With an old friend rushing over from afar to help, I couldn't feel more reassured.
examples.f: ｜旧友[きゅうゆう]が｜遠[とお]くから｜駆[か]けつけてくれて、｜心強[こころづよ]い｜限[かぎ]りだ。

examples.ja: 長年の研究がこうして実を結び、嬉しい限りです。
examples.en: To see many years of research bear fruit like this, I couldn't be happier.
examples.f: ｜長年[ながねん]の｜研究[けんきゅう]がこうして｜実[み]を｜結[むす]び、｜嬉[うれ]しい｜限[かぎ]りです。

synonyms.note: 〜の至り expresses reaching the height of a feeling (formal, set phrases like 光栄の至り); 限りだ is a slightly less rigid 'utterly ~'.
〜の極み marks the extreme peak of a state (感激の極み); 限りだ centers the speaker's own emotion 'to the utmost'.

related.note: 〜極まりない says a quality is 'extreme beyond limit' (often negative); 限りだ voices a personal emotion at its height.

title: 〜かたがた
meaning: while also; combining the purpose of; partly in order to
summary: 〜かたがた marks that a single action serves two purposes at once — the main one, plus the かたがた one done along with it. It attaches to a noun, almost always a formal social act such as 挨拶かたがた (partly to pay one's respects), お礼かたがた (partly to say thanks), or お詫びかたがた (partly to apologize). The tone is stiff and old-fashioned, at home in letters and polite visits. One deed accomplishes both aims.
pitfalls: Attaches to a noun (usually a formal suru-noun like 挨拶・お礼・お詫び), not to a verb.
One single action fulfils both purposes at the same time; it is not two separate errands.
Formal and written; in casual speech がてら or ついでに are more natural.

examples.ja: 先日のお礼かたがた、近くまで参りましたのでお立ち寄りいたしました。
examples.en: Partly to thank you for the other day, and since I happened to be in the area, I have dropped by.
examples.f: ｜先日[せんじつ]のお｜礼[れい]かたがた、｜近[ちか]くまで｜参[まい]りましたのでお｜立ち寄[たちよ]りいたしました。

examples.ja: 帰省かたがた、長らくご無沙汰していた恩師のお宅を訪ねた。
examples.en: On my trip back to my hometown, I also visited the home of the mentor I had long neglected to contact.
examples.f: ｜帰省[きせい]かたがた、｜長[なが]らくご｜無沙汰[ぶさた]していた｜恩師[おんし]のお｜宅[たく]を｜訪[たず]ねた。

synonyms.note: がてら does two things on one outing too, but is more casual and often involves physically going somewhere; かたがた is formal and noun-only.

related.note: ついでに frames the second action as an afterthought taken while doing the first; かたがた presents both purposes as intended together, in stiffer register.
かたわら pairs two sustained activities over a long span; かたがた joins two purposes in one single act.

title: 〜かたわら
meaning: while; alongside (one's main occupation or activity)
summary: 〜かたわら presents two ongoing pursuits: while doing A as one's main occupation, one also does B on the side over the same period. 傍ら literally means 'beside', and the figure is of B running parallel to a central activity — 仕事のかたわら (alongside one's work), 教えるかたわら (while teaching). It attaches to a dictionary-form verb or a noun + の, and belongs to written, somewhat literary style.
pitfalls: Describes two activities sustained over a long period (a main one plus a side one), not two acts done on a single occasion.
The clause before かたわら names the main occupation; the side activity comes after.
Written and literary; heavier than everyday 〜ながら.

examples.ja: 彼は大学で経済学を教えるかたわら、小説を書き続けている。
examples.en: Alongside teaching economics at the university, he continues to write novels.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜大学[だいがく]で｜経済[けいざい]｜学[がく]を｜教[おし]えるかたわら、｜小説[しょうせつ]を｜書[か]き｜続[つづ]けている。

examples.ja: 家業を手伝うかたわら、地域のボランティア活動にも力を注いできた。
examples.en: While helping with the family business, she has also devoted her energy to local volunteer work.
examples.f: ｜家業[かぎょう]を｜手伝[てつだ]うかたわら、｜地域[ちいき]のボランティア｜活動[かつどう]にも｜力[ちから]を｜注[そそ]いできた。

synonyms.note: ながら links two actions happening at the same moment; かたわら links two ongoing pursuits carried on over a long stretch of one's life.

related.note: かたがた joins two purposes within one single act; かたわら sets one long-term side activity beside a main occupation.

title: かつて
meaning: once; formerly; (with a negative) never before
summary: かつて is a formal adverb pointing to some time in the past: 'once, formerly, in days gone by'. かつて栄えた町 = a town that once flourished. With a following negative it means 'never (up to now)', as in かつてない ('unprecedented, never seen before'). It carries a literary, retrospective flavour and is common in writing and formal narration rather than casual chat.
pitfalls: Formal and written; in everyday speech 昔 or 以前 sound more natural.
Followed by a negative it means 'never before': かつてない規模 = a scale never seen until now.

examples.ja: この辺りはかつて城下町として大いに栄えた土地である。
examples.en: This area is land that once flourished greatly as a castle town.
examples.f: この｜辺[あた]りはかつて｜城下町[じょうかまち]として｜大[おお]いに｜栄[さか]えた｜土地[とち]である。

examples.ja: かつてないほどの大雪に、街の交通は完全に麻痺した。
examples.en: Amid snowfall on a scale never seen before, the city's transport was completely paralyzed.
examples.f: かつてないほどの｜大雪[おおゆき]に、｜街[まち]の｜交通[こうつう]は｜完全[かんぜん]に｜麻痺[まひ]した。

related.note: 未だに fixes on a state that still persists into the present; かつて points back to a moment in the past.

title: 〜がてら
meaning: while; on the same occasion as; taking the opportunity of
summary: 〜がてら marks doing two things on one occasion, typically while going somewhere: you set out to do A and, on the same trip, also do B. 散歩がてら (while out for a walk), 買い物に行きがてら (on the way to shop). It attaches to a suru-noun or a verb stem. A is the nominal reason for the outing and B is folded in along the way — lighter and more everyday than the formal かたがた.
pitfalls: One single occasion, usually involving going somewhere; the two actions share the same trip.
Attaches to a noun or verb stem — 行きがてら, not 行くがてら.
More casual than かたがた, which is reserved for formal social acts.

examples.ja: 散歩がてら、駅前に新しくできたパン屋をのぞいてみた。
examples.en: While out for a walk, I popped into the new bakery that had opened in front of the station.
examples.f: ｜散歩[さんぽ]がてら、｜駅前[えきまえ]に｜新[あたら]しくできたパン｜屋[や]をのぞいてみた。

examples.ja: 買い物に行きがてら、借りていた本を図書館に返してきた。
examples.en: On my way out to go shopping, I returned the books I had borrowed to the library.
examples.f: ｜買い物[かいもの]に｜行[い]きがてら、｜借[か]りていた｜本[ほん]を｜図書館[としょかん]に｜返[かえ]してきた。

synonyms.note: かたがた joins two purposes in stiff, formal register and only attaches to nouns; がてら is casual and often centres on a trip.
ついでに treats the second act as an incidental afterthought; がてら presents both as roughly planned into the one outing.

related.note: かたわら pairs two long-term pursuits; がてら pairs two acts squeezed into a single occasion.

title: 〜かと思いきや
meaning: contrary to what one thought; one would think ~, but actually
summary: 〜かと思いきや sets up an expectation and then overturns it: you thought A, but in fact the opposite or something quite different turned out to be the case. 思いきや is a fixed classical form and gives the phrase a slightly literary, sometimes wry tone. It attaches to a plain-form clause (a noun or な-adjective may drop だ). The reality after it always contradicts the assumption before it.
pitfalls: What follows always reverses the expectation — never merely continues or confirms it.
思いきや is a frozen classical form; it is not conjugated further.
Literary and often lightly humorous; not for neutral, matter-of-fact writing.

examples.ja: 作業は簡単に終わるかと思いきや、予想外の問題が次々と出てきた。
examples.en: I thought the work would finish easily, but contrary to expectation one unforeseen problem after another cropped up.
examples.f: ｜作業[さぎょう]は｜簡単[かんたん]に｜終[お]わるかと｜思[おも]いきや、｜予想[よそう]｜外[がい]の｜問題[もんだい]が｜次々[つぎつぎ]と｜出[で]てきた。

examples.ja: 桜はもう散ってしまったかと思いきや、日陰にはまだ花が残っていた。
examples.en: I assumed the cherry blossoms had already fallen, but to my surprise some flowers still lingered in the shade.
examples.f: ｜桜[さくら]はもう｜散[ち]ってしまったかと｜思[おも]いきや、｜日陰[ひかげ]にはまだ｜花[はな]が｜残[のこ]っていた。

related.note: に反して neutrally states a result running counter to an expectation or standard; かと思いきや dramatizes the speaker's own assumption being upended.
とはいえ concedes a point then qualifies it; かと思いきや reveals that the anticipated situation was simply wrong.

title: 〜可能性がある
meaning: there is a possibility that; it is possible that
summary: 〜可能性がある states that some outcome is objectively possible — 'there is a possibility that ~'. It attaches to a plain-form verb or adjective, or to a noun via の / である. 中止になる可能性がある = there is a chance it will be called off. The degree can be tuned with 高い or 低い (可能性が高い = a strong possibility). Compared with かもしれない it is more analytical and neutral, suited to reports and formal explanation.
structure: Noun＋の／である＋可能性がある
pitfalls: States an objective likelihood; it is more formal and detached than the speaker's guess かもしれない.
Modify the strength with 高い／低い rather than treating every possibility as equal.

examples.ja: 台風の影響で、明日の便が欠航になる可能性がある。
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, there is a possibility that tomorrow's flight will be cancelled.
examples.f: ｜台風[たいふう]の｜影響[えいきょう]で、｜明日[あした]の｜便[びん]が｜欠航[けっこう]になる｜可能[かのう]｜性[せい]がある。

examples.ja: この数値は、測定上の誤差である可能性も否定できない。
examples.en: We cannot rule out the possibility that this figure is a measurement error.
examples.f: この｜数値[すうち]は、｜測定[そくてい]｜上[じょう]の｜誤差[ごさ]である｜可能[かのう]｜性[せい]も｜否定[ひてい]できない。

synonyms.note: かもしれない voices the speaker's own conjecture; 可能性がある frames the same chance as an objective, measurable one.
かねない warns that a bad outcome could happen; 可能性がある is neutral about whether the outcome is good or bad.

related.note: 恐れがある reserves itself for the risk of an undesirable result; 可能性がある covers any outcome.

title: 〜が早いか
meaning: no sooner than; the instant that
summary: 〜が早いか says that the moment A happened, B followed almost simultaneously — 'no sooner had A than B'. It attaches to a dictionary-form (occasionally た-form) verb and belongs to written, narrative style. The second event is typically a sudden, vigorous action that actually took place, so the whole describes a real past sequence with the two events nearly overlapping in time.
pitfalls: The second event follows almost instantly — the two are essentially simultaneous, not merely 'soon after'.
B describes something that really happened (past), not a command, intention, or negative.
Literary and written; unnatural in casual conversation.

examples.ja: 終業のベルが鳴るが早いか、生徒たちは教室を飛び出していった。
examples.en: No sooner had the closing bell rung than the students dashed out of the classroom.
examples.f: ｜終業[しゅうぎょう]のベルが｜鳴[な]るが｜早[はや]いか、｜生徒[せいと]たちは｜教室[きょうしつ]を｜飛び出[とびだ]していった。

examples.ja: その知らせを聞くが早いか、彼は席を立って部屋を出て行った。
examples.en: The instant he heard the news, he rose from his seat and left the room.
examples.f: その｜知[し]らせを｜聞[き]くが｜早[はや]いか、｜彼[かれ]は｜席[せき]を｜立[た]って｜部屋[へや]を｜出[で]て｜行[い]った。

synonyms.note: や否や is nearly identical and equally literary; が早いか leans a touch more toward a briskly following, deliberate action.
なり also marks an immediate next action, often one the speaker found unexpected; が早いか stresses the near-simultaneity of the timing.

related.note: たとたん often marks a sudden change or realization at that moment; が早いか highlights a swift follow-on action in narration.

title: 〜がましい
meaning: bordering on; smacking of; having an (unfavourable) air of
summary: 〜がましい is a suffix that turns a noun or verb stem into an い-adjective meaning 'coming across as ~, smacking of ~', always with a disapproving edge. It lives in a fixed set of formations: 言い訳がましい (sounding like an excuse), 押し付けがましい (pushy), 未練がましい (clinging), 差し出がましい (presumptuous). The word describes an unwelcome quality that a manner or attitude gives off.
pitfalls: Always carries a negative, critical nuance; never used to praise.
Not freely productive — it appears in a limited stock of set forms (言い訳がましい, 押し付けがましい, 未練がましい, etc.).
The result is an い-adjective and inflects like one (がましく, がましかった).

examples.ja: 言い訳がましく聞こえるかもしれないが、事情だけは説明させてほしい。
examples.en: It may sound like I'm making excuses, but please at least let me explain the circumstances.
examples.f: ｜言い訳[いいわけ]がましく｜聞[き]こえるかもしれないが、｜事情[じじょう]だけは｜説明[せつめい]させてほしい。

examples.ja: そんな押し付けがましい言い方では、相手も素直に従う気にはなれない。
examples.en: With such a pushy way of putting it, the other person won't feel inclined to go along willingly.
examples.f: そんな｜押し付[おしつ]けがましい｜言い方[いいかた]では、｜相手[あいて]も｜素直[すなお]に｜従[したが]う｜気[き]にはなれない。

synonyms.note: めく neutrally says something 'shows signs of / has a touch of'; がましい specifically adds an unfavourable, off-putting flavour.
っぽい is casual and can be neutral ('-ish, tends to'); がましい is formal and inherently critical.

title: 〜からある・〜からする・〜からの
kana: からある・からする・からの
romaji: kara aru / kara suru / kara no
meaning: as much/many as; no less than; upwards of
summary: This pattern follows a number and stresses that the amount is impressively large — 'no less than, a good ~'. からある is used for size, weight, or quantity; からする for price or cost; からの comes before a noun for numbers of things or people. 五十キロからある荷物, 百万円からする品, 百人からの人. In every case the speaker is underscoring that the figure is at least that big.
pitfalls: からある for quantity, size, or weight; からする for prices; からの directly before a noun for counts.
Used only to emphasize large amounts, never small ones.
Means 'at least that much (and impressively so)', not an exact figure.

examples.ja: 彼は五十キロからある大きな荷物を、軽々と肩に担ぎ上げた。
examples.en: He hoisted onto his shoulder with ease a huge load of no less than fifty kilograms.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜五[ご]｜十[じゅう]キロからある｜大[おお]きな｜荷物[にもつ]を、｜軽々[かるがる]と｜肩[かた]に｜担[かつ]ぎ｜上[あ]げた。

examples.ja: この壺は、一つ百万円からする高級な骨董品らしい。
examples.en: This vase is apparently a high-class antique costing no less than a million yen apiece.
examples.f: この｜壺[つぼ]は、｜一[ひと]つ｜百[ひゃく]｜万[まん]｜円[えん]からする｜高級[こうきゅう]な｜骨董[こっとう]｜品[ひん]らしい。

title: かれ〜かれ
meaning: whether ~ or ~; either way; to a greater or lesser degree
summary: かれ〜かれ pairs two opposite adjective stems in a fixed idiom meaning that whichever of the two holds, the same conclusion applies. It survives only in set phrases: 遅かれ早かれ (sooner or later), 多かれ少なかれ (more or less, to some degree), 良かれ悪しかれ (for better or worse). The かれ is a classical adjective ending, so these are memorized wholes rather than a freely built pattern.
structure: い-adjective［classical stem］＋かれ＋（opposite）＋かれ［fixed set phrase］
pitfalls: Occurs only in fixed pairs (遅かれ早かれ, 多かれ少なかれ, 良かれ悪しかれ); not freely productive.
良かれ／悪しかれ use irregular classical forms from よし／あし, not the modern いい／悪い.
The point is that both alternatives lead to the same result, so it is not a real choice.

examples.ja: 遅かれ早かれ、隠していた事実はいずれ明るみに出るだろう。
examples.en: Sooner or later, the facts that were hidden will eventually come to light.
examples.f: ｜遅[おそ]かれ｜早[はや]かれ、｜隠[かく]していた｜事実[じじつ]はいずれ｜明[あか]るみに｜出[で]るだろう。

examples.ja: 人は誰でも、多かれ少なかれ何らかの欠点を抱えているものだ。
examples.en: Everyone, to a greater or lesser degree, carries some sort of flaw.
examples.f: ｜人[ひと]は｜誰[だれ]でも、｜多[おお]かれ｜少[すく]なかれ｜何[なん]らかの｜欠点[けってん]を｜抱[かか]えているものだ。

title: がん〜
meaning: (slang) hard; intensely; totally (intensifying prefix)
summary: がん〜 is a colloquial slang prefix that intensifies the word it attaches to, conveying 'hard, intensely, full-on'. It combines with a small set of verbs and nouns: がん見 (staring hard), がん無視 (totally ignoring), がん飛ばす (glaring at). It belongs firmly to casual spoken Japanese, especially among younger speakers, and would be out of place in any formal or written context.
pitfalls: Slang — completely inappropriate in formal or written Japanese.
Combines only with a limited stock of words (がん見, がん無視, がん飛ばす); not freely attachable.
Emphasizes intensity of an action, not size or quantity.

examples.ja: さっきから前の席の人にがん見されていて、ちょっと気まずい。
examples.en: The person in the seat ahead has been staring hard at me for a while now, and it's a bit awkward.
examples.f: さっきから｜前[まえ]の｜席[せき]の｜人[ひと]にがん｜見[み]されていて、ちょっと｜気[き]まずい。

examples.ja: せっかく話しかけたのに、あいつにがん無視されてしまった。
examples.en: Even though I went to the trouble of speaking to him, he totally ignored me.
examples.f: せっかく｜話[はな]しかけたのに、あいつにがん｜無視[むし]されてしまった。

title: 〜きっての
meaning: the best/foremost ~ in (a group, place, or field)
summary: 〜きっての singles someone or something out as the very best within a defined group, place, or field. The noun before きって names the domain, and the noun after is what ranks number one in it: この業界きっての実力者 = the leading figure in this industry, 当代きっての名優 = the finest actor of the age. It is a set adnominal form (きって + の + noun) with a somewhat elevated, admiring tone.
pitfalls: The first noun is the group or arena within which someone is foremost; the second is the one who ranks highest.
Fixed as きっての directly before a noun; it always modifies a following noun.
Used for a superlative standing ('the best in ~'), generally in a positive, admiring sense.

examples.ja: 彼女はこの業界きっての実力者として、広く名を知られている。
examples.en: She is widely known as the most capable figure in this industry.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]はこの｜業界[ぎょうかい]きっての｜実力[じつりょく]｜者[しゃ]として、｜広[ひろ]く｜名[な]を｜知[し]られている。

examples.ja: あの古書店の主人は、町きっての物知りとして評判だ。
examples.en: The owner of that used-book shop has a reputation as the most knowledgeable person in town.
examples.f: あの｜古書[こしょ]｜店[てん]の｜主人[しゅじん]は、｜町[まち]きっての｜物知[ものし]りとして｜評判[ひょうばん]だ。

related.note: ならでは points to a quality only that person or place could produce; きっての ranks someone as number one within a group.

title: 〜嫌いがある
meaning: to have a (bad) tendency to; to be inclined to
summary: 〜嫌いがある points out an unfavourable disposition — a tendency to do something the speaker regards as regrettable. 物事を悲観的に考える嫌いがある = to have a tendency to think about things pessimistically. It attaches to a dictionary- or ない-form verb, or a noun + の, and belongs to formal, written style. The 嫌い here means 'inclination', unrelated to the everyday word for 'dislike'.
structure: Verb［dictionary form／ない form］＋嫌いがある
pitfalls: Describes a negative predisposition and carries mild criticism; not used for good tendencies.
嫌い here means 'inclination', not 'dislike' — don't read it as the emotion.
Formal and written; heavier and more judgmental than casual がち.

examples.ja: 彼はどうも物事を大げさに考える嫌いがある。
examples.en: He does seem to have a tendency to think about things in an exaggerated way.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]はどうも｜物事[ものごと]を｜大[おお]げさに｜考[かんが]える｜嫌[きら]いがある。

examples.ja: 最近の報道は、物事の一面だけを強調する嫌いがあるように思う。
examples.en: Recent news coverage seems to have a tendency to emphasize only one side of things.
examples.f: ｜最近[さいきん]の｜報道[ほうどう]は、｜物事[ものごと]の｜一[いち]｜面[めん]だけを｜強調[きょうちょう]する｜嫌[きら]いがあるように｜思[おも]う。

synonyms.note: がち is casual and simply notes a frequent tendency; 嫌いがある is formal and pointedly critical of an ingrained inclination.

title: 切りがない
meaning: there is no end to; endless; no stopping point
summary: 切りがない says that something has no natural stopping point — pursue it and you could go on forever. It often appears as 〜ばきりがない: 数え上げればきりがない (there's no end to listing them). きり here means a cut-off or limit, so 切りがない is literally 'there is no cut-off'. It is used to break off an open-ended enumeration or to note that wants and demands have no ceiling.
pitfalls: Frequently framed as 〜ばきりがない ('if you start ~ing, there's no end to it').
きり here means a limit or stopping point, not the 'only' きり of 一人きり.
Often used to cut a discussion short by admitting the topic could go on endlessly.

examples.ja: 欲を言えばきりがないが、今の暮らしに大きな不満はない。
examples.en: If I started listing wishes there'd be no end to it, but I have no real complaints about my life as it is.
examples.f: ｜欲[よく]を｜言[い]えばきりがないが、｜今[いま]の｜暮[く]らしに｜大[おお]きな｜不満[ふまん]はない。

examples.ja: 細かい問題点を挙げていけばきりがないので、主なものだけ述べる。
examples.en: There's no end to listing minor issues, so I'll mention only the main ones.
examples.f: ｜細[こま]かい｜問題[もんだい]｜点[てん]を｜挙[あ]げていけばきりがないので、｜主[おも]なものだけ｜述[の]べる。

title: 〜極まる・〜極まりない
kana: きわまる・きわまりない
meaning: extremely; utterly; in the highest degree
summary: 〜極まる and 〜極まりない both attach to a な-adjective stem and mean 'extremely, utterly ~', describing a quality pushed to its limit: 失礼極まりない (extremely rude), 危険極まる (utterly dangerous). Curiously, despite the ない, 極まりない means the same as 極まる — both are affirmative in force. The pattern is formal, emphatic, and often voices strong disapproval or strong feeling in written style.
pitfalls: 極まりない and 極まる mean the same thing here ('extremely'); the ない does not make it negative.
Attaches to a な-adjective naming a quality taken to its extreme, not to ordinary verbs.
Formal, emphatic, and usually charged with strong (often negative) feeling.

examples.ja: あのような公の場で騒ぎ立てるとは、失礼極まりない態度だ。
examples.en: To make a scene in a public setting like that is an utterly rude way to behave.
examples.f: あのような｜公[おおやけ]の｜場[ば]で｜騒ぎ立[さわぎた]てるとは、｜失礼[しつれい]｜極[きわ]まりない｜態度[たいど]だ。

examples.ja: 彼らは危険極まる高所での作業を、何の装備もなしに続けていた。
examples.en: They kept up their extremely dangerous work at height without any protective equipment at all.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]らは｜危険[きけん]｜極[きわ]まる｜高所[こうしょ]での｜作業[さぎょう]を、｜何[なに]の｜装備[そうび]もなしに｜続[つづ]けていた。

synonyms.note: の極み attaches to a noun and names 'the very height of ~'; 極まる／極まりない attach to a な-adjective quality.
限りだ conveys the speaker's own feeling at its utmost (嬉しい限りだ); 極まりない more often condemns an external quality.

related.note: の至り expresses an emotion or state reaching its extreme, often in set humble phrases; 極まる rates a described quality as extreme.

title: 〜くらいなら・〜ぐらいなら
kana: くらいなら・ぐらいなら
meaning: rather than (do something that unpleasant); if it comes to ~, I'd sooner
summary: 〜くらいなら weighs the first option as something so unpleasant that the speaker would sooner take another, often drastic, alternative — 'rather than A, I'd rather B'. 途中でやめるくらいなら、最初からやらない = rather than quit halfway, I'd not start at all. It attaches to a dictionary-form verb and frequently pairs with むしろ or 〜ほうがましだ. It is a pointed comparison, not a neutral one.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋くらいなら＋（むしろ）～ほうがましだ／～たい
pitfalls: The くらいなら option is presented as bad or unbearable, and the alternative as the lesser evil — not an even-handed choice.
Often paired with むしろ or 〜ほうがましだ to point to the preferred, sometimes extreme, alternative.
くらい here downgrades the first option rather than estimating a quantity.

examples.ja: 満員電車で通勤するくらいなら、少し遠回りでも自転車で行きたい。
examples.en: Rather than commute on a packed train, I'd sooner go by bicycle even if it means a bit of a detour.
examples.f: ｜満員[まんいん]｜電車[でんしゃ]で｜通勤[つうきん]するくらいなら、｜少[すこ]し｜遠回[とおまわ]りでも｜自転車[じてんしゃ]で｜行[い]きたい。

examples.ja: 人に頭を下げて頼むくらいなら、自分でやったほうがまだましだ。
examples.en: Rather than bow my head and beg someone, I'd be better off just doing it myself.
examples.f: ｜人[ひと]に｜頭[あたま]を｜下[さ]げて｜頼[たの]むくらいなら、｜自分[じぶん]でやったほうがまだましだ。

synonyms.note: むしろ marks the 'rather / sooner' side of the choice and often co-occurs; くらいなら packages the rejected option as an unbearable one.

related.note: より makes a plain comparison ('than'); くらいなら adds that the first option is bad enough to reject outright.

title: 〜くらいのものだ
meaning: about the only ~; ~ is just about the only one
summary: 〜くらいのものだ narrows things down to essentially a single case — 'that's about the only one'. こんなことを言うのは彼くらいのものだ = he's about the only one who'd say such a thing. It attaches to a noun (often after a 〜のは clause), and the くらい softens a flat 'only' into 'more or less the sole case'. The tone is one of resigned or wry observation that scarcely anyone else qualifies.
structure: Verb［plain form］＋のは＋Noun＋くらいのものだ
pitfalls: Singles out essentially the only case that fits — close to だけ but softer, with a nuance of 'that's about all'.
くらい here limits the scope, not approximates a quantity.
Commonly set up by a 〜のは clause naming what almost no one does.

examples.ja: こんな時間まで残って仕事をしているのは、私たちくらいのものだろう。
examples.en: We're probably about the only ones still here working at this hour.
examples.f: こんな｜時間[じかん]まで｜残[のこ]って｜仕事[しごと]をしているのは、｜私[わたし]たちくらいのものだろう。

examples.ja: あの店のことを今でも覚えているのは、地元の古い住民くらいのものだ。
examples.en: Longtime local residents are just about the only ones who still remember that shop.
examples.f: あの｜店[みせ]のことを｜今[いま]でも｜覚[おぼ]えているのは、｜地元[じもと]の｜古[ふる]い｜住民[じゅうみん]くらいのものだ。

synonyms.note: だけ states 'only' flatly; くらいのものだ softens it to 'about the only one', with a resigned or wry undertone.
にすぎない downplays something as 'no more than'; くらいのものだ limits the field to essentially a single case.

title: 〜ぐるみ
meaning: the whole ~; -wide; everyone/everything included
summary: 〜ぐるみ is a suffix meaning 'the whole ~ together, involving everyone in it'. It attaches to a limited set of nouns: 家族ぐるみ (the whole family), 会社ぐるみ (company-wide), 町ぐるみ (the whole town), 地域ぐるみ, and 身ぐるみ (everything one owns). The image is of the named group acting or being involved as a single unit, with no member left out.
pitfalls: Attaches to a limited stock of nouns (家族, 会社, 町, 地域, 身); not freely productive.
Means 'the whole group as a unit', implying everyone in it is involved.
身ぐるみ is idiomatic for 'everything one has (on one)', as in 身ぐるみはがされる.

examples.ja: その不正は、一部の社員ではなく会社ぐるみで行われていた。
examples.en: The wrongdoing was carried out not by a handful of employees but by the entire company.
examples.f: その｜不正[ふせい]は、｜一部[いちぶ]の｜社員[しゃいん]ではなく｜会社[かいしゃ]ぐるみで｜行[おこな]われていた。

examples.ja: 隣の一家とは、もう何年も家族ぐるみの付き合いが続いている。
examples.en: We've kept up a whole-family friendship with the household next door for many years now.
examples.f: ｜隣[となり]の｜一家[いっか]とは、もう｜何[なん]｜年[ねん]も｜家族[かぞく]ぐるみの｜付き合[つきあ]いが｜続[つづ]いている。

title: 〜こそ〜が
meaning: it is true that ~, but; ~ indeed, yet
summary: In the 〜こそ〜が pattern, こそ emphasizes a point that is then conceded, while が (or けれど) introduces the contrasting main claim. The shape is 'A こそ ~, が B' = 'A may indeed be the case, but B'. 規模こそ小さいが = small in scale it may be, but... The real weight of the sentence falls on the clause after が; the こそ part is granted only to be set against it.
pitfalls: こそ marks the conceded point; the true emphasis lands on the clause after が/けれど.
It is a concessive 'A indeed, but B', not a plain listing of two facts.
Written and somewhat emphatic in tone.

examples.ja: 返事こそしなかったが、彼女が納得していないのは表情から明らかだった。
examples.en: She may not have replied, but it was clear from her expression that she wasn't convinced.
examples.f: ｜返事[へんじ]こそしなかったが、｜彼女[かのじょ]が｜納得[なっとく]していないのは｜表情[ひょうじょう]から｜明[あき]らかだった。

examples.ja: 規模こそ小さいが、この工房の職人技は他の追随を許さない。
examples.en: Small in scale it may be, but this workshop's craftsmanship is second to none.
examples.f: ｜規模[きぼ]こそ｜小[ちい]さいが、この｜工房[こうぼう]の｜職人[しょくにん]｜技[わざ]は｜他[た]の｜追随[ついずい]を｜許[ゆる]さない。

related.note: こそ on its own simply emphasizes ('it is precisely ~'); 〜こそ〜が uses that emphasis to set up a concession before a contrast.
こそあれ concedes that A exists then downplays it; 〜こそ〜が concedes A then contrasts it with a weightier main claim.

title: 〜こそあれ
meaning: though there may be ~; there is ~, but
summary: 〜こそあれ concedes that A does exist or is the case, then goes on to a contrasting statement that discounts its importance — 'there may indeed be A, but ~'. 多少の違いこそあれ、本質は同じだ = there may be slight differences, but the essence is the same. It attaches to a noun (a な-adjective takes で before it) and uses the classical あれ. The tone is formal and literary, and the following clause often negates or minimizes.
pitfalls: Concedes that A exists, then the following clause downplays or denies its significance — often 〜こそあれ、〜ない.
Uses the classical あれ (from ある); formal and literary.
Attaches to a noun; a な-adjective needs で before こそあれ.

examples.ja: 表現に多少の違いこそあれ、両者の主張の本質は変わらない。
examples.en: There may be slight differences in wording, but the essence of the two arguments is the same.
examples.f: ｜表現[ひょうげん]に｜多少[たしょう]の｜違[ちが]いこそあれ、｜両者[りょうしゃ]の｜主張[しゅちょう]の｜本質[ほんしつ]は｜変[か]わらない。

examples.ja: 程度の差こそあれ、誰もが何らかの不安を抱えて生きている。
examples.en: To differing degrees, to be sure, everyone lives carrying some kind of anxiety.
examples.f: ｜程度[ていど]の｜差[さ]こそあれ、｜誰[だれ]もが｜何[なん]らかの｜不安[ふあん]を｜抱[かか]えて｜生[い]きている。

synonyms.note: こそすれ builds on a verb ('may well ~, but certainly not ...'); こそあれ builds on a noun ('there may be ~, but ...').
とはいえ concedes a whole statement then qualifies it; こそあれ concedes the existence of a specific thing then downplays it.

related.note: 〜こそ〜が concedes a point then contrasts it with a heavier main claim; こそあれ concedes existence then minimizes its weight.

title: 〜こそすれ
meaning: may well ~, but certainly not ...
summary: 〜こそすれ concedes that one thing does hold — and then flatly denies the alternative the listener might expect. 感謝こそすれ、恨みはない = I may well feel gratitude, but resentment, never. It uses すれ, the classical conditional stem of する, after こそ, and the clause that follows must be a denial. The tone is formal and literary; in speech people would say 〜することはあっても instead.
pitfalls: The second clause must deny something: 感謝こそすれ、恨むことはない — ending on an affirmative statement breaks the pattern.
すれ is the classical 已然形 of する, not the conditional すれば — write こそすれ, not こそすれば.
This is formal, written-style Japanese; it sounds stiff in casual conversation.

examples.ja: あなたには感謝こそすれ、恨む気持ちなど少しもありません。
examples.en: Toward you I feel nothing but gratitude — not the slightest trace of resentment.
examples.f: あなたには｜感謝[かんしゃ]こそすれ、｜恨[うら]む｜気持[きも]ちなど｜少[すこ]しもありません。

examples.ja: この案では状況は悪化こそすれ、改善することはないだろう。
examples.en: Under this plan the situation may well get worse; it will certainly not improve.
examples.f: この｜案[あん]では｜状況[じょうきょう]は｜悪化[あっか]こそすれ、｜改善[かいぜん]することはないだろう。

related.note: こそ simply spotlights one element ('precisely X'); こそすれ builds on it to concede X while denying the alternative.
ばこそ emphasizes a reason ('precisely because'); こそすれ concedes one action and rules out another.

title: 〜如く・〜如き・〜如し
kana: ごとく・ごとき・ごとし
meaning: like; as if; such as (literary)
summary: ごとく is the literary counterpart of ように: 雪のごとく = like snow. It inflects like a classical auxiliary — ごとく modifies a verb or adjective, ごとき modifies a noun, and ごとし ends a sentence. After a noun it takes の (氷のごとく); after a verb it often appears as （かの）ごとく. Attached directly to a person, ごとき belittles that person — 私ごとき is humble, 彼ごとき is dismissive. Today it survives in essays, proverbs, and formal speeches; everyday speech uses ように・ような・ようだ.
pitfalls: Match the form to what follows: ごとく before verbs and adjectives, ごとき before nouns, ごとし only at the end of a sentence.
Person＋ごとき (without の) belittles: 私ごとき is self-deprecating, 彼ごときに負けた is contemptuous — do not use it neutrally about superiors.
This is literary register; in conversation, use ように instead.

examples.ja: 桜の花びらが、雪のごとく舞い散っていた。
examples.en: The cherry blossom petals were fluttering down like snow.
examples.f: ｜桜[さくら]の｜花[はな]びらが、｜雪[ゆき]のごとく｜舞[ま]い｜散[ち]っていた。

examples.ja: 私ごときが社長に意見を申し上げるなど、とんでもないことです。
examples.en: It would be unthinkable for the likes of me to offer an opinion to the president.
examples.f: ｜私[わたし]ごときが｜社長[しゃちょう]に｜意見[いけん]を｜申し上[もうしあ]げるなど、とんでもないことです。

synonyms.note: かのように is the standard modern way to say 'as if'; ごとく says the same thing in literary register.
ように・ような is the neutral everyday equivalent; ごとく・ごとき belongs to written and ceremonial style.

related.note: ことごとく ('without exception') looks similar but is an unrelated word — it comes from 悉く, not from 如く.

title: ことごとく
meaning: entirely; every last one; without exception
summary: ことごとく is a formal adverb meaning that something applies to every single item with no exceptions: 提案がことごとく否決された = every last proposal was voted down. It typically sweeps over a set of things (plans, predictions, buildings) and very often the outcome is unwelcome — everything failed, everything was destroyed. In kanji it is 悉く, but it is normally written in kana. It belongs to written and news-report style; casual speech prefers 全部 or すべて.
pitfalls: It strongly tends to appear with unfavorable outcomes (ことごとく外れる, ことごとく失敗する); for neutral 'all', すべて or 全部 is safer.
Despite the look, it has no connection to 〜ごとく ('like') — ことごとく is one word meaning 'without exception'.

examples.ja: 私の提案は、会議でことごとく否定されてしまった。
examples.en: Every single one of my proposals was shot down at the meeting.
examples.f: ｜私[わたし]の｜提案[ていあん]は、｜会議[かいぎ]でことごとく｜否定[ひてい]されてしまった。

examples.ja: 台風で、海沿いの建物はことごとく被害を受けた。
examples.en: The typhoon damaged every last building along the coast.
examples.f: ｜台風[たいふう]で、｜海沿[うみぞ]いの｜建物[たてもの]はことごとく｜被害[ひがい]を｜受[う]けた。

related.note: 〜ごとく means 'like, as if' and is a different word entirely — don't let the shared kana mislead you.
まるっきり means 'utterly, completely' about degree; ことごとく counts through every member of a set.

title: 〜ことこの上ない・この上ない
kana: ことこのうえない・このうえない
romaji: koto kono ue nai / kono ue nai
meaning: unsurpassed; in the extreme; couldn't be more ~
summary: この上ない literally says 'there is nothing above this' — the degree is the highest possible. After an adjective plus こと it grades that quality to the extreme: 不用心なことこの上ない = careless in the extreme. On its own it modifies a noun (この上ない喜び = the greatest possible joy), and the adverbial この上なく intensifies a predicate (この上なく幸せだ). The tone is formal-written, and unlike 極まりない it works comfortably with positive qualities as well as negative ones.
pitfalls: It grades qualities, so it attaches to adjectives (via こと) or nouns — not directly to verbs.
極まりない leans heavily toward negative qualities; この上ない is equally natural with positive ones (この上ない幸せ).

examples.ja: 鍵をかけずに出かけるとは、不用心なことこの上ない。
examples.en: Going out without locking the door is careless in the extreme.
examples.f: ｜鍵[かぎ]をかけずに｜出[で]かけるとは、｜不用心[ぶようじん]なことこの｜上[うえ]ない。

examples.ja: 長年の夢がかなって、今はこの上なく幸せだ。
examples.en: My long-held dream has come true, and I couldn't be happier.
examples.f: ｜長年の夢[ながねんのゆめ]がかなって、｜今[いま]はこの｜上[うえ]なく｜幸[しあわ]せだ。

synonyms.note: 極まりない also marks an extreme degree but attaches to な-adjective stems and skews negative; この上ない welcomes positive qualities.
の極み attaches to nouns (感激の極み); この上ない grades adjectives and modifies nouns directly.

related.note: の至り expresses an extreme of emotion in fixed formal phrases (光栄の至り); この上ない is a more general superlative.

title: 〜ことだし
meaning: since; seeing as (one reason among others)
summary: 〜ことだし offers one reason — while hinting there are others — as gentle grounds for a suggestion or decision: 雨も上がったことだし、出かけよう = the rain's stopped (among other things), so let's head out. The こと wraps the reason up as an established circumstance, and し adds the 'and other reasons too' flavor. It is conversational but slightly considered in tone, and the sentence usually ends with a proposal, intention, or request rather than a plain statement.
pitfalls: It implies the stated reason is not the only one — for a single, direct cause, use から or ので.
The main clause is typically a suggestion, decision, or request (〜しよう, 〜たらどう), not a neutral report.

examples.ja: 雨も上がったことだし、そろそろ出かけようか。
examples.en: The rain has stopped, so shall we head out soon?
examples.f: ｜雨[あめ]も｜上[あ]がったことだし、そろそろ｜出[で]かけようか。

examples.ja: 仕事も一段落したことだし、今夜は早めに帰るつもりだ。
examples.en: Work has settled down for now, so I plan to head home early tonight.
examples.f: ｜仕事[しごと]も｜一段落[いちだんらく]したことだし、｜今夜[こんや]は｜早[はや]めに｜帰[かえ]るつもりだ。

synonyms.note: Plain し also lists reasons; ことだし is softer and frames the reason as a settled circumstance leading to a proposal.

related.note: こともあって reports a partial cause of a fact; ことだし gives a reason for what the speaker proposes to do.
ことだから reasons from someone's known character; ことだし cites a circumstance as one reason among several.

title: 〜こととて
meaning: because; as (formal, often apologetic)
summary: 〜こととて presents a circumstance as the reason for something — most often as an excuse when apologizing or asking for indulgence: 慣れぬこととて = as (I am) unaccustomed to it. It is markedly old-fashioned and formal, at home in business letters, formal apologies, and period fiction. It follows a plain-form clause or Noun＋の, and famously combines with the classical negative ぬ (知らぬこととて, 慣れぬこととて).
pitfalls: It is archaic-formal; using it in casual conversation sounds theatrical. In speech, ものですから or ので fills the same role.
With negatives it characteristically takes the classical ぬ (慣れぬこととて); the plain ない (慣れないこととて) is also used but sounds less set.
The main clause is usually an apology or a request for understanding, not a neutral consequence.

examples.ja: 何分新人のこととて、行き届かない点はどうかお許しください。
examples.en: As he is still new to the job, please forgive any points where he falls short.
examples.f: ｜何分[なにぶん]｜新人[しんじん]のこととて、｜行き届[いきとど]かない｜点[てん]はどうかお｜許[ゆる]しください。

examples.ja: 慣れぬこととて、ご迷惑をおかけしましたことを深くお詫び申し上げます。
examples.en: Being unaccustomed to the task, I sincerely apologize for the trouble I caused.
examples.f: ｜慣[な]れぬこととて、ご｜迷惑[めいわく]をおかけしましたことを｜深[ふか]くお｜詫[わ]び｜申し上[もうしあ]げます。

synonyms.note: もので also gives an excuse-flavored reason, but is ordinary polite speech; こととて is archaic and ceremonious.

related.note: ことだし casually offers one reason for a proposal; こととて formally excuses a shortcoming.

title: 〜ことなしに
meaning: without doing; unless (one does)
summary: 〜ことなしに attaches to a dictionary-form verb and means the main action happens without that verb ever occurring: 誰にも相談することなしに決めた = decided without consulting anyone. In its second, more argumentative use, the main clause is negative or potential-negative and the whole sentence reads 'unless you do X, Y is impossible' — 努力することなしに成功はあり得ない. Both uses are formal and written in flavor; everyday speech would use 〜ないで or 〜ずに.
pitfalls: Attach it to the dictionary form via こと: 相談することなしに, not 相談したことなしに.
It is distinctly formal; for everyday 'without doing', 〜ないで or 〜ずに is the natural choice.
In the 'unless' use, the main clause must be negative in sense: 犠牲を払うことなしに自由は得られない.

examples.ja: 彼は誰にも相談することなしに、退職を決めてしまった。
examples.en: He decided to quit his job without consulting anyone at all.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜誰[だれ]にも｜相談[そうだん]することなしに、｜退職[たいしょく]を｜決[き]めてしまった。

examples.ja: 地道に努力することなしに、成功はあり得ない。
examples.en: Success is impossible without steady, patient effort.
examples.f: ｜地道[じみち]に｜努力[どりょく]することなしに、｜成功[せいこう]はあり｜得[え]ない。

synonyms.note: なしに attaches directly to nouns (連絡なしに); ことなしに packages a verb phrase into the same construction.
ないで is the neutral spoken 'without doing'; ことなしに is its stiff written counterpart.

related.note: なくしては ('without ~, no ...') also builds an 'impossible without' argument, but from a noun.

title: 〜ことのないように
meaning: so as never to; to make sure ~ never happens
summary: 〜ことのないように wraps a feared event in ことのない ('such that it never happens') and aims an action at preventing it: 二度と起こることのないように対策する = take measures so it never happens again. It is the formal, emphatic version of plain ないように, common in official apologies, announcements, and warnings, and frequently reinforced with 二度と ('never again'). The main clause states the precaution or request.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ことのないように
pitfalls: It is more formal and emphatic than plain 〜ないように; in casual speech, 忘れないようにね is enough.
The verb before ことのない is in the dictionary form: 起こることのないように, not 起こったことのないように.

examples.ja: このような事故が二度と起こることのないように、対策を徹底いたします。
examples.en: We will take thorough measures to ensure that an accident like this never happens again.
examples.f: このような｜事故[じこ]が｜二度[にど]と｜起[お]こることのないように、｜対策[たいさく]を｜徹底[てってい]いたします。

examples.ja: お帰りの際は、貴重品をお忘れになることのないようにご注意ください。
examples.en: When leaving, please take care not to leave any valuables behind.
examples.f: お｜帰[かえ]りの｜際[さい]は、｜貴重[きちょう]｜品[ひん]をお｜忘[わす]れになることのないようにご｜注意[ちゅうい]ください。

synonyms.note: Plain ように expresses the same purpose neutrally; ことのないように adds formal weight and the sense of 'never'.

related.note: べからず bluntly prohibits on signs; ことのないように politely urges prevention.

title: 〜こともあって
meaning: partly because; with ~ also being a factor
summary: 〜こともあって cites one contributing reason while openly signaling it is not the whole story: 駅から近いこともあって、いつも混んでいる = partly because it's near the station, it's always crowded. The も does the work — 'this factor, among others, exists'. It attaches to plain-form clauses (nouns take という or である) and suits neutral explanation in both speech and writing; the main clause states the resulting situation.
structure: な-adjective＋な／である＋こともあって
Noun＋という／である＋こともあって
pitfalls: It presents a partial cause — if the reason is the sole, direct cause, use ので or ため instead.
The main clause reports an observed result, not a proposal; for reason-plus-suggestion, use ことだし.

examples.ja: 駅から近いこともあって、この店はいつも混んでいる。
examples.en: Partly because it is close to the station, this shop is always crowded.
examples.f: ｜駅[えき]から｜近[ちか]いこともあって、この｜店[みせ]はいつも｜混[こ]んでいる。

examples.ja: 連休だったこともあって、遊園地は家族連れでにぎわっていた。
examples.en: Partly because it was a holiday weekend, the amusement park was bustling with families.
examples.f: ｜連休[れんきゅう]だったこともあって、｜遊園[ゆうえん]｜地[ち]は｜家族[かぞく]｜連[づ]れでにぎわっていた。

related.note: せいか guesses at an uncertain (often negative) cause; こともあって confidently names one factor among several.
ことだし gives a reason for what the speaker will do; こともあって explains why a situation is the way it is.

title: さぞ
meaning: surely; how ~ it must be (empathetic conjecture)
summary: さぞ introduces an empathetic guess about someone else's feelings or situation, imagining how intense it must be: さぞうれしかったことでしょう = how happy you must have been. It obligatorily pairs with a conjecture ending — だろう, でしょう, ことだろう — because the speaker is imagining, not asserting. さぞかし is an emphatic variant. The feeling guessed at is usually someone else's, and the tone is warm or sympathetic rather than analytical.
structure: さぞ（かし）＋Adjective／Verb＋だろう／でしょう／ことだろう
pitfalls: It must end in conjecture: さぞお疲れでしょう, not ×さぞお疲れです.
It imagines someone else's inner state; for your own feelings, just state them — ×私はさぞうれしい.
さぞかし is simply an emphatic さぞ; the pairing rule is the same.

examples.ja: 息子さんが第一志望に合格して、さぞうれしかったことでしょう。
examples.en: You must have been overjoyed that your son got into his first-choice school.
examples.f: ｜息子[むすこ]さんが｜第[だい]｜一[いち]｜志望[しぼう]に｜合格[ごうかく]して、さぞうれしかったことでしょう。

examples.ja: 言葉も通じない土地での暮らしは、さぞ心細いだろう。
examples.en: Living in a place where you can't even speak the language must be terribly lonely.
examples.f: ｜言葉[ことば]も｜通[つう]じない｜土地[とち]での｜暮[く]らしは、さぞ｜心細[こころぼそ]いだろう。

related.note: だろう is the plain conjecture さぞ must lean on; さぞ adds 'I can just imagine how much'.
に違いない draws a confident conclusion from evidence; さぞ〜だろう empathetically imagines degree.

title: さも
meaning: as if; for all the world like; utterly (in appearance)
summary: さも intensifies how convincingly something looks or sounds a certain way, pairing with appearance expressions like 〜そうに and 〜かのように: さも気持ちよさそうに = looking utterly content; さも見てきたかのように = for all the world as if he'd seen it himself. With かのように it often implies the appearance is put on — the person acts as if something were true when it isn't. It is somewhat literary but heard in speech too.
pitfalls: さも needs a partner expression of appearance (そうに, かのように, と言わんばかりに); it cannot stand alone before a plain verb.
With かのように it often hints the appearance is false — さも知っているかのように話す implies he doesn't actually know.

examples.ja: 猫は、さも気持ちよさそうに日なたで眠っている。
examples.en: The cat is sleeping in a sunny spot, looking utterly content.
examples.f: ｜猫[ねこ]は、さも｜気持[きも]ちよさそうに｜日[ひ]なたで｜眠[ねむ]っている。

examples.ja: 彼はさも自分が発見したかのように、その話を得意げに語った。
examples.en: He recounted the story proudly, as if he himself had discovered it.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]はさも｜自分[じぶん]が｜発見[はっけん]したかのように、その｜話[はなし]を｜得意[とくい]げに｜語[かた]った。

synonyms.note: まるで states a plain resemblance ('just like'); さも stresses how convincing — and often how feigned — the appearance is.

related.note: かのように supplies the 'as if' clause that さも typically intensifies.

title: さもないと
meaning: otherwise; or else
summary: さもないと follows a command, warning, or statement of what must be done, and spells out the bad consequence of not complying: 早くしなさい。さもないと遅れるよ = hurry up — otherwise you'll be late. Literally 'if it is not so', it always points to an undesirable outcome, which makes it a natural partner for warnings. さもなければ and the stiffer さもなくば mean the same; in casual speech, そうしないと is more common.
pitfalls: The clause after さもないと must be an undesirable outcome — it warns, it doesn't promise rewards.
It follows commands or statements of necessity; after a mere description, use そうでないと instead.
さもなければ・さもなくば are more formal equivalents; さもないと itself already leans written or emphatic.

examples.ja: 早めに申し込んだほうがいい。さもないと、席がなくなってしまうよ。
examples.en: You should apply early. Otherwise, there won't be any seats left.
examples.f: ｜早[はや]めに｜申し込[もうしこ]んだほうがいい。さもないと、｜席[せき]がなくなってしまうよ。

examples.ja: 今すぐ出発しなさい。さもないと、飛行機に乗り遅れますよ。
examples.en: Leave right now. Otherwise you'll miss your plane.
examples.f: ｜今[いま]すぐ｜出発[しゅっぱつ]しなさい。さもないと、｜飛行機[ひこうき]に｜乗り遅[のりおく]れますよ。

related.note: ないと puts the same warning inside one sentence (急がないと遅れる); さもないと starts a new sentence with 'otherwise'.

title: 〜次第です
meaning: that is how/why it came about (formal explanation)
summary: 〜次第です closes a formal explanation of the circumstances that led to one's action: ご連絡を差し上げた次第です = and that is why I am contacting you. It follows a plain-form clause — typically containing humble language — and is a staple of business e-mail and formal speech, where it presents your action as the natural outcome of the events just described. It sounds courteous and slightly self-effacing.
pitfalls: Keep it apart from its relatives: verb-stem + 次第 means 'as soon as' (着き次第) and Noun + 次第だ means 'depends on' (君次第だ) — this pattern only explains how things came about.
It explains your own actions in formal contexts; using it about other people's actions sounds odd.
It belongs to business and ceremonial register — in ordinary speech, 〜というわけです covers the same ground.

examples.ja: 担当者が急に退職いたしましたので、私からご連絡を差し上げた次第です。
examples.en: The person in charge left the company suddenly, which is why I am the one contacting you.
examples.f: ｜担当[たんとう]｜者[しゃ]が｜急[きゅう]に｜退職[たいしょく]いたしましたので、｜私[わたし]からご｜連絡[れんらく]を｜差し上[さしあ]げた｜次第[しだい]です。

examples.ja: 以上のような経緯で、本日の会議を延期させていただいた次第です。
examples.en: Such were the circumstances that led us to postpone today's meeting.
examples.f: ｜以上[いじょう]のような｜経緯[けいい]で、｜本日[ほんじつ]の｜会議[かいぎ]を｜延期[えんき]させていただいた｜次第[しだい]です。

related.note: Verb-stem + 次第 means 'as soon as ~' (分かり次第連絡します) — a different pattern sharing the word.
Noun + 次第で means 'depending on ~'; 次第です after a clause explains how a situation came about.

title: 〜始末だ
meaning: ended up (in a deplorable state); to top it all off
summary: 〜始末だ caps off a chain of bad developments with the final, worst stage: 遅刻を繰り返し、ついには無断欠勤までする始末だ = he kept coming late, and to top it all off he started skipping work without notice. The speaker is exasperated or critical; the pattern almost demands set-up phrases like さんざん〜したあげく or ついには. It follows the dictionary form, and この始末だ ('look how it ended up') is a common set phrase.
pitfalls: The outcome must be deplorable and the speaker critical — it cannot report a happy ending: ×合格する始末だ.
It marks the last stage of a downhill sequence, so it usually needs lead-up like ついには or 〜たあげく.
Attach it to the dictionary form: 泣き出す始末だ, not 泣き出した始末だ.

examples.ja: 彼は遅刻を繰り返し、ついには無断欠勤までする始末だ。
examples.en: He kept showing up late, and to top it all off he even started skipping work without notice.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜遅刻[ちこく]を｜繰り返[くりかえ]し、ついには｜無断[むだん]｜欠勤[けっきん]までする｜始末[しまつ]だ。

examples.ja: 兄はさんざん散財したあげく、友人にまでお金を借りる始末だった。
examples.en: After spending recklessly, my brother ended up borrowing money even from his friends.
examples.f: ｜兄[あに]はさんざん｜散財[さんざい]したあげく、｜友人[ゆうじん]にまでお｜金[かね]を｜借[か]りる｜始末[しまつ]だった。

synonyms.note: あげく marks 'after a long, trying process'; 始末だ goes further and condemns the final state it led to.

related.note: 末に is neutral about the outcome of a long process; 始末だ is reserved for outcomes the speaker deplores.
羽目になる laments the unlucky situation one falls into; 始末だ criticizes conduct that spiraled to a sorry end.

title: 〜じみた
meaning: looking like; smacking of (something undesirable)
summary: 〜じみた, from the verb 染みる ('to soak into'), says something has taken on the unwelcome look or air of a noun: 子供じみた態度 = a childish attitude, 芝居じみた言い訳 = a theatrical excuse. The judgment is always negative — the thing resembles something it shouldn't. It attaches to a limited set of nouns (子供, 芝居, 狂気, 説教, 年寄り...), modifies nouns as じみた, and predicates as じみている.
pitfalls: The nuance is always critical: 子供じみた condemns immaturity, while 子供らしい can praise childlike charm.
It works only with a conventional set of nouns (子供, 芝居, 狂気, 説教...); it is not freely productive like っぽい.
As a predicate use じみている: 彼の話は説教じみている, not 説教じみたです.

examples.ja: いい年をして、そんな子供じみたまねはやめなさい。
examples.en: You're too old for that kind of childish behavior — stop it.
examples.f: いい｜年[とし]をして、そんな｜子供[こども]じみたまねはやめなさい。

examples.ja: 彼の言い訳はどこか芝居じみていて、信用できなかった。
examples.en: His excuse felt somehow theatrical, and I couldn't bring myself to trust it.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜言い訳[いいわけ]はどこか｜芝居[しばい]じみていて、｜信用[しんよう]できなかった。

synonyms.note: っぽい is colloquial, freely productive, and can be neutral; じみた is critical and limited to set nouns.
めく says something 'has an air of' fairly neutrally (春めく); じみた always disapproves of the resemblance.

related.note: らしい affirms something shows its proper, expected character; じみた accuses it of an improper resemblance.

title: 〜ずくめ
meaning: nothing but; entirely; full of
summary: Noun＋ずくめ means the whole of something consists of that noun through and through: いいことずくめ = nothing but good things, 黒ずくめ = (dressed) all in black, 規則ずくめ = rules upon rules. It attaches to a limited group of nouns — colors, ごちそう, いいこと, 規則, 異例 — and, unlike だらけ, it happily describes good things as well as oppressive ones. It often characterizes a period, an outfit, or an organization.
pitfalls: Only a conventional set of nouns takes ずくめ (黒, いいこと, ごちそう, 規則, 異例...); you cannot coin freely with it.
It is not inherently negative — いいことずくめ is common; for 'covered in something undesirable', だらけ is the right choice.
Standard orthography is ずくめ, not づくめ.

examples.ja: 今年は結婚に昇進にと、いいことずくめの一年だった。
examples.en: With a wedding and a promotion, this was a year full of nothing but good things.
examples.f: ｜今年[ことし]は｜結婚[けっこん]に｜昇進[しょうしん]にと、いいことずくめの｜一[いち]｜年[ねん]だった。

examples.ja: 黒ずくめの服装の男が、店の前にじっと立っていた。
examples.en: A man dressed entirely in black was standing motionless in front of the shop.
examples.f: ｜黒[くろ]ずくめの｜服装[ふくそう]の｜男[おとこ]が、｜店[みせ]の｜前[まえ]にじっと｜立[た]っていた。

synonyms.note: だらけ means 'full of / covered in' something undesirable (泥だらけ, 間違いだらけ); ずくめ can be entirely positive.
まみれ is physical smearing over a surface (汗まみれ); ずくめ says the whole content or makeup is that thing.

title: 〜ずじまい
meaning: ended up never doing (and the chance is gone)
summary: 〜ずじまい combines the negative ず with 仕舞い ('the end') to say a period closed with the action never done — and the speaker regrets it: 結局行かずじまいだった = in the end I never did go. The chance is understood to be lost now. It follows the ない-stem (する becomes せずじまい), almost always appears in the past (〜ずじまいだった), and pairs naturally with 結局 or とうとう.
structure: Verb［ない stem］＋ずじまい（だった）
pitfalls: する becomes せずじまい — ×しずじまい is wrong.
It implies the opportunity has closed and carries regret; for a neutral 'didn't do', plain しなかった is enough.
It normally reports a finished period, so the past 〜ずじまいだった is the usual form.

examples.ja: 京都に三年も住んでいたのに、結局金閣寺には行かずじまいだった。
examples.en: Even though I lived in Kyoto for three whole years, I ended up never visiting Kinkaku-ji.
examples.f: ｜京都[きょうと]に｜三[さん]｜年[ねん]も｜住[す]んでいたのに、｜結局[けっきょく]｜金閣寺[きんかくじ]には｜行[い]かずじまいだった。

examples.ja: 言おう言おうと思いながら、本当の気持ちは伝えられずじまいだった。
examples.en: I kept meaning to say it, but in the end I never managed to convey my true feelings.
examples.f: ｜言[い]おう｜言[い]おうと｜思[おも]いながら、｜本当[ほんとう]の｜気持[きも]ちは｜伝[つた]えられずじまいだった。

related.note: 〜そこなう marks missing a particular chance to do something; ずじまい looks back on a whole period that ended without it.
ずとも is a concessive 'even without doing'; ずじまい reports that the doing never happened, with regret.

title: 〜ずとも
meaning: even without doing; even if not
summary: 〜ずとも is a literary concessive: even without doing the verb, the main clause still holds. 言わずとも分かる = you needn't say it — I understand anyway. It is the classical equivalent of 〜なくても, built from the negative ず plus concessive とも, and する becomes せずとも. Today it appears in written style, formal speech, and set turns of phrase, lending a dignified or aphoristic ring.
pitfalls: It is literary register — in conversation, 〜なくても is the natural equivalent.
する becomes せずとも: 説明せずとも, not ×しずとも.
It attaches to verbs; for nouns and adjectives, use でなくとも or くとも patterns instead.

examples.ja: そこまで説明せずとも、この図を見れば誰でも理解できます。
examples.en: Even without explaining in that much detail, anyone can understand just by looking at this diagram.
examples.f: そこまで｜説明[せつめい]せずとも、この｜図[ず]を｜見[み]れば｜誰[だれ]でも｜理解[りかい]できます。

examples.ja: 実物を見ずとも、写真だけでその美しさは十分に伝わってくる。
examples.en: Even without seeing the real thing, the photographs alone fully convey its beauty.
examples.f: ｜実物[じつぶつ]を｜見[み]ずとも、｜写真[しゃしん]だけでその｜美[うつく]しさは｜十分[じゅうぶん]に｜伝[つた]わってくる。

synonyms.note: 〜なくても is the everyday equivalent; ずとも says the same in classical, written style.

related.note: までもない judges an action unnecessary ('no need to'); ずとも concedes its absence and moves on.
ことなしに states that something happens without the action; ずとも concedes 'even if it doesn't happen'.

title: 〜ずにはおかない・〜ないではおかない
kana: ずにはおかない・ないではおかない
romaji: zu niwa okanai / nai dewa okanai
meaning: will inevitably cause; will not rest until
summary: 〜ずにはおかない declares that a force will not let things end without the verb happening. With causative or emotive verbs, the subject is often a thing whose power inevitably affects people: 聴く人を感動させずにはおかない = it cannot fail to move listeners. With a personal subject it voices fierce determination: 謝らせずにはおかない = I won't rest until I make him apologize. It is emphatic, formal, and written in flavor; する becomes せずにはおかない.
structure: Verb［ない stem］＋ずにはおかない
Verb［ない form］＋ではおかない
pitfalls: Don't confuse it with ずにはいられない, which is the speaker's own uncontrollable urge; ずにはおかない is an external force or resolve that will inevitably bring the action about.
In the 'inevitable effect' use the verb is typically causative (感動させる, 考えさせる) and the subject is often a work, event, or statement.
する becomes せずにはおかない.

examples.ja: 彼女の歌声は、聴く人を感動させずにはおかない。
examples.en: Her singing voice never fails to move those who hear it.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]の｜歌声[うたごえ]は、｜聴[き]く｜人[ひと]を｜感動[かんどう]させずにはおかない。

examples.ja: 今回の不正は、世間の厳しい批判を招かずにはおかないだろう。
examples.en: This misconduct is bound to draw harsh public criticism.
examples.f: ｜今回[こんかい]の｜不正[ふせい]は、｜世間[せけん]の｜厳[きび]しい｜批判[ひはん]を｜招[まね]かずにはおかないだろう。

related.note: ずにはいられない is an internal urge you cannot suppress; ずにはおかない is an outcome the force of things will not fail to produce.
ずには済まない says circumstances oblige you to act; ずにはおかない says the action will inevitably be brought about.

title: 〜ずには済まない・〜ないでは済まない
kana: ずにはすまない・ないではすまない
romaji: zu niwa sumanai / nai dewa sumanai
meaning: cannot get away without doing; will have to
summary: 〜ずには済まない says the matter cannot be settled unless the action is taken — social or moral circumstances leave no way out: 謝らずには済まない = an apology is unavoidable. 済む means 'to be settled', so the pattern literally reads 'it won't be settled without doing'. Typical contexts are apologies, compensation, and explanations that society demands. It follows the ない-stem (する → せずには済まない) and is formal in tone.
structure: Verb［ない stem］＋ずには済まない
Verb［ない form］＋では済まない
pitfalls: The pressure is external — social or moral obligation; for an inner emotional urge, use ずにはいられない.
Its counterpart ずに済む means the opposite: you got by without having to do it. Keep the two apart.
する becomes せずには済まない.

examples.ja: 借りた本を汚してしまった以上、謝らずには済まないだろう。
examples.en: Now that I've gotten the borrowed book dirty, I can hardly get away without apologizing.
examples.f: ｜借[か]りた｜本[ほん]を｜汚[よご]してしまった｜以上[いじょう]、｜謝[あやま]らずには｜済[す]まないだろう。

examples.ja: これほどの損害を出したのだから、会社として補償せずには済まない。
examples.en: Given the scale of the damage, the company has no choice but to pay compensation.
examples.f: これほどの｜損害[そんがい]を｜出[だ]したのだから、｜会社[かいしゃ]として｜補償[ほしょう]せずには｜済[す]まない。

antonyms.note: ずに済む means you managed to get by without doing it — the mirror image of ずには済まない.

related.note: ずにはおかない is an inevitable effect or fierce resolve; ずには済まない is an obligation circumstances impose.
ずにはいられない is an emotion you cannot hold back; ずには済まない is a duty you cannot dodge.

title: 〜術がない
meaning: there is no way/means to; nothing one can do to
summary: 術 (read すべ, not じゅつ) is a literary noun meaning 'means' or 'method'. 〜術がない attaches to a dictionary-form verb and says there is simply no way to carry out that action — 真相を知る術がない = there is no way to learn the truth, なす術がない = there is nothing one can do. 術もない is a slightly stronger variant. The expression is formal and written, conveying helplessness in the face of a situation.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋術（すべ）がない／術もない
pitfalls: 術 here is read すべ, not じゅつ; the whole phrase is formal and largely confined to written or serious speech.
It states that no means exists at all, not merely that something is difficult.

examples.ja: 当時は連絡の手段がなく、彼の安否を確かめるすべがなかった。
examples.en: Back then there was no means of communication, and I had no way of confirming whether he was safe.
examples.f: ｜当時[とうじ]は｜連絡[れんらく]の｜手段[しゅだん]がなく、｜彼[かれ]の｜安否[あんぴ]を｜確[たし]かめるすべがなかった。

examples.ja: 証拠が何一つ残っておらず、真相を知るすべもない。
examples.en: With not a shred of evidence left, there is no way even to get at the truth.
examples.f: ｜証拠[しょうこ]が｜何一[なにひと]つ｜残[のこ]っておらず、｜真相[しんそう]を｜知[し]るすべもない。

synonyms.note: ようがない also means 'no way to ~', but is far more common and everyday; 術がない is literary and formal.
べくもない means 'cannot possibly ~'; 術がない specifically says no method or means exists.

title: 〜すら・〜ですら
meaning: even; even so much as (emphatic)
summary: すら singles out an extreme example to imply that if even this holds, the rest goes without saying — 専門家ですら分からない = even experts don't understand (so of course others don't). It attaches to a noun (ですら adds a copula-like emphasis) and very often pairs with a negative predicate. It is the more formal, literary counterpart of さえ.
pitfalls: すら is more formal and literary than さえ; in casual speech さえ is the natural choice.
It typically presents an extreme case and is very often followed by a negative.

examples.ja: 忙しすぎて、昼食をとる時間すらない。
examples.en: I'm so busy I don't even have time to eat lunch.
examples.f: ｜忙[いそが]しすぎて、｜昼食[ちゅうしょく]をとる｜時間[じかん]すらない。

examples.ja: その理論は、専門家ですら完全には説明できないという。
