examples.en: They say that even specialists cannot fully explain that theory.
examples.f: その｜理論[りろん]は、｜専門[せんもん]｜家[か]ですら｜完全[かんぜん]には｜説明[せつめい]できないという。

synonyms.note: さえ carries the same 'even' emphasis but is more neutral and everyday; すら is more literary.
だに also means 'even', but is archaic and limited to set phrases; すら is freer to use.

title: 〜ぞ・〜ぜ
meaning: emphatic masculine sentence-final particles
summary: ぞ and ぜ are rough, masculine sentence-final particles that add force to an assertion. ぞ can be aimed at oneself as resolve or at others as a warning (負けないぞ = I won't lose; 危ないぞ = watch out). ぜ is directed at a listener to press a point or urge agreement (もう行くぜ = come on, let's go). Both belong to casual, informal speech and sound blunt or tough.
pitfalls: Both are informal and masculine-sounding; they are out of place in polite or formal speech.
ぞ can be muttered to oneself as resolve, whereas ぜ is always aimed at a listener.

examples.ja: この試合だけは、絶対に負けないぞ。
examples.en: This one match — I am absolutely not going to lose it.
examples.f: この｜試合[しあい]だけは、｜絶対[ぜったい]に｜負[ま]けないぞ。

examples.ja: そろそろ出発するぜ。準備はいいか。
examples.en: We're heading out soon. You ready?
examples.f: そろそろ｜出発[しゅっぱつ]するぜ。｜準備[じゅんび]はいいか。

title: 〜損なう・〜損ねる・〜損じる
kana: そこなう・そこねる・そんじる
meaning: to fail to do; to miss doing; to do (something) wrong
summary: Attached to a verb stem, 損なう / 損ねる / 損じる means you failed to complete an action or missed the chance — 乗り損なう = miss (fail to catch) the train, 言い損なう = fail to say. It can also mean doing something incorrectly (書き損じる = miswrite). The three endings are largely interchangeable, though 損じる leans toward 'do wrong'. Note that 損なう / 損ねる can separately mean 'to damage or harm' (健康を損なう, 機嫌を損ねる).
pitfalls: It attaches to the verb stem: 乗り損なう, not 乗る損なう.
On its own, 損なう／損ねる can also mean 'to damage / hurt', as in 気分を損ねる; here the suffix use means 'fail to / miss doing'.

examples.ja: 大事な場面で、シャッターを押し損なってしまった。
examples.en: I failed to press the shutter at the crucial moment.
examples.f: ｜大事[だいじ]な｜場面[ばめん]で、シャッターを｜押[お]し｜損[そこ]なってしまった。

examples.ja: 宛名を書き損じたので、封筒を一枚無駄にした。
examples.en: I wrote the address wrong, so I wasted an envelope.
examples.f: ｜宛名[あてな]を｜書き損[かきそん]じたので、｜封筒[ふうとう]を｜一[いち]｜枚[まい]｜無駄[むだ]にした。

synonyms.note: そびれる also means 'miss the chance to', but only for a missed opportunity; 損なう also covers doing something wrong.

related.note: かける means an action was begun but left unfinished; 損なう means it failed or misfired.

title: 〜そばから
meaning: as soon as (and it is immediately undone again); no sooner than
summary: 〜そばから describes a repeated frustration: no sooner do you do X than the result is immediately undone, over and over. 片付けるそばから散らかす = the moment I tidy up, it gets messy again. It attaches to the dictionary or た-form and, unlike a one-time 'as soon as', implies a habitual cycle where effort is constantly negated.
pitfalls: It implies a repeated, habitual cycle, not a single one-off event.
The nuance is usually frustration that one's effort is undone again and again.

examples.ja: 新しい単語は、覚えるそばから忘れてしまう。
examples.en: No sooner do I memorize new words than I forget them again.
examples.f: ｜新[あたら]しい｜単語[たんご]は、｜覚[おぼ]えるそばから｜忘[わす]れてしまう。

examples.ja: 子どもが片付けるそばから、また部屋を散らかす。
examples.en: The moment I tidy up, the kids mess the room again.
examples.f: ｜子[こ]どもが｜片付[かたづ]けるそばから、また｜部屋[へや]を｜散[ち]らかす。

synonyms.note: が早いか marks a single 'the instant one did X, Y happened'; そばから stresses a repeated, recurring pattern.
たとたん marks one sudden moment; そばから implies the undoing happens again and again.

title: 〜そびれる
meaning: to miss the chance to; to fail to do (though one meant to)
summary: Attached to a verb stem, 〜そびれる means you intended to do something but the timing slipped away, so it never got done — 言いそびれる = miss one's chance to say, 食べそびれる = miss out on eating. The nuance is regret over a lost opportunity rather than being unable in principle.
pitfalls: It attaches to the verb stem: 言いそびれる, not 言うそびれる.
The nuance is that you meant to but the chance slipped by, not that you were incapable.

examples.ja: タイミングを逃して、お礼を言いそびれてしまった。
examples.en: I missed the moment and never got the chance to thank them.
examples.f: タイミングを｜逃[のが]して、お｜礼[れい]を｜言[い]いそびれてしまった。

examples.ja: 会議が長引いて、昼食を食べそびれた。
examples.en: The meeting dragged on and I missed my chance to have lunch.
examples.f: ｜会議[かいぎ]が｜長引[ながび]いて、｜昼食[ちゅうしょく]を｜食[た]べそびれた。

synonyms.note: 損なう also means 'fail to / miss doing', but additionally covers doing something incorrectly; そびれる is only about a missed chance.

title: 〜たことにする・〜たことになる
kana: たことにする・たことになる
romaji: ta koto ni suru / ta koto ni naru
meaning: to pretend/treat as if ~ happened; to be regarded as if ~ happened
summary: 〜たことにする means someone decides to treat something as if it happened (or, with なかった, as if it didn't), often contrary to fact — 聞かなかったことにする = pretend I didn't hear it. 〜たことになる is the passive counterpart: it ends up officially or effectively counting as having happened — サインすれば受け取ったことになる = signing counts as having received it. Both build on the た-form.
pitfalls: ことにする = someone chooses to treat it that way (often against the facts); ことになる = it ends up counting that way as a result.
Distinct from plain ことにする ('decide to do'), which follows the dictionary form.

examples.ja: さっきの話は、聞かなかったことにするよ。
examples.en: I'll pretend I never heard what you just said.
examples.f: さっきの｜話[はなし]は、｜聞[き]かなかったことにするよ。

examples.ja: この書類にサインすれば、代金を受け取ったことになる。
examples.en: Once you sign this document, it counts as having received the payment.
examples.f: この｜書類[しょるい]にサインすれば、｜代金[だいきん]を｜受け取[うけと]ったことになる。

synonyms.note: ふりをする is to put on an act in the moment; たことにする sets up a fact to be treated as settled afterward.

title: ただ〜のみだ
meaning: nothing but; merely; all that remains is
summary: ただ〜のみだ frames something as 'nothing but ~' or 'all that is left is ~'. のみ is the literary equivalent of だけ, and ただ reinforces it with the sense of 'merely / simply'. あとはただ待つのみだ = all that remains now is to wait. It attaches to a dictionary-form verb or a noun and belongs to formal, written-style Japanese.
pitfalls: のみ is formal and written; in ordinary conversation だけ is the natural choice.
ただ here means 'merely / nothing but', not the unrelated ただ meaning 'free of charge'.

examples.ja: 準備はすべて整った。あとはただ本番を待つのみだ。
examples.en: All the preparations are complete. Now the only thing left is to wait for the real event.
examples.f: ｜準備[じゅんび]はすべて｜整[ととの]った。あとはただ｜本番[ほんばん]を｜待[ま]つのみだ。

examples.ja: 彼は弁明もせず、ただ黙ってうなずくのみだった。
examples.en: He offered no excuse and did nothing but nod silently.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜弁明[べんめい]もせず、ただ｜黙[だま]ってうなずくのみだった。

synonyms.note: のみ alone already means 'only' in a literary register; ただ〜のみだ frames it emphatically as 'nothing but'.
だけ is the everyday word for 'only'; ただ〜のみだ is its formal, emphatic counterpart.

related.note: ばかり also limits to 'only / just', but colloquially and often with a nuance of excess; ただ〜のみだ is formal and clean.

title: 〜たつもりはない
meaning: have no sense of having done ~; didn't mean to have done ~
summary: Built on the た-form, 〜たつもりはない denies, from the speaker's own standpoint, that they did or intended a certain thing — 嘘をついたつもりはない = I don't believe I lied / I didn't mean to lie. It defends against an accusation or impression by asserting one had no such intent or awareness. Contrast with dictionary-form 〜つもりはない, which denies a future intention.
pitfalls: た-form つもりはない denies having done/intended something ('I didn't mean to have ~'); dictionary-form 〜つもりはない denies future intention ('I don't intend to ~').
It expresses the speaker's own view, so it often reads as a defense against how one is being perceived.

examples.ja: 君を傷つけたつもりはないが、そう感じたのなら謝る。
examples.en: I didn't mean to hurt you, but if that's how you felt, I apologize.
examples.f: ｜君[きみ]を｜傷[きず]つけたつもりはないが、そう｜感[かん]じたのなら｜謝[あやま]る。

examples.ja: 手を抜いたつもりはない。これが全力を尽くした結果だ。
examples.en: It's not that I cut corners — this is the result of giving it everything I had.
examples.f: ｜手[て]を｜抜[ぬ]いたつもりはない。これが｜全力[ぜんりょく]を｜尽[つ]くした｜結果[けっか]だ。

synonyms.note: つもり on its own states an intention; たつもりはない denies having had a given intention or awareness after the fact.

title: 〜たところで
meaning: even if (one does/did) ~, it would be no use
summary: 〜たところで sets up a hypothetical and dismisses it as futile: even if you do X, the result won't help. The main clause is negative or pointless — 急いだところで間に合わない = even if I hurry, I won't make it. Though it uses the た-form, it refers to a hypothetical or future action, and often follows いくら or 今さら.
pitfalls: The main clause is negative or futile: 'even if ~, it won't help' — not a neutral 'even if'.
It takes the た-form but points to a hypothetical/future action, not a past one.

examples.ja: 今から走ったところで、終電には間に合わないだろう。
examples.en: Even if I run now, I still won't make the last train.
examples.f: ｜今[いま]から｜走[はし]ったところで、｜終電[しゅうでん]には｜間に合[まにあ]わないだろう。

examples.ja: いくら悔やんだところで、過ぎたことはもう戻らない。
examples.en: No matter how much you regret it, what's done can't be undone.
examples.f: いくら｜悔[く]やんだところで、｜過[す]ぎたことはもう｜戻[もど]らない。

synonyms.note: たって is a casual 'even if'; たところで adds the specific nuance that the effort would be pointless.
ても is a neutral 'even if'; たところで strongly implies the outcome would be futile.

title: 〜だに・〜だにしない
meaning: even (just); (not) even
summary: だに is an archaic 'even' surviving mainly in fixed expressions. With an affirmative, 想像するだに恐ろしい = it is terrifying just to imagine. In the form 〜だにしない it means 'not even ~': 微動だにしない = doesn't budge in the slightest, 予想だにしなかった = didn't even imagine. It attaches to a dictionary-form verb or noun and is strongly literary.
pitfalls: だに is archaic and not freely productive; it lives mostly in set phrases (想像するだに, 微動だにしない, 予想だにしない).
For a plain, modern 'even', use さえ or すら instead.

examples.ja: あんな悲劇が起こるとは、当時は予想だにしなかった。
examples.en: At the time, I never even imagined that such a tragedy could happen.
examples.f: あんな｜悲劇[ひげき]が｜起[お]こるとは、｜当時[とうじ]は｜予想[よそう]だにしなかった。

examples.ja: 厳しい批判を浴びても、彼の決意は微動だにしなかった。
examples.en: Even under harsh criticism, his resolve did not waver in the slightest.
examples.f: ｜厳[きび]しい｜批判[ひはん]を｜浴[あ]びても、｜彼[かれ]の｜決意[けつい]は｜微動[びどう]だにしなかった。

synonyms.note: すら is emphatic 'even' and freer to use; だに is archaic and confined to fixed expressions.
さえ is the everyday 'even'; だに is its literary, restricted counterpart.

title: 〜だの〜だの
meaning: and the like; ~ and ~ (dismissive listing)
summary: Aだの Bだの lists representative examples, usually with a dismissive, complaining, or exasperated tone — 給料が安いだの休みがないだの = 'pay is low, there are no days off,' and so on. It attaches to nouns, plain-form verbs, and adjectives, and implies there are more grievances of the same kind. The listed items are often other people's complaints the speaker finds tiresome.
pitfalls: だの〜だの usually carries a dismissive or complaining nuance, unlike neutral とか〜とか.
The listed items are treated as a bothersome sample; the implication is that there are yet more of them.

examples.ja: 給料が安いだの残業が多いだの、彼は不満ばかり口にしている。
examples.en: The pay's low, there's too much overtime — he does nothing but voice complaints like these.
examples.f: ｜給料[きゅうりょう]が｜安[やす]いだの｜残業[ざんぎょう]が｜多[おお]いだの、｜彼[かれ]は｜不満[ふまん]ばかり｜口[くち]にしている。

examples.ja: 暑いだの寒いだのと、あの人はいつも文句が多い。
examples.en: Too hot, too cold — that person is always full of complaints.
examples.f: ｜暑[あつ]いだの｜寒[さむ]いだのと、あの｜人[ひと]はいつも｜文句[もんく]が｜多[おお]い。

synonyms.note: とか〜とか lists examples neutrally; だの〜だの adds a complaining, dismissive tone.
やら〜やら lists things amid confusion or overwhelm; だの〜だの leans toward criticism or grievance.

related.note: なり〜なり offers alternatives to choose from ('either ~ or ~'); だの〜だの merely lists grievances.

title: 〜たはいいが
meaning: it's all well and good that ~, but; ~ turned out fine, only then
summary: 〜たはいいが presents a completed action as a positive, decisive step, then reveals an unforeseen problem it led to — 買ったはいいが使い方が分からない = buying it was fine, but I can't figure out how to use it. It builds on the た-form and often appears as はいいけれど. The pattern always pivots on that 'but', where trouble follows the good first move.
structure: Verb［た form］＋はいいが／はいいけれど
pitfalls: The first clause is viewed positively as done; the twist is that it produced an unexpected difficulty.
The problem in the second clause is essential — without it the pattern makes no sense.

examples.ja: 思い切って起業したはいいが、資金繰りに苦労している。
examples.en: Taking the plunge and starting a business was all well and good, but I'm struggling to manage the cash flow.
examples.f: ｜思い切[おもいき]って｜起業[きぎょう]したはいいが、｜資金繰[しきんぐ]りに｜苦労[くろう]している。

examples.ja: 仕事を引き受けたはいいが、締め切りに間に合いそうもない。
examples.en: Taking on the job was fine, but it doesn't look like I'll make the deadline.
examples.f: ｜仕事[しごと]を｜引き受[ひきう]けたはいいが、｜締め切[しめき]りに｜間に合[まにあ]いそうもない。

synonyms.note: ものの means 'although' generally; たはいいが specifically frames 'did the thing, but then hit trouble'.
とはいえ concedes a point before qualifying it; たはいいが centers on a completed action followed by an unforeseen snag.

title: 〜た弾みに・〜た拍子に
kana: たはずみに・たひょうしに
romaji: ta hazumi ni / ta hyoushi ni
meaning: in the instant of doing ~; and just then (accidentally)
summary: 弾み (はずみ) and 拍子 (ひょうし) both mean 'the momentary instant of' an action, after which an unintended, reflexive result follows — 転んだ拍子に手をついた = the moment I fell, I threw out my hand. Built on the た-form, the pattern stresses that the second event was accidental and triggered in that instant. It can also follow a noun as 〜の拍子に (何かの拍子に = by some chance).
structure: Verb［た form］＋弾み（はずみ）に／拍子（ひょうし）に
pitfalls: 弾み is read はずみ and 拍子 is read ひょうし here.
The following event is usually unintended or reflexive — a spontaneous reaction, not a planned action.

examples.ja: 急に振り向いた拍子に、棚に頭をぶつけてしまった。
examples.en: The instant I turned around, I bumped my head on the shelf.
examples.f: ｜急[きゅう]に｜振り向[ふりむ]いた｜拍子[ひょうし]に、｜棚[たな]に｜頭[あたま]をぶつけてしまった。

examples.ja: 立ち上がった弾みに、机の上のコップを倒してしまった。
examples.en: As I stood up, I knocked over the cup on the desk without meaning to.
examples.f: ｜立ち上[たちあ]がった｜弾[はず]みに、｜机[つくえ]の｜上[うえ]のコップを｜倒[たお]してしまった。

synonyms.note: たとたん marks 'the moment ~, then ~' for any following event; 弾みに／拍子に stresses that the result was accidental and reflexive.

title: 〜ためしがない
meaning: there has never once been a case of ~; has never happened
summary: ためし (例) means 'a precedent or instance'. 〜ためしがない, built on the た-form, says that a certain thing has never once occurred, usually with a note of reproach or disappointment — 約束を守ったためしがない = has never once kept a promise. It stresses that despite expectation, the event simply never happens.
pitfalls: It normally attaches to the た-form and carries a critical tone: 'never once, despite expectations'.
ためし here is 例 ('instance'), not the verb 試す ('to try').

examples.ja: 彼の天気予想が当たったためしがない。
examples.en: His weather predictions have never once come true.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜天気[てんき]｜予想[よそう]が｜当[あ]たったためしがない。

examples.ja: あの人が時間どおりに来たためしがないので、当てにしないほうがいい。
examples.en: That person has never once shown up on time, so you'd better not count on it.
examples.f: あの｜人[ひと]が｜時間[じかん]どおりに｜来[き]たためしがないので、｜当[あ]てにしないほうがいい。

synonyms.note: たことがない states plainly 'have never done'; ためしがない adds that it never happens despite being expected to, with a reproachful tone.

title: 〜たら〜たで
meaning: even if/when ~ does turn out so, that brings its own issues
summary: Aたら Aたで repeats the same predicate to say that even when a situation does come about, it carries its own downside — or works out somehow either way. お金があったらあったで悩みがある = even having money brings its own worries. The nuance is that neither outcome is clean: whichever way it goes, there is something to deal with.
structure: Verb［た form］＋ら＋Verb［た form, same word］＋で
pitfalls: The same predicate is repeated on both sides; it is not two different actions.
The sense is 'even if it does happen, that has its own downside / it's fine either way', not a purely positive result.

examples.ja: お金なんて、あったらあったで使ってしまうものだ。
examples.en: Money is the sort of thing you just end up spending once you have it.
examples.f: お｜金[かね]なんて、あったらあったで｜使[つか]ってしまうものだ。

examples.ja: 試験が終わったら終わったで、今度は結果が気になり出す。
examples.en: Once the exam is over, then you start fretting about the results instead.
examples.f: ｜試験[しけん]が｜終[お]わったら｜終[お]わったで、｜今度[こんど]は｜結果[けっか]が｜気[き]になり｜出[だ]す。

synonyms.note: なら〜で carries the same 'if it is ~, that's its own matter' sense but attaches via なら to nouns/adjectives; たら〜たで uses the た-conditional.

title: 〜たら〜ところだ
meaning: if (counterfactually) ~ had been so, ~ would have happened
summary: This pattern pairs a counterfactual condition (〜たら) with a would-be result (〜ところだ, usually ところだった) — もう少し遅かったら、乗り遅れるところだった = if I'd been a little later, I would have missed it. The condition did not actually hold, and the ところだ clause describes what would have been on the verge of happening. It often appears with 危うく or あと少しで.
structure: Verb［た form］＋ら＋Verb［dictionary form］＋ところだった／ところだ
pitfalls: It usually ends in ところだった for a past counterfactual: the condition did not actually occur.
The result clause describes what almost happened, so it often pairs with 危うく or あと少しで.

examples.ja: あと少し出発が遅れていたら、渋滞に巻き込まれるところだった。
examples.en: If we'd left just a bit later, we would have gotten caught in the traffic jam.
examples.f: あと｜少[すこ]し｜出発[しゅっぱつ]が｜遅[おく]れていたら、｜渋滞[じゅうたい]に｜巻き込[まきこ]まれるところだった。

examples.ja: 君が教えてくれなかったら、危うく騙されるところだった。
examples.en: If you hadn't told me, I would very nearly have been deceived.
examples.f: ｜君[きみ]が｜教[おし]えてくれなかったら、｜危[あや]うく｜騙[だま]されるところだった。

synonyms.note: ところだった alone already means 'was about to / nearly happened'; たら〜ところだ supplies the explicit counterfactual condition.
ば〜のに expresses 'would have, if only' with regret; たら〜ところだ pairs the condition with a would-be event, often a narrow escape.

title: 〜たら最後・〜たが最後
kana: たらさいご・たがさいご
meaning: once you do ~, that's the end of it; there's no going back
summary: 〜たら最後 (or the more emphatic 〜たが最後) says that once a certain action occurs, an inevitable and usually undesirable consequence follows, with no way back — 一度引き受けたら最後、途中でやめられない = once you take it on, there's no quitting halfway. Built on the た-form, it stresses a point of no return.
pitfalls: 最後 is read さいご; the consequence that follows is inevitable and usually undesirable.
が最後 is a slightly more emphatic and literary variant of ら最後.

examples.ja: あの人は話し出したら最後、延々としゃべり続ける。
examples.en: Once that person starts talking, they go on and on without end.
examples.f: あの｜人[ひと]は｜話し出[はなしだ]したら｜最後[さいご]、｜延々[えんえん]としゃべり｜続[つづ]ける。

examples.ja: この魚は、一度水から出したが最後、すぐに弱ってしまう。
examples.en: Once you take this fish out of the water, it weakens right away.
examples.f: この｜魚[さかな]は、｜一度[いちど]｜水[みず]から｜出[だ]したが｜最後[さいご]、すぐに｜弱[よわ]ってしまう。

synonyms.note: ばそれまでだ means 'if ~, then it's all over'; たら最後 stresses that the action itself sets off an unstoppable chain.
ようものなら warns of dire consequences if one merely tried something; たら最後 says the deed, once done, cannot be undone.

related.note: ものなら sets up a hypothetical with serious consequences; たら最後 fixes on the irreversible point after the action.

title: 〜たりとも
meaning: not even a single ~; not so much as one ~
summary: たりとも follows '一 + counter' and pairs with a negative to mean 'not even one' — 一日たりとも忘れない = I won't forget for even a single day, 一円たりとも無駄にできない = can't waste even one yen. It is emphatic and literary. The separate idiom 何人（なんぴと）たりとも means 'no one whosoever'.
pitfalls: It is fixed with 一 + a counter and requires a negative: it means 'not even one'.
何人（なんぴと）たりとも is a separate set idiom meaning 'no one whosoever', not the counting use.

examples.ja: この計画では、一日たりとも無駄にはできない。
examples.en: In this plan, we cannot afford to waste even a single day.
examples.f: この｜計画[けいかく]では、｜一[いち]｜日[にち]たりとも｜無駄[むだ]にはできない。

examples.ja: 敵を前に、兵士たちは一瞬たりとも気を緩めなかった。
examples.en: Facing the enemy, the soldiers did not let their guard down for even an instant.
examples.f: ｜敵[てき]を｜前[まえ]に、｜兵士[へいし]たちは｜一瞬[いっしゅん]たりとも｜気[き]を｜緩[ゆる]めなかった。

synonyms.note: も with a minimal amount and a negative also gives 'not even ~'; たりとも is more emphatic and literary, and locks onto 一 + counter.

related.note: だに also gives an emphatic 'not even', but attaches to nouns/verbs in set phrases; たりとも counts with 一 + a counter.

title: 〜たる・〜たるもの
meaning: one who is (in the position of) ~ should; befitting one who is ~
summary: たる is a literary copula (equivalent to である) used attributively. 〜たるもの(は) names someone in a certain role and states how a person in that position ought to behave — 指導者たるもの、模範を示すべきだ = one who is a leader should set an example. It is formal and written, and the following clause typically expresses duty or expectation. たる can also directly modify a noun (堂々たる態度).
pitfalls: たる is a literary copula (= である); the whole pattern is formal and written.
たるもの typically leads to a statement of what befits or is required of someone in that role.

examples.ja: 指導者たるもの、常に部下の模範を示さねばならない。
examples.en: One who is a leader must always set an example for those under them.
examples.f: ｜指導[しどう]｜者[しゃ]たるもの、｜常[つね]に｜部下[ぶか]の｜模範[もはん]を｜示[しめ]さねばならない。

examples.ja: 医師たるもの、患者の前で弱音を吐くべきではない。
examples.en: A person in the position of a doctor should not show weakness in front of patients.
examples.f: ｜医師[いし]たるもの、｜患者[かんじゃ]の｜前[まえ]で｜弱音[よわね]を｜吐[は]くべきではない。

synonyms.note: ともあろうものが reproaches someone in a high position for a lapse; たるもの prescribes how such a person should act.
として states a role or capacity neutrally ('as a ~'); たるもの is formal and adds the weight of expected conduct.

title: 〜だろうに
meaning: surely ~ (and yet); would ~ if only (regret, sympathy, or reproach)
summary: だろうに follows a plain-form clause to state what would surely be true under some — usually counterfactual — condition, while the actual situation falls short, leaving a feeling of pity, regret, or mild reproach. 早く言ってくれれば助けられただろうに = if you had told me sooner I could have helped you (but you didn't). The に carries the unspoken 'and yet…'. It often follows a conditional, and the disappointing reality is frequently left implied.
pitfalls: The disappointing reality is often left unsaid; だろうに itself carries the 'and yet…' of regret or reproach.
This is the wistful だろう＋に; don't read に as the location or target particle.

examples.ja: もう少し早く家を出ていれば、間に合っただろうに。
examples.en: If you had left the house a little earlier, you surely would have made it in time.
examples.f: もう｜少[すこ]し｜早[はや]く｜家[いえ]を｜出[で]ていれば、｜間に合[まにあ]っただろうに。

examples.ja: 彼女に一言相談してくれれば、こんな失敗はしなかっただろうに。
examples.en: If only he had consulted her with a single word, he wouldn't have made a mistake like this.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]に｜一言[ひとこと]｜相談[そうだん]してくれれば、こんな｜失敗[しっぱい]はしなかっただろうに。

synonyms.note: ものを also voices regret that reality went against a preferable hypothetical, but is more literary and reproachful; だろうに centers on the speaker's 'surely it would have…' inference.

related.note: plain だろう is a conjecture ('probably'); adding に turns it into wistful regret or reproach about how things could have been.
のに contrasts an actual result with expectation; だろうに contrasts a desirable hypothetical with a disappointing, often counterfactual, reality.

title: 〜つ〜つ
meaning: now ~ now ~; alternately doing one thing and its opposite
summary: A literary pattern that joins two verb stems (連用形) each with つ, describing two actions that alternate or play off one another — typically a pair of opposites. 行きつ戻りつ = pacing back and forth, 追いつ追われつ = chasing and being chased by turns. It survives mainly in set expressions, often pairing one active verb with its passive form. The tone is descriptive and literary, not everyday speech.
pitfalls: Mostly limited to fixed pairs (行きつ戻りつ, 浮きつ沈みつ, 追いつ追われつ); it is not freely productive with any two verbs.
The two verbs are usually opposites, and often one is the active and the other the passive form of the same verb.

examples.ja: 小舟が波に浮きつ沈みつしていた。
examples.en: The small boat bobbed on the waves, rising and sinking by turns.
examples.f: ｜小舟[こぶね]が｜波[なみ]に｜浮[う]きつ｜沈[しず]みつしていた。

examples.ja: 彼は返事を書こうとして、部屋を行きつ戻りつしていた。
examples.en: Trying to write a reply, he paced back and forth across the room.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜返事[へんじ]を｜書[か]こうとして、｜部屋[へや]を｜行[い]きつ｜戻[もど]りつしていた。

synonyms.note: 〜たり〜たり is the everyday way to list alternating or representative actions; つ〜つ is a frozen literary form confined to set opposite-verb pairs.

related.note: つつ ('while / although') marks one action accompanying another and is fully productive; the doubled つ〜つ is a separate fixed pattern for two alternating actions.

title: 〜尽くす
meaning: to do (something) thoroughly / to the very end; to exhaust; to use up completely
summary: Verb stem + 尽くす says the action is carried out completely, to the limit, leaving nothing over — either using something up (使い尽くす = use up entirely, 食べ尽くす = eat it all) or doing something exhaustively (知り尽くす = know inside out, 語り尽くす = talk through completely). It stresses that the action has been taken as far as it can go. The intransitive counterpart 尽きる ('run out') is a separate verb.
pitfalls: 尽くす is transitive ('do fully / use up'); the paired intransitive 尽きる means '(something) runs out' — 力を出し尽くす vs 力が尽きる.
It stresses thoroughness and exhaustion, unlike 〜切る, which often stresses seeing an action decisively through to the end.

examples.ja: できる手はすべて尽くしたが、事態は好転しなかった。
examples.en: We did everything we possibly could, but the situation did not improve.
examples.f: できる｜手[て]はすべて｜尽[つ]くしたが、｜事態[じたい]は｜好転[こうてん]しなかった。

examples.ja: この街のことなら、路地の隅々まで知り尽くしている。
examples.en: When it comes to this town, I know every last corner of its back alleys.
examples.f: この｜街[まち]のことなら、｜路地[ろじ]の｜隅々[すみずみ]まで｜知[し]り｜尽[つ]くしている。

synonyms.note: 〜切る marks carrying an action decisively through to completion (走り切る); 尽くす emphasizes doing it exhaustively or using it up to the last.
〜抜く stresses pushing an action through to the end despite hardship; 尽くす stresses thoroughness and leaving nothing undone.

related.note: 〜通す means keeping an action up all the way through; 尽くす means carrying it out to its fullest extent.

title: 〜ってば・〜ったら
meaning: I said ~! ; come on, ~ (impatient insistence or exasperation)
summary: Both are colloquial sentence-enders that add impatience or exasperation. ってば reasserts something the listener didn't heed — もう行くってば = I said I'm going! ったら similarly nags or scolds, and after a person's name expresses exasperated fondness or complaint — お父さんったら = oh, Dad, honestly… They belong to casual spoken Japanese and always carry clear emotion.
pitfalls: Casual spoken style only; too emotional and informal for polite or written contexts.
This ったら is the exasperated ender; don't confuse it with conditional 〜たら ('if / when').

examples.ja: 大丈夫だってば。そんなに心配しないで。
examples.en: I'm fine, I told you. Don't worry so much.
examples.f: ｜大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]だってば。そんなに｜心配[しんぱい]しないで。

examples.ja: お母さんったら、私の話を全然聞いてないんだから。
examples.en: Honestly, Mom — you're not listening to a word I say.
examples.f: お｜母[かあ]さんったら、｜私[わたし]の｜話[はなし]を｜全然[ぜんぜん]｜聞[き]いてないんだから。

synonyms.note: casual って quotes or restates what was said; adding ば (ってば) turns it into impatient insistence that the point already stands.

title: であれ〜であれ
meaning: whether A or B; be it A or B (it makes no difference)
summary: Placing であれ after each of two (or more) nouns lists them as alternatives that don't change the outcome — 'whether A or B'. 大人であれ子どもであれ、ルールは同じだ = whether adult or child, the rules are the same. であれ is the concessive form of である, so the register is formal or written. The main clause states something that holds across every listed case.
pitfalls: Attaches directly to nouns (and な-adjective stems); it does not take だ — 晴れであれ雨であれ, not 晴れだであれ.
Formal, written register; in casual speech でも〜でも covers the same 'whether A or B'.

examples.ja: 賛成であれ反対であれ、まずは自分の意見をはっきり述べてほしい。
examples.en: Whether you are for or against, I first want you to state your own opinion clearly.
examples.f: ｜賛成[さんせい]であれ｜反対[はんたい]であれ、まずは｜自分[じぶん]の｜意見[いけん]をはっきり｜述[の]べてほしい。

examples.ja: 仕事であれ趣味であれ、中途半端にするのが一番よくない。
examples.en: Be it work or a hobby, doing it half-heartedly is the worst thing of all.
examples.f: ｜仕事[しごと]であれ｜趣味[しゅみ]であれ、｜中途半端[ちゅうとはんぱ]にするのが｜一番[いちばん]よくない。

synonyms.note: single であれ pairs with a question word ('no matter what/who'); であれ〜であれ lists two specific named alternatives.
にしろ〜にしろ also lists 'whether A or B' alternatives; であれ〜であれ is a touch more formal and literary.

related.note: ようが〜ようが lists contrasting verb or adjective cases ('whether one does or not'); であれ〜であれ lists noun alternatives.

title: 〜であれ・〜であろうと
meaning: no matter what/who/how ~; whatever ~ may be
summary: After a question word (or a noun paired with one), であれ and であろうと concede that the outcome holds regardless — どんな事情であれ = whatever the circumstances, 誰であろうと = no matter who it is. であろうと adds a slightly stronger 'even supposing' nuance. Both are the concessive of である and belong to formal or written Japanese; the main clause states what applies in every case.
structure: Question word＋であれ／であろうと
pitfalls: It typically pairs with a question word (どんな, 誰, どこ) to give the 'no matter ~' reading.
Formal register; the everyday equivalent is でも (どんな理由でも, 誰でも).

examples.ja: どんな困難であろうと、最後までやり遂げる覚悟だ。
examples.en: No matter what hardships arise, I am resolved to see it through to the end.
examples.f: どんな｜困難[こんなん]であろうと、｜最後[さいご]までやり｜遂[と]げる｜覚悟[かくご]だ。

examples.ja: 相手が誰であれ、言うべきことははっきり言う。
examples.en: No matter who I am dealing with, I say clearly what needs to be said.
examples.f: ｜相手[あいて]が｜誰[だれ]であれ、｜言[い]うべきことははっきり｜言[い]う。

synonyms.note: であれ〜であれ lists two named alternatives; single であれ pairs with a question word for 'no matter what'.
ようが／ようと concedes over verbs and adjectives ('no matter how one does'); であれ concedes over a noun or question word.
いかなる〜であれ／であろうと is a set formal pairing; であれ supplies the concession that いかなる ('any whatsoever') modifies.

related.note: 〜ても is the basic 'even if'; であれ／であろうと is its formal noun-based counterpart for 'whatever it may be'.

title: 〜てかなわない・〜てはかなわない
kana: てかなわない・てはかなわない
meaning: unbearably ~; can't stand it that ~; too ~ to put up with
summary: 〜てかなわない says a condition is more than the speaker can bear — it is unbearably or intolerably so. 暑くてかなわない = unbearably hot, this heat is too much. It typically follows adjectives or verbs describing a sensation or feeling and expresses the speaker's own discomfort. The variant 〜てはかなわない frames it as 'it would be unbearable if ~', pushing back against a possibility.
pitfalls: Expresses the speaker's own unbearable discomfort; it isn't used to report someone else's feelings objectively.
Here かなわない means 'cannot endure', not the other 敵わない ('be no match for').

examples.ja: 隣の工事の音がうるさくてかなわない。
examples.en: The noise from the construction next door is unbearably loud.
examples.f: ｜隣[となり]の｜工事[こうじ]の｜音[おと]がうるさくてかなわない。

examples.ja: 毎日こう残業続きではかなわない。
examples.en: If overtime keeps piling up like this every day, I just can't take it.
examples.f: ｜毎日[まいにち]こう｜残業[ざんぎょう]｜続[つづ]きではかなわない。

synonyms.note: 〜てたまらない ('unbearably ~') is close and a touch more neutral in feeling; てかなわない stresses annoyance and exasperation at having to put up with it.
〜てならない marks a feeling that wells up uncontrollably; てかなわない specifically marks something as too much to endure.
〜てしょうがない ('can't help feeling ~') is the casual all-purpose version; てかなわない leans toward an intolerable nuisance.

title: 〜てからというもの
meaning: ever since ~; from the time ~, and continuing ever after
summary: 〜てからというもの marks a past event as the turning point after which a state has held continuously ever since. 引っ越してからというもの、一度も会っていない = ever since I moved, I haven't seen them even once. It is more emphatic and emotive than plain てから, stressing that a lasting change set in from that moment and persists. The following clause describes the ongoing situation.
structure: Verb［て form］＋からというもの
pitfalls: Points to a lasting change that has continued ever since a single past event, not a one-time result.
More emphatic and emotional than plain 〜てから; reserve it for a genuine before-and-after shift.

examples.ja: あの本に出会ってからというもの、彼の人生観は大きく変わった。
examples.en: Ever since he came across that book, his outlook on life changed completely.
examples.f: あの｜本[ほん]に｜出会[であ]ってからというもの、｜彼[かれ]の｜人生[じんせい]｜観[かん]は｜大[おお]きく｜変[か]わった。

examples.ja: 犬を飼い始めてからというもの、毎朝の散歩が日課になった。
examples.en: Ever since we started keeping a dog, a walk every morning has become part of the routine.
examples.f: ｜犬[いぬ]を｜飼[か]い｜始[はじ]めてからというもの、｜毎朝[まいあさ]の｜散歩[さんぽ]が｜日課[にっか]になった。

synonyms.note: 〜て以来 also means 'ever since ~' and is more neutral and objective; てからというもの adds emotional emphasis on the sustained change.

related.note: plain 〜てから just orders one action after another; てからというもの stresses a lasting change that has held ever since.

title: 〜てしかるべきだ
meaning: ought to be ~; it is only natural/proper that ~; deserves to be ~
summary: 〜てしかるべきだ says something is proper and to be expected — it ought to be so as a matter of course. 努力は評価されてしかるべきだ = such effort ought to be, and deserves to be, recognized. しかるべき means 'appropriate / as it should be', so the phrase asserts that the state described by the て-form is the natural, reasonable thing. It is formal and often argues that something rightly should happen.
pitfalls: Formal, written or argumentative register; not for everyday conversation.
It often attaches to a passive て-form (評価されて, 認められて) to say 'ought rightly to be ~ed'.

examples.ja: これだけの成果を上げたのだから、正当に評価されてしかるべきだ。
examples.en: Having produced results of this magnitude, he ought by rights to be properly recognized.
examples.f: これだけの｜成果[せいか]を｜上[あ]げたのだから、｜正当[せいとう]に｜評価[ひょうか]されてしかるべきだ。

examples.ja: 消費者への説明があってしかるべきだったが、企業は沈黙を続けた。
examples.en: There should by rights have been an explanation to consumers, yet the company kept silent.
examples.f: ｜消費[しょうひ]｜者[しゃ]への｜説明[せつめい]があってしかるべきだったが、｜企業[きぎょう]は｜沈黙[ちんもく]を｜続[つづ]けた。

synonyms.note: plain 〜べきだ states a direct 'should / ought to'; てしかるべきだ frames it as what is only natural and proper, often more measured and formal.
〜て当然だ ('naturally ~; no wonder ~') also says something is to be expected; てしかるべきだ adds the sense that it is the proper, deserved thing.

title: 〜て済むことではない
meaning: not something that ~ will settle; ~ing is not enough to resolve it
summary: 〜て済むことではない declares that merely doing the stated action is not enough to put a matter to rest — the problem is too serious for that. 謝って済むことではない = this isn't something an apology will make right. 済む here means 'be settled / get by', so the negative says the issue won't be closed off just by that action, implying graver consequences or responsibility. It carries a reproachful, weighty tone.
structure: Verb［て form］＋済むことではない
pitfalls: 済む here means 'be settled / suffice', so 〜て済むことではない says the action falls short of resolving the matter — it is not about literally 'finishing'.
Carries a reproachful, serious tone; reserve it for genuinely grave matters.

examples.ja: 人を傷つけておいて、「知らなかった」で済むことではない。
examples.en: Having hurt someone, this is not something you can settle with 'I didn't know'.
examples.f: ｜人[ひと]を｜傷[きず]つけておいて、「｜知[し]らなかった」で｜済[す]むことではない。

examples.ja: これは担当者が辞めて済むことではない、組織全体の問題だ。
examples.en: This is not something that gets resolved by the person in charge quitting; it is a problem for the whole organization.
examples.f: これは｜担当[たんとう]｜者[しゃ]が｜辞[や]めて｜済[す]むことではない、｜組織[そしき]｜全体[ぜんたい]の｜問題[もんだい]だ。

synonyms.note: 〜では済まない says a situation won't end with just ~ (and worse will follow); て済むことではない specifically denies that a given action can settle the matter.
〜ずには済まない means one can't avoid doing ~ (it's unavoidable); て済むことではない means doing ~ isn't enough to resolve things — the opposite angle on 済む.

related.note: 〜て済む affirms that something can be gotten through or settled by ~; て済むことではない negates exactly that.

title: 〜でなくてなんだろう
meaning: if this is not ~, then what is it? (this is surely ~)
summary: A rhetorical construction: 'if this is not (a) ~, what could it be?' — used to assert emphatically that something truly deserves to be called ~. これが奇跡でなくてなんだろう = if this isn't a miracle, what is? It attaches to a noun and drives home a heartfelt, often emotional judgment. Literary and emphatic, it appears in essays and impassioned writing rather than casual talk.
structure: Noun＋でなくてなんだろう（か）
pitfalls: It is rhetorical: the 'what is it?' expects no answer and firmly asserts that the noun does apply.
Literary and emotive; the noun is usually a weighty, evaluative one (愛, 奇跡, 運命, 幸福).

examples.ja: 見ず知らずの人のために命を懸ける。これが勇気でなくてなんだろう。
examples.en: To risk one's life for a total stranger — if this is not courage, then what is?
examples.f: ｜見ず知[みずし]らずの｜人[ひと]のために｜命[いのち]を｜懸[か]ける。これが｜勇気[ゆうき]でなくてなんだろう。

examples.ja: 長年の努力がこうして実った。これが幸福でなくてなんだろうか。
examples.en: Years of effort have borne fruit like this. If this is not happiness, what could it be?
examples.f: ｜長年[ながねん]の｜努力[どりょく]がこうして｜実[みの]った。これが｜幸福[こうふく]でなくてなんだろうか。

synonyms.note: 〜にほかならない flatly asserts 'is nothing other than ~'; でなくてなんだろう reaches the same conclusion through an emotional rhetorical question.

title: 〜ではあるまいか
meaning: isn't it perhaps that ~? ; might it not be the case that ~?
summary: 〜ではあるまいか is a formal, literary way to float a tentative supposition — 'might it not be ~? / perhaps it is ~'. あるまい is the classical negative conjecture of ある, so this equals a bookish ではないだろうか. 何か誤解があるのではあるまいか = might there not be some misunderstanding? The speaker advances a guess while leaving room for doubt, in an essayistic or formal register.
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋のではあるまいか
pitfalls: Formal, literary register; the everyday equivalent is 〜のではないだろうか / 〜んじゃないか.
あるまい is a negative conjecture ('surely not'), so the whole phrase softly proposes 'perhaps ~?', not a firm denial.

examples.ja: この計画には、どこか無理があるのではあるまいか。
examples.en: Might there not be something unworkable about this plan?
examples.f: この｜計画[けいかく]には、どこか｜無理[むり]があるのではあるまいか。

examples.ja: 彼の沈黙こそ、何よりの答えなのではあるまいか。
examples.en: Is his silence not, perhaps, the clearest answer of all?
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜沈黙[ちんもく]こそ、｜何[なに]よりの｜答[こた]えなのではあるまいか。

synonyms.note: 〜のではないだろうか is the standard 'isn't it that ~?'; ではあるまいか is its formal, literary equivalent built on classical あるまい.
〜ではないか asserts 'isn't it ~!' with some force; ではあるまいか stays tentative and reflective ('perhaps ~?').

related.note: まい is the classical negative conjecture behind あるまい ('surely won't be'); ではあるまいか packages it into a softened supposition.

title: 〜ではあるまいし・〜じゃあるまいし
kana: ではあるまいし・じゃあるまいし
romaji: dewa arumai shi / ja arumai shi
meaning: it's not as if ~; ~ is not the case, so (you should…)
summary: 〜ではあるまいし dismisses a scenario as clearly untrue and uses that to justify a criticism, complaint, or piece of advice in the following clause. 子供じゃあるまいし、それくらい自分でやりなさい = you're not a child, so do that much yourself. あるまい gives 'surely it isn't ~', and し adds 'and so…'. The じゃあるまいし form is conversational, and the tone is often reproachful or exasperated.
structure: Noun＋ではあるまいし／じゃあるまいし
Verb［plain form］＋のではあるまいし
pitfalls: The following clause is the real point — usually a rebuke, complaint, or piece of advice that follows from 'it's not as if ~'.
じゃあるまいし is casual spoken style; ではあるまいし is the more formal written form.

examples.ja: 新人じゃあるまいし、この程度のミスには気をつけてほしい。
examples.en: It's not as if you're a newcomer, so I'd like you to be careful about mistakes at this level.
examples.f: ｜新人[しんじん]じゃあるまいし、この｜程度[ていど]のミスには｜気[き]をつけてほしい。

examples.ja: 神様ではあるまいし、未来のことなど誰にも分からない。
examples.en: None of us is a god, so no one can know what the future holds.
examples.f: ｜神様[かみさま]ではあるまいし、｜未来[みらい]のことなど｜誰[だれ]にも｜分[わ]からない。

related.note: まい supplies the negative conjecture あるまい ('surely not ~'); ではあるまいし turns that into grounds for the criticism that follows.

title: 〜では済まない
meaning: won't be settled with just ~; ~ won't be the end of it
summary: 〜では済まない warns that a matter will not be brought to a close by merely the stated thing — worse will be required or will follow. 口先の謝罪だけでは済まないだろう = a token apology won't be enough to settle this. 済む means 'be settled / get by', so the negative says getting off with just ~ is impossible. It signals that the consequences run deeper than the listener might hope.
structure: Verb［plain form］＋だけでは済まない
pitfalls: 済まない here means 'won't be settled / won't get by', not 'sorry' (the apology すまない).
It warns that the matter needs more than ~, implying heavier consequences to come.

examples.ja: これだけの損害を出したのだ。始末書一枚では済まないだろう。
examples.en: We've caused this much damage. It won't be settled with a single letter of apology.
examples.f: これだけの｜損害[そんがい]を｜出[だ]したのだ。｜始末[しまつ]｜書[しょ]｜一[いち]｜枚[まい]では｜済[す]まないだろう。

examples.ja: 約束を破れば、ただの謝罪では済まない。
examples.en: If you break the promise, a mere apology won't be the end of it.
examples.f: ｜約束[やくそく]を｜破[やぶ]れば、ただの｜謝罪[しゃざい]では｜済[す]まない。

synonyms.note: 〜て済むことではない denies that a specific action can settle things; では済まない says a given measure won't suffice and worse will follow — both turn on 済む.
〜ずには済まない means one won't get away without doing ~ (unavoidable); では済まない means one won't get away with just ~.

related.note: 〜て済む says a matter can be settled or gotten through with ~; では済まない denies exactly that possibility.

title: 〜てみせる
meaning: I'll do ~ (and show them); to demonstrate by actually doing ~
summary: 〜てみせる has two related senses. Literally it means performing an action to show someone how — お手本を書いてみせる = write it out to demonstrate. More pointedly, with volitional force it declares firm determination to accomplish something, often to prove others wrong: 必ず成功してみせる = I'll succeed, just you watch. The determination reading is emphatic and self-assertive, common in resolutions and challenges.
pitfalls: Distinguish the two readings: neutral 'demonstrate by doing' vs. emphatic 'I'll definitely do it (and prove it)' — context and often 必ず/きっと signal the latter.
The determination sense is about the speaker's own resolve; it isn't used to describe a third person's plans neutrally.

examples.ja: 今度こそ合格して、家族を安心させてみせる。
examples.en: This time for sure I'll pass and put my family's mind at ease — just watch me.
examples.f: ｜今度[こんど]こそ｜合格[ごうかく]して、｜家族[かぞく]を｜安心[あんしん]させてみせる。

examples.ja: 先生は正しい持ち方を、ゆっくりやってみせてくれた。
examples.en: The teacher slowly demonstrated the correct way to hold it for us.
examples.f: ｜先生[せんせい]は｜正[ただ]しい｜持[も]ち｜方[かた]を、ゆっくりやってみせてくれた。

synonyms.note: 〜てやる can also express defiant determination ('I'll show them / just you wait'); てみせる adds the nuance of proving it before others' eyes.

related.note: 〜てみる is 'try doing ~ (to see how it goes)'; てみせる is 'do ~ to show someone' or 'vow to pull it off' — resolve, not tentative trying.

title: 〜でもあり〜でもある
romaji: de mo ari ~ de mo aru
meaning: is both ~ and ~; is at once ~ and ~
summary: 〜でもあり〜でもある presents two qualities or roles that hold at the same time — X is both A and B. 彼は研究者でもあり、教育者でもある = he is both a researcher and an educator. It attaches to nouns (and な-adjective stems) and stresses that the subject genuinely embodies two aspects together, often ones that complement or contrast. The register is somewhat formal and measured.
pitfalls: Both halves describe one and the same subject holding two qualities at once, not two separate things.
It uses でもあり／でもある (the connective form あり in the first half); it is not 〜でもあって〜でもある in careful writing.

examples.ja: この作品は娯楽でもあり、同時に社会への鋭い批評でもある。
examples.en: This work is entertainment and, at the same time, a sharp critique of society.
examples.f: この｜作品[さくひん]は｜娯楽[ごらく]でもあり、｜同時[どうじ]に｜社会[しゃかい]への｜鋭[するど]い｜批評[ひひょう]でもある。

examples.ja: 彼女にとって庭仕事は趣味でもあり、心を整える時間でもある。
examples.en: For her, gardening is both a hobby and a time to settle her mind.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]にとって｜庭[にわ]｜仕事[しごと]は｜趣味[しゅみ]でもあり、｜心[こころ]を｜整[ととの]える｜時間[じかん]でもある。

synonyms.note: 〜でもある notes one additional quality ('is also ~'); でもあり〜でもある pairs two qualities as simultaneously true.

title: 〜ても差し支えない
meaning: it's fine even if ~; there is no problem with ~; may ~
summary: 〜ても差し支えない grants that doing something causes no problem or inconvenience — it is permissible. 写真を撮っても差し支えありません = you may take photos; there's no problem. 差し支え means 'hindrance / obstacle', so the phrase says 'even if ~, there is no hindrance'. It is a formal, polite way of giving permission, more measured than the everyday てもいい.
structure: Verb［て form］＋も差し支えない
い-adjective［て form］＋も差し支えない
pitfalls: Formal, polite permission; in casual situations 〜てもいい is the natural choice.
差し支え means 'hindrance', so 差し支えない = 'poses no problem' — the whole says permission is granted, not that something is required.

examples.ja: 記入は鉛筆でも差し支えありませんが、はっきりと書いてください。
examples.en: It is perfectly fine to fill this in with pencil, but please write clearly.
examples.f: ｜記入[きにゅう]は｜鉛筆[えんぴつ]でも｜差し支[さしつか]えありませんが、はっきりと｜書[か]いてください。

examples.ja: ご都合が悪ければ、日程を変更しても差し支えございません。
examples.en: If it is inconvenient for you, there is no problem with changing the schedule.
examples.f: ご｜都合[つごう]が｜悪[わる]ければ、｜日程[にってい]を｜変更[へんこう]しても｜差し支[さしつか]えございません。

synonyms.note: 〜てもいい is the everyday 'may / it's okay to ~'; ても差し支えない is a formal, polite equivalent for granting permission.
〜ても構わない means 'I don't mind if ~'; ても差し支えない frames the same permission as 'causes no problem', slightly more formal.

title: 〜ても知らない
meaning: don't blame me if ~; I won't be responsible even if ~
summary: 〜ても知らない is a warning that the speaker washes their hands of the consequences: 'even if ~ happens, that's not my problem'. そんなに食べたら、お腹を壊しても知らないよ = if you eat that much and get a stomachache, don't blame me. 知らない here means 'I take no responsibility', not 'I don't know'. It typically follows a hypothetical the speaker has advised against, and is casual and admonishing.
structure: Sentence＋（どう）なっても知らない
pitfalls: 知らない here means 'I won't be responsible', not literally 'I don't know'.
Conversational and admonishing; usually aimed at behavior the speaker has warned against, often ending in 〜よ.

examples.ja: 宿題をやらないで行って、先生に叱られても知らないよ。
examples.en: If you go without doing your homework and get scolded by the teacher, don't come crying to me.
examples.f: ｜宿題[しゅくだい]をやらないで｜行[い]って、｜先生[せんせい]に｜叱[しか]られても｜知[し]らないよ。

examples.ja: 今から準備しないと、当日慌てても知らないからね。
examples.en: If you don't start preparing now, don't blame me when you're in a panic on the day.
examples.f: ｜今[いま]から｜準備[じゅんび]しないと、｜当日[とうじつ]｜慌[あわ]てても｜知[し]らないからね。

related.note: 〜たら最後 warns that once ~ happens an unavoidable bad result follows; ても知らない warns that the speaker won't take responsibility for such a result.

title: 〜てもどうにもならない
kana: てもどうにもならない
romaji: te mo dou ni mo naranai
meaning: it's no use even if ~; ~ won't help; nothing can be done even if ~
summary: 〜てもどうにもならない says that even doing the stated thing changes nothing — the situation is beyond remedy. 今さら後悔してもどうにもならない = there's no use regretting it now. どうにもならない means 'nothing can be done about it', so the pattern declares the action futile against an unfixable situation. It is often used to dismiss pointless worry, regret, or effort.
structure: Verb［て form］＋もどうにもならない
pitfalls: Declares the action pointless because the situation can't be changed — stronger than merely 'it's not very useful'.
Often paired with 今さら ('at this late stage') to stress that acting now would be futile.

examples.ja: 過ぎたことをいつまでも悔やんでも、どうにもならない。
examples.en: No matter how long you keep regretting what's past, it won't change a thing.
examples.f: ｜過[か]ぎたことをいつまでも｜悔[く]やんでも、どうにもならない。

examples.ja: ひとりで抱え込んでもどうにもならないから、正直に相談したほうがいい。
examples.en: Bottling it up on your own won't fix anything, so you had better talk to someone honestly.
examples.f: ひとりで｜抱え込[かかえこ]んでもどうにもならないから、｜正直[しょうじき]に｜相談[そうだん]したほうがいい。

synonyms.note: 〜ても始まらない says there's no point setting out on ~ because it leads nowhere; てもどうにもならない says even doing ~ can't fix the situation.
〜てもしょうがない ('no use ~ing') is the casual all-purpose version; てもどうにもならない stresses that the situation itself is beyond remedy.

related.note: どうにも〜ない means '(cannot) ~ in any way at all'; てもどうにもならない is the fixed 'even if ~, nothing can be done'.

title: 〜でも何でもない・〜くも何ともない
kana: でもなんでもない・くもなんともない
romaji: de mo nan de mo nai / ku mo nan to mo nai
meaning: not ~ at all; nothing of the sort; not in the least ~
summary: 〜でも何でもない emphatically denies that something is the case — it's nothing of the kind. 友達でも何でもない = he's not a friend, not anything of the sort. With い-adjectives the parallel form is 〜くも何ともない (痛くも何ともない = doesn't hurt in the least). Both flatly reject a label or feeling with more force than a plain negative, often to push back against an assumption. The tone is emphatic and can be curt.
pitfalls: Use でも何でもない for nouns and な-adjectives, but くも何ともない for い-adjectives (怖くも何ともない, not 怖いでも何でもない).
Far more emphatic than a plain 〜ではない; it rejects the idea outright, often with irritation.

examples.ja: あんな人、もう友達でも何でもない。ただの他人だ。
examples.en: Someone like that is no friend of mine anymore — nothing of the sort. Just a stranger.
examples.f: あんな｜人[ひと]、もう｜友達[ともだち]でも｜何[なに]でもない。ただの｜他人[たにん]だ。

examples.ja: この程度の傷、痛くも何ともないよ。
examples.en: A scratch like this doesn't hurt in the least.
examples.f: この｜程度[ていど]の｜傷[きず]、｜痛[いた]くも｜何[なん]ともないよ。

synonyms.note: 〜わけではない is a measured partial denial ('it's not that ~'); でも何でもない is a blunt, total denial ('nothing of the sort').

related.note: 〜どころか corrects an assumption to the contrary ('far from ~, actually…'); でも何でもない simply denies the label outright.

title: 〜てやまない
meaning: to never cease to (wish, hope, love); to ~ from the bottom of one's heart
summary: 〜てやまない attaches to the て-form of a verb of emotion or desire and says the speaker holds that feeling ceaselessly, straight from the heart. It pairs only with a small set of feeling verbs — 願う, 祈る, 期待する, 愛する, 尊敬する — so 願ってやまない = never cease to wish, 尊敬してやまない = hold in unending respect. It is formal, literary language at home in speeches, tributes, and written prose.
pitfalls: Only a small set of emotion/desire verbs fit: 願う, 祈る, 期待する, 愛する, 尊敬する. It does not attach to ordinary action verbs (×食べてやまない).
Formal, written or ceremonial language; it sounds out of place in casual conversation.

examples.ja: 皆様の今後ますますのご活躍を願ってやみません。
examples.en: I wish you all continued and ever-greater success in the days ahead.
examples.f: ｜皆様[みなさま]の｜今後[こんご]ますますのご｜活躍[かつやく]を｜願[ねが]ってやみません。

examples.ja: 彼は生涯、故郷の海と山を愛してやまなかった。
examples.en: All his life, he never ceased to love the sea and mountains of his hometown.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜生涯[しょうがい]、｜故郷[こきょう]の｜海[うみ]と｜山[やま]を｜愛[あい]してやまなかった。

synonyms.note: てたまらない voices an emotion the speaker can hardly bear right now; てやまない is a lasting, heartfelt wish or feeling in formal prose.

related.note: てならない marks a feeling that wells up spontaneously and won't be suppressed; てやまない stresses a devoted feeling held without end.

title: 〜と相まって
meaning: combined with; coupled with; in tandem with
summary: 〜と相まって marks that one factor works together with another to produce a heightened result — 'combined with ~, coupled with ~'. A が B と相まって means A, together with B, brings something about, and the two factors reinforce each other so the outcome is notably strong. It is formal, written-style language, common in commentary and description.
pitfalls: The two factors combine to strengthen a single outcome; it is not a plain 'A and B' listing.
Formal written style; 相まって is the て-form of 相まつ and is rarely heard in casual talk.

examples.ja: 彼の才能は、たゆまぬ努力と相まって、見事な結果を生んだ。
examples.en: His talent, coupled with tireless effort, produced splendid results.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜才能[さいのう]は、たゆまぬ｜努力[どりょく]と｜相[あい]まって、｜見事[みごと]な｜結果[けっか]を｜生[う]んだ。

examples.ja: 円安が原油高と相まって、物価は急激に上昇した。
examples.en: The weak yen, combined with high crude-oil prices, drove prices up sharply.
examples.f: ｜円[えん]｜安[やす]が｜原油[げんゆ]｜高[だか]と｜相[あい]まって、｜物価[ぶっか]は｜急激[きゅうげき]に｜上昇[じょうしょう]した。

related.note: だけに gives a single reason all the more fitting for its nature; と相まって says two factors act together to amplify a result.

title: 〜とあって
meaning: because (of the special circumstance); given that
summary: 〜とあって presents a special or noteworthy circumstance as the reason a fitting consequence follows naturally — 'because it's ~, given that ~'. 連休とあって = it being a long holiday (so naturally...), 人気店とあって = as it's a popular shop. The situation is unusual or newsworthy enough that the result comes as a matter of course. It is common in reportage and in describing others' situations objectively.
pitfalls: The reason is a special or notable situation and the result follows naturally; it is not used for ordinary, everyday causes.
It describes others' or general situations objectively; avoid it for stating a personal reason about yourself.

examples.ja: 十年ぶりの優勝とあって、街全体がお祭り騒ぎになった。
examples.en: With it being their first championship in ten years, the whole town erupted into festivities.
examples.f: ｜十[じゅう]｜年[ねん]ぶりの｜優勝[ゆうしょう]とあって、｜街[まち]｜全体[ぜんたい]がお｜祭り騒[まつりさわ]ぎになった。

examples.ja: 連休最終日とあって、高速道路はどこも渋滞していた。
examples.en: Given that it was the last day of the long holiday, the expressways were jammed everywhere.
examples.f: ｜連休[れんきゅう]｜最終[さいしゅう]｜日[び]とあって、｜高速[こうそく]｜道路[どうろ]はどこも｜渋滞[じゅうたい]していた。

synonyms.note: だけあって praises a result as living up to what a quality would lead you to expect; とあって simply gives a special situation as the reason a natural result follows.
こととて offers a reason in a soft, apologetic, literary tone; とあって states a notable circumstance behind an unremarkable-to-expect result.

related.note: だけに stresses 'precisely because ~, all the more'; とあって leans on the situation being special or newsworthy.

title: 〜とあれば
meaning: if it is (a case of); if it's for the sake of ~
summary: 〜とあれば sets up a special condition and says that, given it, one will readily do something one otherwise might not — 'if it's for ~, then...'. 子供のためとあれば = if it's for the children's sake, 必要とあれば = if it should prove necessary. The main clause usually expresses willing resolve or an inevitable response to that particular circumstance. It is more formal and weighty than a plain なら.
pitfalls: The condition is a special, weighty one that justifies the (often unusual) action that follows; it is stronger and more formal than a plain なら.
The main clause states a willing response or a natural consequence, not a neutral hypothetical.

examples.ja: お客様のご要望とあれば、できる限り対応いたします。
examples.en: If it is what the customer wishes, we will do our utmost to accommodate it.
examples.f: お｜客様[きゃくさま]のご｜要望[ようぼう]とあれば、できる｜限[かぎ]り｜対応[たいおう]いたします。

examples.ja: 恩師の頼みとあれば、断るわけにはいかない。
examples.en: If it's a request from my old teacher, I can hardly refuse.
examples.f: ｜恩師[おんし]の｜頼[たの]みとあれば、｜断[ことわ]るわけにはいかない。

synonyms.note: なら is a general 'if / in that case'; とあれば adds that the condition is special enough to prompt a willing or inevitable response.

related.note: とあって treats the special situation as an actual fact behind a result; とあれば treats it as a supposed condition prompting resolve.

title: 〜といい〜といい
meaning: both ~ and ~; whether you look at ~ or ~ (in every respect)
summary: 〜といい〜といい picks out two representative aspects of something and comments that, judging by both, an overall evaluation holds — 'both ~ and ~'. 色といいデザインといい = in both color and design, 味といい香りといい = both in taste and aroma. The speaker cites two examples to back a subjective judgment about the whole, and the closing clause is that evaluation, often admiration or criticism.
pitfalls: It takes two nouns naming aspects or examples and leads to a subjective evaluation of the whole; the final clause is a judgment, not a neutral fact.
Different from 〜も〜も (plain 'both'): といい〜といい frames the two as evidence for an overall impression.

examples.ja: この旅館は、料理といい景色といい、申し分がなかった。
examples.en: This inn, in both its cuisine and its scenery, left nothing to be desired.
examples.f: この｜旅館[りょかん]は、｜料理[りょうり]といい｜景色[けしき]といい、｜申し分[もうしぶん]がなかった。

examples.ja: 態度といい言葉遣いといい、彼のふるまいには失望させられた。
examples.en: In both his attitude and his choice of words, his conduct was disappointing.
examples.f: ｜態度[たいど]といい｜言葉[ことば]｜遣[づか]いといい、｜彼[かれ]のふるまいには｜失望[しつぼう]させられた。

related.note: といわず〜といわず means 'not just these two but everywhere, without distinction'; といい〜といい lists two aspects to support an overall evaluation.

title: 〜というか〜というか
romaji: to iu ka to iu ka
meaning: or rather; I'd say ~, or maybe ~; how should I put it
summary: 〜というか〜というか lines up two ways of describing something when neither quite fits, letting the speaker grope toward the right characterization — '~, or should I say ~'. うれしいというか、ほっとしたというか = happy, or rather relieved. It conveys a mixed, hard-to-pin-down impression in a casual, thinking-aloud tone, and the two terms are often near-synonyms or two facets of one feeling.
structure: ［first phrase］＋というか＋［second phrase］＋というか
pitfalls: It signals that the speaker is searching for the right words and settling fully on neither; it is conversational in tone.
The two labels usually describe one thing from two angles, not two separate items.

examples.ja: 彼の絵は、独創的というか、奇抜というか、とにかく忘れられない。
examples.en: His paintings are original, or maybe bizarre — either way, unforgettable.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜絵[え]は、｜独創[どくそう]｜的[てき]というか、｜奇抜[きばつ]というか、とにかく｜忘[わす]れられない。

examples.ja: 合格して、うれしいというか、信じられないというか、複雑な気持ちだ。
examples.en: Passing left me happy, or rather in disbelief — a complicated feeling.
examples.f: ｜合格[ごうかく]して、うれしいというか、｜信[しん]じられないというか、｜複雑[ふくざつ]な｜気持[きも]ちだ。

synonyms.note: といおうか searches for wording in a shade more literary, reflective tone; というか〜というか is the everyday, spoken pairing.
というより corrects one label to a better one ('rather than A, B'); というか〜というか leaves both labels standing as approximations.

title: 〜というところだ・〜といったところだ
kana: というところだ・といったところだ
romaji: to iu tokoro da / to itta tokoro da
meaning: at most; roughly; about (no more than)
summary: 〜というところだ・といったところだ gives an approximate figure or assessment, usually with the sense 'at most, no more than that' — 'I'd say about ~'. せいぜい五千円といったところだ = five thousand yen at the very most, まずまずといったところだ = so-so, about middling. It attaches to nouns, numbers, or short clauses to sum up a modest estimate or a middling evaluation; といったところ is a touch more idiomatic than というところ.
structure: Noun／Number＋というところだ／といったところだ
Sentence［plain form］＋というところだ／といったところだ
pitfalls: It typically caps an estimate at a modest upper limit ('at most ~'); it is not used for large or impressive figures.
Often paired with せいぜい or まずまず to underline 'no more than this'.

examples.ja: 客の入りは、多くても三割といったところだろう。
examples.en: The turnout is thirty percent at most, I'd say.
examples.f: ｜客[きゃく]の｜入[い]りは、｜多[おお]くても｜三[さん]｜割[わり]といったところだろう。

examples.ja: 準備はまずまず、あとは本番を待つだけというところだ。
examples.en: Preparations are so-so; at this point it's just a matter of waiting for the real thing.
examples.f: ｜準備[じゅんび]はまずまず、あとは｜本番[ほんばん]を｜待[ま]つだけというところだ。

title: 〜というもの
meaning: for (a whole stretch of ~); over the entire period of
summary: When 〜というもの follows a length of time, it stresses that throughout that whole span a state continued — 'for the entire ~, all through ~'. ここ一か月というもの = all through this past month, ここ十年というもの = for these ten years now. It emphasizes how long and unbroken the period felt, usually alongside a description of an ongoing state or feeling, and it attaches to time expressions, often with ここ or この.
pitfalls: This use follows a span of time to emphasize its whole unbroken length; it differs from というものだ ('~ is really something' / the nature of ~).
It sets up a continuous state over that period, so the sentence usually describes something lasting, not a one-off event.

examples.ja: ここ一か月というもの、彼はろくに口をきいてくれない。
examples.en: For this whole past month, he has barely spoken a word to me.
examples.f: ここ｜一[いち]か｜月[げつ]というもの、｜彼[かれ]はろくに｜口[くち]をきいてくれない。

examples.ja: 事故以来、この数年というもの、彼女は不安と闘い続けてきた。
examples.en: Ever since the accident, all through these past several years, she has kept battling anxiety.
examples.f: ｜事故[じこ]｜以来[いらい]、この｜数[すう]｜年[ねん]というもの、｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜不安[ふあん]と｜闘[たたか]い｜続[つづ]けてきた。

related.note: というものだ passes an emphatic 'that's just how ~ is' judgment; というもの after a time span instead stresses the unbroken length of the period.
間 neutrally marks 'during / while'; というもの adds emotional emphasis on how long that whole stretch dragged on.

title: 〜というわけだ
meaning: that's why; so that means; it follows that
summary: 〜というわけだ presents the current statement as the natural conclusion or restatement that follows from what was just said — 'so that means ~, that's how it is'. It either draws a logical upshot (終電を逃した、というわけだ = so that's why...) or rephrases a situation more plainly, and the listener is expected to see it as the sensible conclusion of the preceding context.
pitfalls: It marks a conclusion that follows naturally from context; don't confuse it with というわけではない ('it doesn't necessarily mean ~'), which denies such a conclusion.
Different from わけがない ('there's no way'); というわけだ affirms a reasonable upshot.

examples.ja: 終電を逃したので、歩いて帰るしかなかったというわけだ。
examples.en: I missed the last train, so that's why I had no choice but to walk home.
examples.f: ｜終電[しゅうでん]を｜逃[のが]したので、｜歩[ある]いて｜帰[かえ]るしかなかったというわけだ。

examples.ja: つまり、この二つの部署が来月から一つになるというわけですね。
examples.en: In other words, these two departments will be merged into one starting next month — that's the idea, right?
examples.f: つまり、この｜二[ふた]つの｜部署[ぶしょ]が｜来月[らいげつ]から｜一[ひと]つになるというわけですね。

synonyms.note: わけだ draws the conclusion directly; というわけだ frames the whole preceding statement as the thing that leads to it, often when restating.
ということだ can report hearsay or sum up a meaning; というわけだ specifically presents a reasoned upshot of the context.

related.note: つまり cues a restatement or summary; というわけだ closes the sentence by presenting it as the logical conclusion.

title: 〜といえども
meaning: even; even though; although one may say ~
summary: 〜といえども concedes a point and then states something that holds despite it — 'even ~, even though it is ~'. プロといえども = even a professional, 子供といえども = even though they're just a child. It grants that the subject is X, yet the following clause runs against the expectation X would create. It is formal, somewhat literary, and often pairs with a sweeping generalization.
pitfalls: It concedes 'even (granting that it's) ~' and then states a contrary point; it is more formal and emphatic than ても or とはいえ.
The following clause goes against what the conceded point would lead you to expect.

examples.ja: どんなに小さなミスといえども、命に関わる場面では許されない。
examples.en: Even the smallest mistake is unforgivable in a situation where lives are at stake.
examples.f: どんなに｜小[ちい]さなミスといえども、｜命[いのち]に｜関[かか]わる｜場面[ばめん]では｜許[ゆる]されない。

examples.ja: いかに大企業といえども、時代の変化に対応できなければ生き残れない。
examples.en: Even a large corporation, however big, cannot survive if it fails to adapt to the changing times.
examples.f: いかに｜大[だい]｜企業[きぎょう]といえども、｜時代[じだい]の｜変化[へんか]に｜対応[たいおう]できなければ｜生き残[いきのこ]れない。

synonyms.note: ても is the everyday 'even if / even though'; といえども says the same with a formal, literary, concessive weight.

related.note: ものの concedes an established fact then notes it fell short of expectation; といえども concedes a category ('even a ~') before a contrary rule.
ながらも marks 'although, despite ~' between two facts of one subject; といえども concedes a generalized case.

title: 〜と言えなくもない
meaning: one could even say that; it's not impossible to say ~
summary: 〜と言えなくもない is a hedged, doubly-negative way of granting a point — 'you can't say it isn't ~, so in a sense it is'. It offers cautious, partial agreement: 成功と言えなくもない = you could, in a way, call it a success. The speaker admits the description has some validity while staying noncommittal, so it softens an assertion and usually implies reservations.
pitfalls: The double negative makes it a weak, reserved 'you could sort of say ~', not a confident assertion.
It concedes partial truth while leaving room for doubt; the speaker is not fully committing.

examples.ja: 見方によっては、今回の判断は英断だったと言えなくもない。
examples.en: Depending on how you look at it, one could even say this decision was a bold and wise call.
examples.f: ｜見方[みかた]によっては、｜今回[こんかい]の｜判断[はんだん]は｜英断[えいだん]だったと｜言[い]えなくもない。

examples.ja: 彼の頑固さは、信念の強さの表れと言えなくもない。
examples.en: You could, in a way, say his stubbornness is a sign of the strength of his convictions.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜頑固[がんこ]さは、｜信念[しんねん]の｜強[つよ]さの｜表[あらわ]れと｜言[い]えなくもない。

synonyms.note: ないでもない ('it's not that one doesn't ~') is the same reserved double negative applied to actions or feelings; と言えなくもない applies it to a description.

title: 〜といおうか
meaning: how should I put it; or perhaps I should say ~
summary: 〜といおうか introduces a description offered tentatively as the speaker reaches for the fitting words — 'what should I call it, or perhaps ~'. It often comes in pairs (〜といおうか〜といおうか) or just before a rephrasing, marking that the chosen word is only approximate. It is a shade more literary and reflective than 〜というか, and conveys genuine hesitation over how to characterize something.
pitfalls: It flags that the word chosen is only an approximation the speaker is reaching for; it is more formal and literary than というか.
It comments on how to describe something, not on whether the thing is true.

examples.ja: その光景は、荘厳といおうか、神秘的といおうか、言葉にしがたいものだった。
examples.en: The sight was solemn, or perhaps I should say mystical — something hard to put into words.
examples.f: その｜光景[こうけい]は、｜荘厳[そうごん]といおうか、｜神秘[しんぴ]｜的[てき]といおうか、｜言葉[ことば]にしがたいものだった。

examples.ja: 彼の決断は、無謀といおうか、それとも勇敢だったのか、今も判断がつかない。
examples.en: His decision was reckless, or should I say brave — even now I can't decide which.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜決断[けつだん]は、｜無謀[むぼう]といおうか、それとも｜勇敢[ゆうかん]だったのか、｜今[いま]も｜判断[はんだん]がつかない。

synonyms.note: というか〜というか does the same word-searching in an everyday, conversational tone; といおうか is more literary and reflective.

title: 〜といったらない・〜ったらない
kana: といったらない・ったらない
meaning: extremely; indescribably; ~ beyond words
summary: 〜といったらない (casual 〜ったらない) marks a degree so extreme that words fail — 'you can't describe how ~ it is'. うれしいといったらない = indescribably happy, 悔しいったらない = frustrated beyond words. It attaches mainly to adjectives (and some nouns) naming a strong impression and pushes it to the utmost. It is emotive and colloquial, most often about negative feelings but usable for positive extremes too.
pitfalls: It pushes a quality to its extreme ('~ beyond description'), not a middling degree.
ったらない is the more casual, spoken contraction; といったらない is the fuller form.

examples.ja: 一日じゅう並んで、結局買えなかったのだから、情けないといったらない。
examples.en: After lining up all day and still not getting one, it was pathetic beyond words.
examples.f: ｜一[いち]｜日[にち]じゅう｜並[なら]んで、｜結局[けっきょく]｜買[か]えなかったのだから、｜情[なさ]けないといったらない。

examples.ja: 静まり返った夜の山道の心細さといったらなかった。
examples.en: The loneliness of that hushed mountain path at night was beyond describing.
examples.f: ｜静まり返[しずまりかえ]った｜夜[よる]の｜山道[さんどう]の｜心細[こころぼそ]さといったらなかった。

synonyms.note: この上ない states 'the utmost, none higher' rather formally; といったらない voices the same extremity with emotive, colloquial force.
限りだ intensifies an emotion adjective ('extremely ~'); といったらない adds the nuance that the degree defies description.

title: 〜といわず〜といわず
meaning: not just ~ or ~; both ~ and ~ and everywhere in between
summary: 〜といわず〜といわず names two representative parts and says the statement applies not only to them but comprehensively, without distinction — 'not just ~ or ~ but all over'. 手といわず顔といわず = hands, face, everywhere, 昼といわず夜といわず = day and night alike. The two examples are chosen to imply 'and everything or everywhere else too', stressing that no part is exempt.
pitfalls: The two nouns are just examples standing for 'and everywhere or everything else too'; it does not mean only those two.
Different from といい〜といい, which lists two aspects to support an evaluation; といわず stresses 'without distinction, all of it'.

examples.ja: 子供たちは、手といわず服といわず、泥だらけになって帰ってきた。
examples.en: The children came home caked in mud — hands, clothes, everywhere.
examples.f: ｜子供[こども]たちは、｜手[て]といわず｜服[ふく]といわず、｜泥[どろ]だらけになって｜帰[かえ]ってきた。

examples.ja: 平日といわず休日といわず、その店の前には行列ができていた。
examples.en: Weekday or weekend, no matter which, there was always a line in front of that shop.
examples.f: ｜平日[へいじつ]といわず｜休日[きゅうじつ]といわず、その｜店[みせ]の｜前[まえ]には｜行列[ぎょうれつ]ができていた。

synonyms.note: なり〜なり offers 'either ~ or ~, whichever you pick'; といわず〜といわず instead sweeps in everything without exception.

related.note: といい〜といい cites two aspects as evidence for an overall judgment; といわず〜といわず means 'all of it, everywhere, without distinction'.

title: どうにか
meaning: somehow (or other); to (barely) manage to
summary: どうにか means getting something done by some means or other, often only just barely — 'somehow, one way or another'. どうにか間に合った = somehow made it in time, どうにかしてほしい = I want it dealt with somehow. It can express relief at barely succeeding or a wish for some solution to a problem. It is close to なんとか in meaning and everyday register.
pitfalls: It usually implies just barely pulling something off, or wishing for some way out — not doing it easily.
どうにか (getting by somehow) is the positive counterpart to どうにも〜ない (can't manage at all, no matter what).

examples.ja: 締め切りには、どうにか間に合わせることができた。
examples.en: I somehow managed to make the deadline in time.
examples.f: ｜締め切[しめき]りには、どうにか｜間に合[まにあ]わせることができた。

examples.ja: 苦しい資金繰りを、どうにかして立て直さなければならない。
examples.en: We have to somehow get our strained cash flow back on track.
examples.f: ｜苦[くる]しい｜資金繰[しきんぐ]りを、どうにかして｜立て直[たてなお]さなければならない。

antonyms.note: どうにも〜ない is the flip side: 'can't manage it at all, no matter what', where どうにか is 'managed it somehow'.

related.note: どうしても means 'by all means / no matter what' as determination or, with a negative, sheer impossibility; どうにか is 'somehow, barely'.

title: どうにも〜ない
meaning: can't ~ no matter what; there's nothing to be done
summary: どうにも paired with a negative says that, try as one might, nothing can be done about something — 'no way to ~, can't ~ however hard I try'. どうにもならない = nothing can be done, どうにも我慢できない = simply can't stand it. It expresses helplessness or an insurmountable limit, and どうにもならない is a set phrase for a hopeless situation.
pitfalls: どうにも requires a negative predicate; it means 'in no way / no matter what, (can)not ~'.
Contrast with plain どうにか (managing somehow); どうにも〜ない is the helpless, cannot-be-helped side.

examples.ja: こうなってしまっては、私の力ではどうにもならない。
examples.en: Now that it has come to this, there is nothing I can do about it with my own power.
examples.f: こうなってしまっては、｜私[わたし]の｜力[ちから]ではどうにもならない。

examples.ja: 彼のあの態度だけは、どうにも我慢できなかった。
examples.en: That attitude of his was the one thing I simply could not put up with.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]のあの｜態度[たいど]だけは、どうにも｜我慢[がまん]できなかった。

antonyms.note: どうにか is 'somehow manage to ~'; どうにも〜ない is 'can't ~ at all, no matter what'.

related.note: どうしても〜ない also means 'can't ~ however hard I try'; どうにも〜ない leans more on the situation being beyond remedy.

title: 〜ときたら
meaning: when it comes to ~ (with exasperation); as for ~
summary: 〜ときたら singles out a topic — usually a person or thing close to the speaker — and leads into a complaint or exasperated remark about it. うちの息子ときたら = as for my son (honestly...), この天気ときたら = this weather, of all things. It sets up the topic with a fed-up, critical attitude, so the following comment is typically negative. It is colloquial and emotive.
pitfalls: The comment that follows is almost always a complaint or criticism; it carries an exasperated tone, not a neutral 'as for'.
The topic is usually someone or something familiar to the speaker; don't use it for distant, respectful reference.

examples.ja: うちの課長ときたら、自分のミスを絶対に認めようとしない。
examples.en: My section chief, honestly — he will never once admit his own mistakes.
examples.f: うちの｜課長[かちょう]ときたら、｜自分[じぶん]のミスを｜絶対[ぜったい]に｜認[みと]めようとしない。

examples.ja: 最近の若い者ときたら、挨拶の一つもまともにできないのか。
examples.en: The young folks these days — can't they even manage a proper greeting?
examples.f: ｜最近[さいきん]の｜若[わか]い｜者[もの]ときたら、｜挨拶[あいさつ]の｜一[ひと]つもまともにできないのか。

synonyms.note: とは reacts with surprise or evaluation to a fact ('to think that ~'); ときたら fixes a familiar topic and grumbles about it.

related.note: ときている piles on an extra clinching reason; ときたら opens a topic to complain about.

title: 〜ときている
meaning: and on top of that; what's more, it's ~ (so naturally...)
summary: 〜ときている adds an emphatic supporting fact, usually one more reason piling onto a situation — 'and what's more it's ~, on top of that ~'. The added fact is presented as a given that clinches the point, often with an air of 'no wonder'. It typically comes after a run of listed merits or faults and sums up why some result is only to be expected. It is colloquial.
pitfalls: It piles on an extra, clinching reason ('and on top of that ~'), reinforcing the conclusion; it is not a neutral 'and'.
Colloquial and emphatic; the added point usually explains why a result is only to be expected.

examples.ja: あの店は味もいいし、値段も手ごろ、おまけに店員が親切ときているから、いつも満席だ。
examples.en: That place has good food and reasonable prices, and on top of that the staff are friendly, so it's always packed.
examples.f: あの｜店[みせ]は｜味[あじ]もいいし、｜値段[ねだん]も｜手[て]ごろ、おまけに｜店員[てんいん]が｜親切[しんせつ]ときているから、いつも｜満席[まんせき]だ。

examples.ja: 彼は仕事はできる、人柄もいい、おまけに聞き上手ときているのだから、慕われるのも当然だ。
examples.en: He's good at his job, likeable, and a good listener on top of it all — no wonder people look up to him.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜仕事[しごと]はできる、｜人柄[ひとがら]もいい、おまけに｜聞き上手[ききじょうず]ときているのだから、｜慕[した]われるのも｜当然[とうぜん]だ。

related.note: ときたら opens a familiar topic for complaint; ときている adds a final reinforcing reason to a build-up.
だけに gives one reason 'all the more fitting'; ときている tacks on an extra reason that clinches an expected result.

title: 〜ところを
meaning: although (it is a time/situation when ~); even though you are ~
summary: 〜ところを marks a situation or moment and then says that, despite it, something happens — most often in set courtesy phrases thanking or apologizing for imposing at an inconvenient time. お忙しいところを = though you are busy, お休みのところを = though you were resting. It concedes the other person's circumstances before the main action. It can also mark the very moment an action is caught or interrupted (勉強しているところを見られた).
pitfalls: In polite formulas it concedes the listener's (often inconvenient) circumstances: お忙しいところを、恐れ入ります.
It also marks the moment an ongoing action is caught or interrupted, with を as the object of that catching (見つかる, 見られる).

examples.ja: お忙しいところをわざわざお越しいただき、誠にありがとうございます。
examples.en: Thank you so very much for taking the trouble to come all this way despite how busy you are.
examples.f: お｜忙[いそが]しいところをわざわざお｜越[こ]しいただき、｜誠[まこと]にありがとうございます。

examples.ja: サボっているところを、運悪く上司に見つかってしまった。
examples.en: As luck would have it, I got caught slacking off by my boss.
examples.f: サボっているところを、｜運[うん]｜悪[わる]く｜上司[じょうし]に｜見[み]つかってしまった。

related.note: ところに marks 'right at the moment when ~' as the timing of an arrival or event; ところを concedes a situation ('though it is ~') or marks the object caught in the act.
ものの is a plain 'although ~'; ところを specifically concedes the listener's circumstances in courtesy phrases or frames the moment of an interruption.

title: 〜とされる
meaning: is regarded as; is held to be; is said to be
summary: 〜とされる presents something as what is generally held, established, or officially regarded to be the case — 'is considered ~, is deemed ~'. 健康に良いとされる = is held to be good for one's health, 最古とされる = regarded as the oldest. The judgment is attributed to society, authorities, or general consensus rather than the speaker's own view. It is common in explanatory, academic, and news writing; とされている stresses the ongoing established state.
pitfalls: The view is attributed to general consensus, rules, or authority — not offered as the speaker's own fresh opinion.
とされる/とされている reports an established judgment; と言われる leans more toward general hearsay ('people say').

examples.ja: この神社は、国内で最も古い木造建築の一つとされている。
examples.en: This shrine is regarded as one of the oldest wooden structures in the country.
examples.f: この｜神社[じんじゃ]は、｜国内[こくない]で｜最[もっと]も｜古[ふる]い｜木造[もくぞう]｜建築[けんちく]の｜一[ひと]つとされている。

examples.ja: 昔から、この植物には熱を下げる効果があるとされてきた。
examples.en: This plant has long been held to have fever-reducing effects.
examples.f: ｜昔[むかし]から、この｜植物[しょくぶつ]には｜熱[ねつ]を｜下[さ]げる｜効果[こうか]があるとされてきた。

synonyms.note: そうだ (hearsay) reports 'I hear that ~' from a specific source; とされる presents an established, widely-held judgment.

related.note: The passive れる/られる underlies とされる; on its own it marks who is affected, while とされる specifically frames a view as generally accepted.

title: 〜としたことが
meaning: of all people, ~ (an out-of-character blunder)
summary: 〜としたことが expresses dismay that a normally reliable person did something so unlike them. It attaches to a person (very often 私), and the clause that follows admits an uncharacteristic mistake or lapse: 私としたことが、うっかりしていた = of all people, I was being careless. The tone is self-reproach or gentle astonishment that someone who should have known better slipped up.
structure: Noun［person, usually 私］＋としたことが
pitfalls: The following clause admits an out-of-character mistake, not a routine one; the point is that this person of all people slipped up.
Most natural about oneself with 私; the が marks the subject, and the blunder is stated in the clause that follows.

examples.ja: 私としたことが、初歩的なミスを見逃してしまった。
examples.en: I of all people overlooked such an elementary mistake.
examples.f: ｜私[わたし]としたことが、｜初歩[しょほ]｜的[てき]なミスを｜見逃[みのが]してしまった。

examples.ja: ベテランの彼としたことが、こんな単純な問題でつまずくとは。
examples.en: For a veteran like him to trip over such a simple problem — how unlike him.
examples.f: ベテランの｜彼[かれ]としたことが、こんな｜単純[たんじゅん]な｜問題[もんだい]でつまずくとは。

synonyms.note: ともあろうものが criticizes someone by their lofty role or title; としたことが centers on behavior that is out of character, often one's own.

related.note: とは voices bare surprise that a fact is even true; としたことが adds that the person responsible should have known better.

title: とっさに
meaning: instantly; reflexively; on the spur of the moment
summary: とっさに describes an instinctive reaction made in a split second, before there is time to think — typically in response to something sudden. とっさに身をかわす = dodge reflexively, とっさに手が出る = one's hand shoots out on reflex. The emphasis is that the action was unplanned and immediate. The noun form とっさの also appears, as in とっさの判断 (a split-second decision).
pitfalls: This is an instinctive, unplanned reaction to something sudden, not merely an action you chose to do quickly.
Often paired with emergencies or surprises; the noun-modifying form is とっさの＋Noun (とっさの判断).

examples.ja: 車が飛び出してきて、とっさにブレーキを踏んだ。
examples.en: A car darted out, and I hit the brakes on reflex.
examples.f: ｜車[くるま]が｜飛び出[とびだ]してきて、とっさにブレーキを｜踏[ふ]んだ。

examples.ja: 急に質問されて、とっさにはうまい返事が思いつかなかった。
examples.en: Asked out of the blue, I couldn't come up with a good reply on the spur of the moment.
examples.f: ｜急[きゅう]に｜質問[しつもん]されて、とっさにはうまい｜返事[へんじ]が｜思[おも]いつかなかった。

related.note: つい is doing something you shouldn't without thinking (often a habit); とっさに is reacting instantly to something sudden.

title: 〜とて
meaning: even ~; even if ~ (literary)
summary: 〜とて is a literary particle with two related senses. After a noun it means 'even ~', singling out a case you might think exempt: 子供とて許されない = even a child is not excused. After a verb it means 'even if / even though', usually with a futile or negative outcome: 悔やんだとて、もう遅い = even if you regret it, it's too late now. It belongs to formal or written Japanese; in speech でも or ても does the same work.
pitfalls: Literary; in everyday speech use でも or ても instead.
In the 'even if' sense the result is typically negative or futile: 〜とて〜ない.

examples.ja: プロとて、常に完璧でいられるわけではない。
examples.en: Even a professional cannot always stay flawless.
examples.f: プロとて、｜常[つね]に｜完璧[かんぺき]でいられるわけではない。

examples.ja: 今さら悔やんだとて、過ぎた時間は戻らない。
examples.en: Even if you regret it now, the time that has passed will not come back.
examples.f: ｜今[いま]さら｜悔[く]やんだとて、｜過[す]ぎた｜時間[じかん]は｜戻[もど]らない。

synonyms.note: ても is the everyday 'even if / even though'; とて is its literary, formal-writing equivalent.

related.note: であれ・であろうと concedes across alternatives ('whatever it be'); とて concedes a single case as 'even ~ / even if ~'.
たって is the casual spoken 'even if'; とて sits at the opposite, literary end of the register scale.

title: 〜となると・〜となれば
meaning: when it comes to ~; if it comes to the point that ~
