summary: 〜となると・〜となれば marks that once a matter becomes a real or serious prospect, a fitting reaction or consequence follows — 'when it actually comes to ~'. 留学するとなると、費用がかかる = if it comes to studying abroad, it costs money. It attaches to a noun, a plain-form verb, or a whole clause. The nuance is that raising the matter to a concrete stage changes what is required or how one feels about it.
structure: Verb［plain form］＋となると／となれば
pitfalls: Signals that when a matter becomes a genuine prospect, a particular consequence naturally follows.
Distinguish from ともなると, which adds an 'even / as much as' emphasis on a high level or rank.

examples.ja: いざ本番となると、緊張で手が震えてしまう。
examples.en: When it actually comes to the real performance, my hands tremble with nerves.
examples.f: いざ｜本番[ほんばん]となると、｜緊張[きんちょう]で｜手[て]が｜震[ふる]えてしまう。

examples.ja: 家を買うとなれば、相当な貯金が必要だ。
examples.en: If it comes to buying a house, you'll need considerable savings.
examples.f: ｜家[いえ]を｜買[か]うとなれば、｜相当[そうとう]な｜貯金[ちょきん]が｜必要[ひつよう]だ。

synonyms.note: ともなると・にもなると adds that the level or rank reached is notably high; となると is the neutral 'when it comes to'.

related.note: と言えば raises a topic by association ('speaking of ~'); となると focuses on the consequences of a matter becoming real.

title: 〜との
meaning: ~ that; to the effect that (quote modifying a noun)
summary: 〜との links a quoted statement, report, or thought to a following noun of communication — 連絡・報告・知らせ・指示・話・うわさ. It is the noun-modifying counterpart of と／という: 延期になったとの連絡 = word that it had been postponed. Common in news, business, and other formal writing. It packs a whole reported clause into a modifier of the noun that names how the information came.
pitfalls: Used before nouns of communication or thought (連絡, 指示, うわさ...) to attach a reported clause; the formal counterpart of という in that position.
Do not confuse this quotative との with the plain possessive/comitative の.

examples.ja: 社長は来月退任するとの噂が広まっている。
examples.en: A rumor that the president will step down next month is spreading.
examples.f: ｜社長[しゃちょう]は｜来月[らいげつ]｜退任[たいにん]するとの｜噂[うわさ]が｜広[ひろ]まっている。

examples.ja: 値上げはやむを得ないとの説明があった。
examples.en: There was an explanation to the effect that the price increase was unavoidable.
examples.f: ｜値上[ねあ]げはやむを｜得[え]ないとの｜説明[せつめい]があった。

synonyms.note: という is the general attributive quote; との is used specifically before nouns of communication in formal reports.

related.note: ということだ reports hearsay as a full predicate ('it is said that'); との folds the same kind of report into a noun modifier.

title: 〜とは
meaning: to think that ~!; the very idea that ~
summary: In its emotive use, 〜とは reacts with surprise, shock, admiration, or dismay to a fact — 'to think that ~!'. まさか彼が犯人だったとは = to think he was the culprit. The sentence often trails off after とは, leaving the reaction (驚いた, 情けない...) unspoken. It is a little more formal or written than the colloquial なんて. Separately, とは also serves as a defining marker ('X とは Y' = X means Y).
pitfalls: In the emotive use the sentence often breaks off after とは (…とは！／…とは思わなかった), the reaction left unsaid.
Keep this surprise とは separate from the defining とは, which explains what a term means ('X means Y').

examples.ja: こんな所で君に会うとは、思ってもみなかった。
examples.en: To run into you in a place like this — I never even imagined it.
examples.f: こんな｜所[ところ]で｜君[きみ]に｜会[あ]うとは、｜思[おも]ってもみなかった。

examples.ja: あの真面目な彼が会社を辞めるとは、驚きだ。
examples.en: For that earnest fellow to quit the company — what a surprise.
examples.f: あの｜真面目[まじめ]な｜彼[かれ]が｜会社[かいしゃ]を｜辞[や]めるとは、｜驚[おどろ]きだ。

synonyms.note: なんて is the colloquial 'to think that ~!'; とは carries a slightly more formal, written tone.

related.note: ことか exclaims over a degree ('how very ~!'); とは reacts with surprise that a fact is even the case.

title: とは言うものの
meaning: having said that; that said; nevertheless
summary: とはいうものの concedes what was just stated and then presents a reality that runs against the expectation it creates — 'having said that, ...'. 春とはいうものの、まだ寒い = it may be spring, but it's still cold. It can join clauses within a sentence or open a new one after a full stop. The contrast clause describes an actual situation, not a hypothetical one.
pitfalls: Concedes the previous statement, then states a fact that cuts against the expectation it raises.
The contrasting clause is a real situation, not a supposition.

examples.ja: ダイエット中だとはいうものの、甘い物の誘惑にはなかなか勝てない。
examples.en: I'm supposedly on a diet, but I can hardly resist the lure of sweets.
examples.f: ダイエット｜中[ちゅう]だとはいうものの、｜甘[あま]い｜物[もの]の｜誘惑[ゆうわく]にはなかなか｜勝[か]てない。

examples.ja: 給料は上がった。とはいうものの、物価も上がったので生活は楽にならない。
examples.en: My salary went up. That said, prices rose too, so life hasn't gotten any easier.
examples.f: ｜給料[きゅうりょう]は｜上[あ]がった。とはいうものの、｜物価[ぶっか]も｜上[あ]がったので｜生活[せいかつ]は｜楽[らく]にならない。

synonyms.note: とはいえ carries the same 'that said' meaning in a more compact, formal shape.
ものの joins a concession and its counter within one sentence ('although'); とはいうものの more often stands as its own connective clause.

related.note: と言っても downplays or qualifies a preceding claim; とはいうものの fully concedes it, then contrasts.

title: 〜とはいえ
meaning: that said; even so; nonetheless
summary: 〜とはいえ concedes a point and then states something that runs contrary to what that point would lead you to expect — 'even though ~, still ...'. It is more formal and written than とはいうものの, and can either join clauses or open a sentence as 'Nonetheless, ...'. 便利とはいえ、頼りすぎは良くない = convenient though it is, relying on it too much is bad. The main clause qualifies or resists the conceded premise.
pitfalls: More formal and written than とはいうものの; fine at the head of a sentence ('Nonetheless, ...').
The main clause presents something contrary to what the conceded part would suggest.

examples.ja: 規則とはいえ、これほど厳しいと従業員の不満も大きい。
examples.en: Rules or not, when they're this strict the employees' discontent runs high.
examples.f: ｜規則[きそく]とはいえ、これほど｜厳[きび]しいと｜従業[じゅうぎょう]｜員[いん]の｜不満[ふまん]も｜大[おお]きい。

examples.ja: 内定をもらった。とはいえ、入社までにはまだ準備すべきことが多い。
examples.en: I got a job offer. Even so, there's still a lot to prepare before I start.
examples.f: ｜内定[ないてい]をもらった。とはいえ、｜入社[にゅうしゃ]までにはまだ｜準備[じゅんび]すべきことが｜多[おお]い。

synonyms.note: とはいうものの is nearly identical in meaning, slightly softer and more conversational.

related.note: ものの concedes within a single sentence ('although'); とはいえ can stand alone as a sentence-opening 'nonetheless'.
ながらも concedes about one subject's own action or state ('even while ~ing'); とはいえ concedes a whole statement.

title: 〜とは打って変わって
meaning: in total contrast to ~; utterly unlike ~
summary: 打って変わる means 'to change completely', so 〜とは打って変わって marks a striking, wholesale reversal from a previous state or from the thing named — 'in total contrast to ~'. 昨日とは打って変わって、今日は晴天だ = in complete contrast to yesterday, today is clear. It stresses that the change is dramatic and often surprising, usually within the same subject over time rather than a gradual shift.
structure: Noun［prior state, e.g. 昨日／普段］＋とは打って変わって
pitfalls: Highlights a complete, often surprising reversal from a prior state, not a gradual change.
Typically contrasts the same subject before and after, rather than two unrelated things.

examples.ja: 午前中の混雑とは打って変わって、午後の店内は閑散としていた。
examples.en: In total contrast to the morning crowds, the shop was deserted in the afternoon.
examples.f: ｜午前[ごぜん]｜中[ちゅう]の｜混雑[こんざつ]とは｜打[う]って｜変[か]わって、｜午後[ごご]の｜店内[てんない]は｜閑散[かんさん]としていた。

examples.ja: 彼女は面接では、普段とは打って変わって、はきはきと話した。
examples.en: In the interview she spoke crisply, utterly unlike her usual self.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜面接[めんせつ]では、｜普段[ふだん]とは｜打[う]って｜変[か]わって、はきはきと｜話[はな]した。

related.note: に引き換え contrasts two different things, often with a judgmental edge; とは打って変わって stresses one subject's dramatic change from a former state.
に反して means 'contrary to (an expectation or standard)'; とは打って変わって points to a complete change from how things were before.

title: 〜とばかりに
meaning: as if to say ~; with a manner that all but says ~
summary: 〜とばかりに attaches a quoted thought to someone's behavior: they don't actually speak the words, but their manner or action conveys them — 'as if to say ~'. 帰れとばかりに、彼はドアを指さした = he pointed at the door as if to say 'get out'. It often accompanies a vivid gesture or a decisive move, and captures the attitude the person is broadcasting without words.
pitfalls: The quoted words are not actually spoken — they render the attitude the person's manner conveys.
Do not confuse it with とばかり思っていた ('I was firmly convinced that ~'), which is unrelated.

examples.ja: 待ってましたとばかりに、子供たちは公園へ駆け出した。
examples.en: As if they'd been waiting for just this, the children dashed off to the park.
examples.f: ｜待[ま]ってましたとばかりに、｜子供[こども]たちは｜公園[こうえん]へ｜駆け出[かけだ]した。

examples.ja: 彼は早く帰れとばかりに、時計をちらちら見ていた。
examples.en: He kept glancing at the clock as if to say I should hurry home.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜早[はや]く｜帰[かえ]れとばかりに、｜時計[とけい]をちらちら｜見[み]ていた。

title: 〜とは比べものにならない
kana: とはくらべものにならない
meaning: no comparison with ~; in a different league from ~
summary: 〜とは比べものにならない states that the gap between two things is so wide they cannot be measured on the same scale — 'no comparison with ~'. 昔のとは比べものにならないほど速い = incomparably faster than the old one. Context tells you which side comes out ahead. It often appears as 〜とは比べものにならないほど＋adjective to stress just how far apart they are.
structure: Noun＋とは比べものにならない
pitfalls: Says the gap is too great to compare, not merely that one is somewhat more than the other.
Context, not the phrase itself, tells you which side is superior; often 〜ほど＋adjective follows.

examples.ja: 今の医療技術は、百年前とは比べものにならないほど進歩している。
examples.en: Today's medical technology has advanced beyond any comparison with a century ago.
examples.f: ｜今[いま]の｜医療[いりょう]｜技術[ぎじゅつ]は、｜百[ひゃく]｜年[ねん]｜前[まえ]とは｜比[くら]べものにならないほど｜進歩[しんぽ]している。

examples.ja: このカメラの画質は、スマホのものとは比べものにならない。
examples.en: This camera's image quality is in a different league from a phone's.
examples.f: このカメラの｜画質[がしつ]は、スマホのものとは｜比[くら]べものにならない。

related.note: に比べて makes a plain 'compared with ~'; とは比べものにならない says the two are too far apart to compare at all.
には及ばない says one side clearly falls short of the other; 比べものにならない stresses that the gap itself is beyond comparison.

title: 〜とみると
meaning: upon seeing / judging that ~ (one then acts)
summary: 〜とみると marks that, on perceiving or judging a situation, someone promptly acts in response — 'seeing that ~, he ...'. 客が来ないとみると、店を閉めた = judging that no customers were coming, he closed the shop. The subject sizes up the situation and reacts to it. It is a touch calmer than と見るや, which stresses acting at the very instant of perceiving.
pitfalls: The subject perceives or judges a situation and then acts on that assessment.
Less abrupt than と見るや, which emphasizes acting the very moment of perceiving.

examples.ja: 彼は先生がいないとみると、すぐにおしゃべりを始めた。
examples.en: The moment he saw the teacher was away, he started chatting.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜先生[せんせい]がいないとみると、すぐにおしゃべりを｜始[はじ]めた。

examples.ja: 形勢が不利とみると、相手はあっさり主張を引っ込めた。
examples.en: Judging the situation unfavorable, the other side readily withdrew its claim.
examples.f: ｜形勢[けいせい]が｜不利[ふり]とみると、｜相手[あいて]はあっさり｜主張[しゅちょう]を｜引っ込[ひっこ]めた。

synonyms.note: と見るや carries the same core idea but is more literary and stresses the immediacy of the reaction.

related.note: や否や means 'the instant ~ happened'; とみると adds that the subject judged a situation and then acted on it.

title: 〜と見るや
meaning: the instant one saw / judged that ~
summary: 〜と見るや is a literary, dramatic version of とみると: the very instant someone perceives or judges a situation, they immediately act — 'the moment he saw ~, he ...'. 隙ありと見るや、猫は飛びかかった = the instant it spotted an opening, the cat pounced. The や here marks that the action came without a beat's delay, not a question. It suits vivid narration.
pitfalls: Literary and emphatic; stresses that the action followed the very instant of perceiving.
The や marks immediacy here, not an interrogative.

examples.ja: 警官の姿を見るや、男はあわてて逃げ出した。
examples.en: The instant he caught sight of the police officer, the man fled in a panic.
examples.f: ｜警官[けいかん]の｜姿[すがた]を｜見[み]るや、｜男[おとこ]はあわてて｜逃げ出[にげだ]した。

examples.ja: チャンスと見るや、彼はすかさず質問を投げかけた。
examples.en: The moment he judged it a chance, he fired off a question without hesitation.
examples.f: チャンスと｜見[み]るや、｜彼[かれ]はすかさず｜質問[しつもん]を｜投[な]げかけた。

synonyms.note: とみると shares the same core sense but is calmer and less dramatic than と見るや.
や否や also means 'the instant ~'; と見るや specifically pivots on the subject seeing or judging something first.

related.note: が早いか marks two actions almost overlapping in time; と見るや foregrounds the act of perceiving that triggers the response.
なり marks a second action right on the heels of the first; と見るや adds that a judgment of the situation set it off.

title: 〜とも〜とも
meaning: cannot say whether ~ or ~ (neither is affirmed)
summary: 〜とも〜とも pairs two opposite possibilities and then denies committing to either, closing with a negative — 言えない, 言わない, つかない, 分からない. 良いとも悪いとも言えない = I can't say whether it's good or bad. The two slots hold contrary options (yes/no, good/bad), and the point is that neither one is settled on.
pitfalls: Nearly always closes with a negative (言えない・つかない・分からない): neither alternative is affirmed.
The two slots are usually opposite possibilities, not just any two items.

examples.ja: 彼は行くとも行かないとも言わず、ただ黙っていた。
examples.en: He said neither that he would go nor that he wouldn't, and just stayed silent.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜行[い]くとも｜行[い]かないとも｜言[い]わず、ただ｜黙[だま]っていた。

examples.ja: 結果が良いとも悪いとも判断がつかない状態が続いている。
examples.en: A state in which you can call the outcome neither good nor bad keeps dragging on.
examples.f: ｜結果[けっか]が｜良[よ]いとも｜悪[わる]いとも｜判断[はんだん]がつかない｜状態[じょうたい]が｜続[つづ]いている。

related.note: か〜か lists alternatives, one of which holds; とも〜とも＋negative refuses to commit to either.

title: 〜ともあろうものが
meaning: of all people; someone who is supposed to be ~
summary: 〜ともあろうものが attaches to a person of standing or a respected role and voices criticism or disbelief that someone in that position acted unworthily — 'for someone who is supposed to be ~ to do that'. 教師ともあろう者が = a person who is supposedly a teacher, of all people. The clause that follows expresses disappointment that their reputation should have prevented the behavior. 者 may also appear as 者が or the ending as ものだ.
structure: Noun［person of status／role］＋ともあろうものが
pitfalls: Reserved for someone whose position or reputation should have kept them from the behavior.
The following clause voices criticism or disbelief, not neutral description.

examples.ja: 大臣ともあろうものが、そのような失言をするとは情けない。
examples.en: For someone who is supposed to be a cabinet minister to make such a gaffe is pathetic.
examples.f: ｜大臣[だいじん]ともあろうものが、そのような｜失言[しつげん]をするとは｜情[なさ]けない。

examples.ja: 一流企業ともあろうものが、こんなずさんな対応をするとは驚きだ。
examples.en: That a top-tier company of all things would respond so sloppily is astonishing.
examples.f: ｜一流[いちりゅう]｜企業[きぎょう]ともあろうものが、こんなずさんな｜対応[たいおう]をするとは｜驚[おどろ]きだ。

synonyms.note: としたことが notes an out-of-character blunder, often one's own; ともあろうものが judges someone by their lofty role.

related.note: まじき labels conduct as unbefitting a role (〜にあるまじき); ともあろうものが names the person and expresses the disbelief directly.
とは voices the bare surprise; ともあろうものが frames that surprise around a person's status.

title: ともすれば
meaning: apt to; prone to; liable to
summary: ともすれば sets up a tendency to slip easily into a state — usually an undesirable one — under the right conditions. It pairs naturally with 〜がち, 〜やすい, or 〜かねない: ともすれば油断しがちだ = one is apt to grow careless. The variant ともすると has the same meaning. It flags a pull toward a certain (often negative) outcome, not a one-time event.
structure: ともすれば＋Sentence（〜がち／〜やすい／〜かねない）
pitfalls: Describes a tendency to fall into an often negative state, not a single occurrence.
Frequently paired with 〜がち, 〜やすい, or 〜かねない; the variant ともすると is equivalent.

examples.ja: 気を抜くと、ともすれば食生活が乱れがちになる。
examples.en: Let your guard down and your eating habits are apt to fall into disarray.
examples.f: ｜気[き]を｜抜[ぬ]くと、ともすれば｜食生活[しょくせいかつ]が｜乱[みだ]れがちになる。

examples.ja: 真面目な人ほど、ともすれば自分を追い詰めてしまう。
examples.en: The more earnest a person is, the more prone they are to backing themselves into a corner.
examples.f: ｜真面目[まじめ]な｜人[ひと]ほど、ともすれば｜自分[じぶん]を｜追い詰[おいつ]めてしまう。

synonyms.note: がち is the suffix 'tends to ~' on a verb or noun; ともすれば is the adverb that sets up such a tendency, often with がち itself.
嫌いがある states that something has a (negative) tendency as a trait; ともすれば frames a liability to slip that way under certain conditions.

related.note: 〜やすい says an action is easy to do or happen; ともすれば adds the sense of a worrying pull toward it.

title: 〜ともなく・〜ともなしに
kana: ともなく・ともなしに
meaning: without particular intention; from no definite ~
summary: 〜ともなく・〜ともなしに has two uses. With an action verb it repeats the verb to mean doing it without conscious intent — 見るともなく見る = look without really meaning to, absent-mindedly. With a question word it means 'from/at no definite ~': どこからともなく = from somewhere or other, 誰からともなく = from no one in particular. Despite the ない-like なしに, it is not a plain negative form.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ともなく／ともなしに＋（same verb）
pitfalls: With an action verb the verb is repeated (聞くともなく聞く) to mean 'doing it without meaning to'.
With a question word it means 'from/at no definite ~'; it is not a negation despite the なしに ending.

examples.ja: 窓の外を見るともなく見ていたら、旧友が通りかかった。
examples.en: As I was gazing absent-mindedly out the window, an old friend happened by.
examples.f: ｜窓[まど]の｜外[そと]を｜見[み]るともなく｜見[み]ていたら、｜旧友[きゅうゆう]が｜通[とお]りかかった。

examples.ja: どこからともなく、いい匂いが漂ってきた。
examples.en: From somewhere or other, a lovely smell came drifting in.
examples.f: どこからともなく、いい｜匂[にお]いが｜漂[ただよ]ってきた。

title: 〜ともなると・〜にもなると
kana: ともなると・にもなると
romaji: ~ tomo naru to / ~ ni mo naru to
meaning: once it reaches (as much / as high as) ~
summary: 〜ともなると・〜にもなると marks that once a subject reaches a notably high level — rank, age, amount, or occasion — a matching special situation naturally follows. 社長ともなると、責任も大きい = once you're a company president, the responsibility is great too. The 'even / as much as' emphasis on that elevated level is what sets it apart from the plainer となると.
structure: Noun＋ともなると／にもなると
pitfalls: Implies the subject has reached a notably high level (rank, age, amount, occasion) at which a fitting consequence follows.
Contrast plain となると, which lacks this 'even / as much as' emphasis on degree.

examples.ja: プロの棋士ともなると、何十手も先を読むという。
examples.en: Once you're a professional shogi player, they say you read dozens of moves ahead.
examples.f: プロの｜棋士[きし]ともなると、｜何[なん]｜十[じゅう]｜手[て]も｜先[さき]を｜読[よ]むという。

examples.ja: 年末にもなると、この商店街はいつも買い物客でにぎわう。
examples.en: Come year's end, this shopping street always bustles with shoppers.
examples.f: ｜年末[ねんまつ]にもなると、この｜商店[しょうてん]｜街[がい]はいつも｜買い物[かいもの]｜客[きゃく]でにぎわう。

synonyms.note: となると・となれば is the neutral 'when it comes to', with no emphasis on a high level; ともなると adds that 'as much as' nuance.

title: とりわけ
meaning: especially; above all; in particular
summary: とりわけ singles out one item as exceptional among a group that already shares some quality — 'above all, in particular'. 今年の夏はとりわけ暑い = this summer is especially hot. It is a touch more emphatic and formal than 特に, and can attach to a whole clause or directly qualify an adjective. Use it to pull one case out of many as standing head and shoulders above the rest.
pitfalls: Picks out one item as exceptional within a group that already shares the quality ('~ in particular').
A little more emphatic and formal in tone than 特に.

examples.ja: 果物の中でも、とりわけ桃が好きだ。
examples.en: Among fruits, I like peaches above all.
examples.f: ｜果物[くだもの]の｜中[なか]でも、とりわけ｜桃[もも]が｜好[す]きだ。

examples.ja: 今年の冬は、とりわけ雪が多かった。
examples.en: This winter had especially heavy snowfall.
examples.f: ｜今年[ことし]の｜冬[ふゆ]は、とりわけ｜雪[ゆき]が｜多[おお]かった。

title: 〜ないでもない
meaning: it's not that ~ isn't so; kind of; to some extent
summary: 〜ないでもない is a double negative that expresses reluctant or partial affirmation — 'it's not that I don't ~ / I kind of do'. 気持ちは分からないでもない = I can sort of see how you feel. It is weaker and more hedged than a plain positive, and often appears with verbs of feeling or understanding (分かる, 思う). Use it to concede something grudgingly or in a limited way.
pitfalls: A double negative meaning reluctant or partial 'I kind of do', weaker than a plain positive statement.
Compare 〜ないものでもない, which leans toward 'it could well be possible'.

examples.ja: 君の言い分も、分からないでもない。
examples.en: I can't say I don't see your point, in a way.
examples.f: ｜君[きみ]の｜言い分[いいぶん]も、｜分[わ]からないでもない。

examples.ja: 少し手伝ってくれるなら、引き受けないでもない。
examples.en: If you'll help a little, it's not as though I wouldn't take it on.
examples.f: ｜少[すこ]し｜手伝[てつだ]ってくれるなら、｜引き受[ひきう]けないでもない。

synonyms.note: ないものでもない leans toward possibility ('it's not impossible that ~'); ないでもない is a grudging partial 'I kind of do'.
ないことはない is a similar hedge ('it's not that ~ isn't so'); ないでもない tends to sound a touch more reluctant.

title: 〜ないとも限らない
meaning: cannot rule out that ~; it's not impossible that ~ might happen
summary: 〜ないとも限らない stacks two negatives (a negated predicate plus 〜とも限らない, 'it is not limited to') to make a cautious positive: 'one cannot say for certain that ~ won't happen', i.e. 'there is a chance it might'. 事故が起きないとも限らない = we can't rule out that an accident might occur. It typically raises the possibility of an undesirable outcome as a reason to stay careful, and belongs to formal or written registers.
structure: Verb［ない form］＋とも限らない
pitfalls: It is a double negative that lands on cautious possibility ('might well ~'), not a firm assertion; treat it as 'there's a chance', usually of something unwanted.
The ない belongs to the predicate you attach it to: 漏れない＋とも限らない, so the whole means 'it might leak', not 'it won't leak'.

examples.ja: 準備は万全だが、天候が急変しないとも限らない。
examples.en: Our preparations are thorough, but we can't rule out that the weather might suddenly turn.
examples.f: ｜準備[じゅんび]は｜万全[ばんぜん]だが、｜天候[てんこう]が｜急変[きゅうへん]しないとも｜限[かぎ]らない。

examples.ja: このデータが外部に漏れないとも限らないので、扱いには十分注意してほしい。
examples.en: There's no guarantee this data won't leak outside, so please handle it with the utmost care.
examples.f: このデータが｜外部[がいぶ]に｜漏[も]れないとも｜限[かぎ]らないので、｜扱[あつか]いには｜十分[じゅうぶん]｜注意[ちゅうい]してほしい。

synonyms.note: とは限らない plainly denies that something is always true; ないとも限らない adds a layer of negation to warn that the unwanted case might still occur.

related.note: ないでもない grudgingly admits 'it's kind of the case'; ないとも限らない instead flags a lingering possibility as a caution.

title: 〜ないまでも
meaning: even if not (to that extent), at least ~
summary: 〜ないまでも sets up a high standard that is not reached, then falls back on a lower but still meaningful one: 'even if not ~, at least ~'. 毎日とは言わないまでも = even if not every day (at least often). It attaches to a negated verb (often 〜とは言わない, 〜できない) and the second clause states the more modest expectation or wish that does hold.
pitfalls: The first clause names a level NOT attained; the second clause gives the lower bar that still applies, so keep the two in that order.
Do not confuse it with 〜までもない ('no need to go so far as to'): ないまでも concedes a lesser degree, までもない dismisses the action as unnecessary.

examples.ja: 満点とは言わないまでも、合格点は取りたい。
examples.en: Even if not a perfect score, I at least want to get a passing mark.
examples.f: ｜満点[まんてん]とは｜言[い]わないまでも、｜合格[ごうかく]｜点[てん]は｜取[と]りたい。

examples.ja: 完璧に理解できないまでも、要点だけは押さえておきたい。
examples.en: Even if I can't grasp it perfectly, I at least want to pin down the key points.
examples.f: ｜完璧[かんぺき]に｜理解[りかい]できないまでも、｜要点[ようてん]だけは｜押[お]さえておきたい。

related.note: までもない says the action is not even worth doing; ないまでも grants that a full degree isn't met but a partial one still stands.

title: 〜ないものか・〜ないものだろうか
kana: ないものか・ないものだろうか
romaji: nai mono ka ・ nai mono darou ka
meaning: isn't there some way to ~?; I do wish ~ could happen
summary: 〜ないものか voices a strong, half-rhetorical wish that something could be brought about: 'can't ~ somehow be done?'. なんとか解決できないものか = isn't there some way to solve this? It commonly follows a potential-negative verb (〜できない, 〜られない) and expresses yearning or frustrated hope rather than a real question. The だろうか version softens it into wistful pondering.
structure: Verb［potential negative］＋ものか／ものだろうか
pitfalls: This is an emotional wish, not a yes/no question; it does not expect an answer so much as express longing for the outcome.
It usually rides on a potential negative (できない, 手に入らない), which reads as 'isn't there any way to ~', not a flat 'don't ~'.

examples.ja: この古い町並みを、なんとか保存できないものかと考えている。
examples.en: I keep wondering whether there isn't somehow a way to preserve this old townscape.
examples.f: この｜古[ふる]い｜町並[まちな]みを、なんとか｜保存[ほぞん]できないものかと｜考[かんが]えている。

examples.ja: もう少し安く手に入らないものだろうか。
examples.en: Isn't there some way to get hold of it a little more cheaply?
examples.f: もう｜少[すこ]し｜安[やす]く｜手[て]に｜入[はい]らないものだろうか。

synonyms.note: ないものだろうか is the same wish with a musing, self-directed tone; ないものか alone can sound more pointed or impatient.

title: 〜ないもの（だろう）か
meaning: isn't there some way to ~? (a wistful, pondering wish)
summary: 〜ないものだろうか expresses a heartfelt wish framed as quiet wondering: 'I wonder whether ~ couldn't somehow come about'. The だろうか turns the plea inward, so it reads as reflective musing rather than a demand. It attaches to a negated (usually potential-negative) predicate and often accompanies a wish the speaker feels is hard to realize but hopes for anyway.
structure: Verb［ない form］＋ものだろうか
pitfalls: The だろうか makes it introspective ('I wonder if ~ couldn't ~'), gentler and less insistent than the bare ものか.
It is a wish dressed as a question; do not read だろうか here as genuine uncertainty about a fact.

examples.ja: 若い世代にもっと関心を持ってもらえないものだろうか。
examples.en: I wonder if we couldn't somehow get the younger generation to take more of an interest.
examples.f: ｜若[わか]い｜世代[せだい]にもっと｜関心[かんしん]を｜持[も]ってもらえないものだろうか。

examples.ja: この症状を和らげる方法はないものだろうか。
examples.en: Isn't there some way, I wonder, to ease these symptoms?
examples.f: この｜症状[しょうじょう]を｜和[やわ]らげる｜方法[ほうほう]はないものだろうか。

synonyms.note: ないものか carries the same yearning and can be sharper; the だろうか variant leans into calm, inward pondering.

title: 〜ないものでもない
meaning: it's not entirely impossible; it's not that ~ can't be done
summary: 〜ないものでもない piles up negatives to make a grudging, hedged admission of possibility: 'it's not as though ~ couldn't be'. やってやれないものでもない = it's not that it can't be done (given the right conditions). It often follows a potential-negative verb and signals reluctant, conditional agreement — the speaker allows the possibility without fully committing to it.
structure: Verb［ない form］＋ものでもない
pitfalls: The tone is reluctant and qualified ('I suppose it could be'), not enthusiastic; it usually comes with a condition attached.
Count the negatives: ないものでもない resolves to a cautious positive, so 引き受けないものでもない means 'I might take it on', not 'I won't'.

examples.ja: 条件次第では、引き受けないものでもない。
examples.en: Depending on the terms, it's not as though I wouldn't take it on.
examples.f: ｜条件[じょうけん]｜次第[しだい]では、｜引き受[ひきう]けないものでもない。

examples.ja: 練習すれば、彼女に追いつけないものでもないだろう。
examples.en: With practice, it's not entirely impossible to catch up with her.
examples.f: ｜練習[れんしゅう]すれば、｜彼女[かのじょ]に｜追[お]いつけないものでもないだろう。

synonyms.note: ないでもない makes the same grudging concession more compactly; ないものでもない adds もの and sounds a touch more deliberative.

related.note: ないことはない also means 'it's not impossible'; ものでもない tends to feel more hedged and reluctant.

title: 〜ながらに・〜ながらの
meaning: while remaining in that state; just as it is; as of old
summary: This ながら marks a state that stays unchanged: 〜ながらに works adverbially and 〜ながらの modifies a noun. 涙ながらに = in tears (while weeping), 生まれながらの = innate (as one was born), 昔ながらの = traditional (just as of old), いながらにして = without stirring from where one sits. It attaches to a noun or verb stem and appears largely in fixed expressions of this kind.
pitfalls: This is not the 'doing two things at once' ながら (歩きながら話す); it marks an unchanged, continuing state.
It lives mostly in set phrases — 涙ながらに, 生まれながらの, 昔ながらの, いながらにして — rather than being freely productive.

examples.ja: 彼女は涙ながらに当時の状況を語った。
examples.en: In tears, she recounted the situation at the time.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜涙[なみだ]ながらに｜当時[とうじ]の｜状況[じょうきょう]を｜語[かた]った。

examples.ja: この店では、昔ながらの製法で味噌を造り続けている。
examples.en: At this shop they carry on making miso by the traditional old methods.
examples.f: この｜店[みせ]では、｜昔[むかし]ながらの｜製法[せいほう]で｜味噌[みそ]を｜造[つく]り｜続[つづ]けている。

related.note: The ordinary ながら links two simultaneous actions; ながらに／ながらの instead freezes a state and mostly forms set phrases.
まま also means 'in an unchanged state'; ながらの is more idiomatic and adnominal (昔ながらの), まま is broadly productive (そのまま).

title: 〜なくしては
meaning: without ~ (it would be impossible)
summary: 〜なくしては presents something as an indispensable condition: 'without ~, ... could not happen'. 努力なくしては成功はない = without effort there is no success. It attaches to a noun (or 〜することなくして) and the second clause is negative or denies a possibility, stressing that the named thing is the very thing everything hinges on. The tone is formal and often rhetorical.
pitfalls: The main clause must be negative or a denied possibility (〜ない, 〜えない); without which the pattern doesn't make sense.
It is formal and emphatic, common in speeches and writing — heavier than the everyday なしでは.

examples.ja: 皆様のご支援なくしては、この事業の成功はありえませんでした。
examples.en: Without all of your support, the success of this undertaking would have been impossible.
examples.f: ｜皆様[みなさま]のご｜支援[しえん]なくしては、この｜事業[じぎょう]の｜成功[せいこう]はありえませんでした。

examples.ja: 相互の信頼なくして、真の協力関係は築けない。
examples.en: Without mutual trust, no genuine partnership can be built.
examples.f: ｜相互[そうご]の｜信頼[しんらい]なくして、｜真[しん]の｜協力[きょうりょく]｜関係[かんけい]は｜築[きづ]けない。

synonyms.note: なしに／なしで plainly means 'without doing'; なくしては frames the thing as indispensable and pairs with a negative outcome.

related.note: ことなしに means 'without doing (an action)'; なくしては typically takes a noun and asserts that the result is impossible without it.

title: 〜なしに・〜なしで
meaning: without ~; without doing ~
summary: 〜なしに and 〜なしで attach to a noun to mean 'without ~': 予告なしに = without warning, 許可なしで = without permission. With a verb they take こと first (〜することなしに). なしに tends to feel a little more formal or written than the everyday なしで, but both simply state that the expected thing was absent from the action.
pitfalls: To attach it to a verb you need こと (連絡することなしに), not the bare verb.
It is a neutral 'without'; unlike なくしては it does not by itself claim the result is impossible.

examples.ja: 彼は何の断りもなしに、私の資料を使った。
examples.en: He used my materials without so much as a word of notice.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜何[なに]の｜断[ことわ]りもなしに、｜私[わたし]の｜資料[しりょう]を｜使[つか]った。

examples.ja: 予約なしで入れる店を探している。
examples.en: I'm looking for a restaurant you can get into without a reservation.
examples.f: ｜予約[よやく]なしで｜入[い]れる｜店[みせ]を｜探[さが]している。

synonyms.note: 〜なし is the bare noun suffix ('no ~'); なしに／なしで turn it into an adverbial 'without ~' modifying the action.
ことなしに is exactly the verb-taking form of this pattern ('without doing ~').

related.note: なくしては makes the same 'without' emphatic and ties it to an impossible result; なしに／なしで stay neutral.

title: 〜並み
meaning: on a par with; the same level as; average
summary: 〜並み is a noun suffix meaning 'at the same level or standard as ~'. プロ並み = on a par with a professional, 例年並み = about the same as an average year, 人並み = average, like everyone else. It sets the attached noun as the yardstick and says the thing measures up to it. The reading is なみ.
pitfalls: It measures 'equal in level to a standard', not 'approximately how much'; that is the job of くらい／ほど.
人並み means 'average / like most people', while プロ並み means 'as good as a pro' — the standard set by the noun is what counts.

examples.ja: 彼の料理の腕前は、プロ並みだと言われている。
examples.en: His cooking skills are said to be on a par with a professional's.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜料理[りょうり]の｜腕前[うでまえ]は、プロ｜並[な]みだと｜言[い]われている。

examples.ja: 今年の冬の寒さは、例年並みだそうだ。
examples.en: This winter's cold is said to be about average for the season.
examples.f: ｜今年[ことし]の｜冬[ふゆ]の｜寒[さむ]さは、｜例年[れいねん]｜並[な]みだそうだ。

related.note: ほど marks an approximate degree or comparison point; 並み specifically claims the thing reaches the same level as a set standard.

title: 〜なら〜で
meaning: if it's ~, then that's its own situation (things still work out / bring their own issues)
summary: 〜なら〜で repeats the same word on both sides to say that even in that case, things resolve themselves — or throw up a different problem. あるならあるで = if you have it, then that's its own matter; ないならないで = if there's none, then we'll manage even so. It concedes a situation and shrugs that it too has its own way of playing out. The 〜ば〜で shape (なければないで) is common.
pitfalls: The same word must appear on both sides; the point is that either state carries its own resolution or its own trouble.
It is fairly conversational and often carries a resigned 'well, so be it' nuance.

examples.ja: 部屋が狭いなら狭いで、工夫すれば案外快適に暮らせるものだ。
examples.en: If the room is small, then so be it — with a little ingenuity you can live quite comfortably even so.
examples.f: ｜部屋[へや]が｜狭[せま]いなら｜狭[せま]いで、｜工夫[くふう]すれば｜案外[あんがい]｜快適[かいてき]に｜暮[く]らせるものだ。

examples.ja: 時間がないならないで、その中で工夫するしかない。
examples.en: If there's no time, then so be it — we just have to make do within that.
examples.f: ｜時間[じかん]がないならないで、その｜中[なか]で｜工夫[くふう]するしかない。

title: 〜ならいざ知らず・〜はいざ知らず
kana: ならいざしらず・はいざしらず
romaji: nara iza shirazu ・ wa iza shirazu
meaning: I don't know about ~ (if it were that, fine), but ~
summary: 〜ならいざ知らず sets aside one case as 'that I couldn't say / that might be another matter' in order to sharpen a judgment about the actual case. 子供ならいざ知らず = if it were a child, that would be one thing, but... The set-aside case is usually an extreme or excusable one, and the main clause delivers surprise, criticism, or a firm stance about the real situation. It is formal and somewhat literary.
pitfalls: The case before it is dismissed as 'maybe acceptable / who knows', so the weight falls on the contrasting main clause.
いざ知らず is a fixed literary phrase (from 知る); it is not freely conjugated.

examples.ja: 新人ならいざ知らず、十年選手がこんなミスをするとは情けない。
examples.en: If it were a newcomer that would be one thing, but for a ten-year veteran to make such a mistake is pathetic.
examples.f: ｜新人[しんじん]ならいざ｜知[し]らず、｜十[じゅう]｜年[ねん]｜選手[せんしゅ]がこんなミスをするとは｜情[なさ]けない。

examples.ja: 大昔ならいざ知らず、今の時代にそんな迷信を信じる人はいない。
examples.en: It might have been different in the distant past, but no one in this day and age believes such a superstition.
examples.f: ｜大昔[おおむかし]ならいざ｜知[し]らず、｜今[いま]の｜時代[じだい]にそんな｜迷信[めいしん]を｜信[しん]じる｜人[ひと]はいない。

synonyms.note: ならまだしも sets aside a case as 'comparatively tolerable'; ならいざ知らず sets it aside as 'that I can't speak to', both to spotlight the worse actual case.

title: 〜ならでは
meaning: unique to; only possible for; distinctive of
summary: 〜ならでは(の) praises something as achievable only by the named person, place, or thing: その店ならではの味 = a flavor only that shop can produce. It usually appears as ならではの + noun or ならではだ, and the tone is admiring — it credits a quality to the special character of the referent that nothing else could match.
pitfalls: It carries positive, appreciative force ('only ~ could pull this off'); it is not used to point out drawbacks.
The usual shape is ならではの followed by a noun; ならでは rarely stands without の or だ.

examples.ja: この祭りには、この土地ならではの活気がある。
examples.en: This festival has a liveliness you'll find only in this region.
examples.f: この｜祭[まつ]りには、この｜土地[とち]ならではの｜活気[かっき]がある。

examples.ja: 細部への気配りは、彼女ならではのものだ。
examples.en: This attention to the finest details is something only she can bring.
examples.f: ｜細部[さいぶ]への｜気配[きくば]りは、｜彼女[かのじょ]ならではのものだ。

related.note: だけあって explains an impressive result as living up to a background ('as you'd expect of ~'); ならでは credits a quality as uniquely possible for the referent.

title: 〜ならまだしも
meaning: if it were ~ that would be one thing, but ~
summary: 〜ならまだしも grants that one case would be comparatively acceptable, so as to condemn the actual, worse case: 一度だけならまだしも = if it were just once that would be tolerable, but... The case before it is 'still passable'; the main clause then registers that reality goes beyond that and is unacceptable or hard to accept.
pitfalls: What precedes it is presented as the lesser, still-bearable option; the complaint lands on the actual situation that follows.
Close to plain まだしも (N2), but ならまだしも specifically pins the 'acceptable' case to a condition ('if it were ~').

examples.ja: 一度だけならまだしも、同じ過ちを何度も繰り返すとは。
examples.en: If it were just once that would be one thing, but to repeat the same mistake over and over...
examples.f: ｜一[いち]｜度[ど]だけならまだしも、｜同[おな]じ｜過[あやま]ちを｜何[なん]｜度[ど]も｜繰り返[くりかえ]すとは。

examples.ja: 安いならまだしも、この品質でこの値段では買う気になれない。
examples.en: If it were cheap it would be another matter, but at this quality for this price I can't bring myself to buy it.
examples.f: ｜安[やす]いならまだしも、この｜品質[ひんしつ]でこの｜値段[ねだん]では｜買[か]う｜気[き]になれない。

synonyms.note: まだしも on its own means 'comparatively better / still acceptable'; ならまだしも fixes that acceptable case to an explicit condition.
ならいざ知らず brushes a case aside as 'who's to say'; ならまだしも rates it as 'tolerable by comparison', both to condemn the real case.

title: 〜なり
meaning: as soon as; the moment (one does) ~
summary: Verb［dictionary form］＋なり means the second action follows the very instant the first is done: 家に帰るなり寝てしまった = the moment he got home, he fell asleep. The second event is typically sudden, spontaneous, and a bit unexpected, and both usually share one subject. It is literary. Note the separate た-form use 〜たなり ('left in that unchanged state'), as in 横になったなり.
structure: Verb［た form］＋なり ［left in that state］
pitfalls: Use the dictionary form for the 'as soon as' sense (見るなり), not the past tense.
The second clause describes an actual, often surprising event — not a command, intention, or request.
Distinguish 〜たなり ('remaining in that state', like 〜たまま), e.g. 靴を履いたなり寝る, from the 'the moment ~' sense.

examples.ja: 彼はドアを開けるなり、大声で叫び始めた。
examples.en: The moment he opened the door, he started shouting at the top of his voice.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]はドアを｜開[あ]けるなり、｜大声[おおごえ]で｜叫[さけ]び｜始[はじ]めた。

examples.ja: 子供は母親の顔を見るなり、わっと泣き出した。
examples.en: The instant the child saw its mother's face, it burst into tears.
examples.f: ｜子供[こども]は｜母親[ははおや]の｜顔[かお]を｜見[み]るなり、わっと｜泣[な]き｜出[だ]した。

synonyms.note: や否や is a similar literary 'as soon as'; なり leans harder on the second action being spontaneous and unexpected.
が早いか stresses that the two events were almost simultaneous; なり foregrounds the abrupt reaction that immediately follows.

related.note: か〜ないかのうちに says the second event began before the first fully finished; なり has the first clearly complete, then the reaction right after.

title: なり〜なり
meaning: either ~ or ~ (for instance); ~ or ~ or something
summary: なり〜なり lists two representative options and invites the listener to pick one (or something in that vein): 電話なりメールなりで連絡して = get in touch by phone or email or whatever works. It attaches to nouns or dictionary-form verbs. The list is illustrative rather than exhaustive, and it commonly appears in suggestions or gentle instructions.
pitfalls: The two items are examples, not the only choices; 'or something along those lines' is implied.
Don't confuse the paired なり〜なり (choices) with the single なり ('as soon as').

examples.ja: わからないことがあれば、辞書で調べるなり先生に聞くなりしなさい。
examples.en: If there's something you don't understand, look it up in a dictionary or ask the teacher or something.
examples.f: わからないことがあれば、｜辞書[じしょ]で｜調[しら]べるなり｜先生[せんせい]に｜聞[き]くなりしなさい。

examples.ja: 電話なりメールなり、都合のいい方法で連絡してください。
examples.en: Get in touch by phone or email — whichever is convenient for you.
examples.f: ｜電話[でんわ]なりメールなり、｜都合[つごう]のいい｜方法[ほうほう]で｜連絡[れんらく]してください。

synonyms.note: たり〜たり lists representative actions that occur; なり〜なり lists options offered for the listener to choose among.
か〜か presents a plain 'either A or B' choice; なり〜なり adds an 'or something like that, whichever suits' flavor.

title: 〜なりとも
meaning: even just ~; at least ~
summary: 〜なりとも attaches to a (usually small) amount or noun to mean 'even if only ~, at least ~': 多少なりとも = even a little, 少しなりとも = even slightly. It concedes that the amount is minimal while stressing that even that much matters. It is formal or literary, and appears in fixed forms such as 多少なりとも and 何なりと ('anything at all').
structure: Noun［often a small quantity］＋なりとも
何／誰＋なりと ［fixed: 'anything / anyone at all'］
pitfalls: It is formal and mostly fixed in phrases like 多少なりとも, 少しなりとも, 何なりと; it is not freely productive in casual speech.
The nuance is 'even this small amount is something', so it usually pairs with a modest quantity.

examples.ja: 多少なりとも、お役に立てれば幸いです。
examples.en: I would be glad if I could be of even a little help.
examples.f: ｜多少[たしょう]なりとも、お｜役[やく]に｜立[た]てれば｜幸[さいわ]いです。

examples.ja: 最後にもう一度なりとも、彼に会いたかった。
examples.en: I wanted to see him even just one more time at the end.
examples.f: ｜最後[さいご]にもう｜一度[いちど]なりとも、｜彼[かれ]に｜会[あ]いたかった。

related.note: Same syllables なり, different pattern: なり〜なり offers a choice of examples, while 〜なりとも means 'even just ~, at least'.

title: 〜なりに・〜なりの
meaning: in one's own way; in a manner fitting to ~
summary: 〜なりに (adverbial) and 〜なりの (before a noun) mean 'in a way befitting the person or thing, within its own means': 私なりに考えた = I thought it over in my own way, 子供なりの理屈 = a child's own kind of logic. It respectfully acknowledges that someone did their best according to their own, often limited, capacity or position, without treating that as a shortcoming.
pitfalls: It implies doing one's best within one's own (often modest) means, and is not meant as a put-down.
Use なりに to modify a verb (私なりに頑張る) and なりの to modify a noun (私なりの答え).

examples.ja: 私なりに精一杯やったつもりだ。
examples.en: I did my very best in my own way, or so I believe.
examples.f: ｜私[わたし]なりに｜精一杯[せいいっぱい]やったつもりだ。

examples.ja: 子供には子供なりの理屈があるものだ。
examples.en: Children have their own kind of logic, in their own way.
examples.f: ｜子供[こども]には｜子供[こども]なりの｜理屈[りくつ]があるものだ。

related.note: らしい ('typical of / befitting', as in 子供らしい) judges by an expected image; なりの credits each one's own particular way of doing things.

title: なんという・なんと・なんて
kana: なんという・なんと・なんて
romaji: nan to iu ・ nanto ・ nante
meaning: how ~!; what a ~! (exclamation of strong feeling)
summary: As exclamations, なんという／なんと／なんて express strong emotion — admiration, astonishment, or dismay — before a noun or adjective: なんて美しい景色だろう = what a beautiful view!, なんという偶然 = what a coincidence. They often round off with だろう／でしょう. なんて is the most colloquial of the three; なんと and なんという feel a little more emphatic or written.
structure: なんという／なんと／なんて＋Noun
なんと／なんて＋Adjective＋（だろう／でしょう）
pitfalls: This exclamatory なんて (emotion) is different from the dismissive なんて meaning 'things like ~ / such a thing as' (勉強なんて嫌いだ).
It frequently pairs with だろう／でしょう to complete the exclamation.

examples.ja: なんという美しい眺めだろう。言葉が出ない。
examples.en: What a beautiful view! I'm at a loss for words.
examples.f: なんという｜美[うつく]しい｜眺[なが]めだろう。｜言葉[ことば]が｜出[で]ない。

examples.ja: こんなに早く全部片付けたなんて、なんて手際がいいんだ。
examples.en: To have cleared it all away this quickly — how deft you are!
examples.f: こんなに｜早[はや]く｜全部[ぜんぶ]｜片付[かたづ]けたなんて、なんて｜手際[てぎわ]がいいんだ。

synonyms.note: といったらない conveys an extreme, indescribable degree of feeling; なんという／なんて is a more direct exclamatory 'what a ~!'.

related.note: など (and its colloquial なんて) can dismiss or belittle ('~ and the like / such a thing as'); the exclamatory なんて here voices strong emotion instead.

title: 〜に〜ない
meaning: cannot do ~ even though one wants to; be stuck unable to ~
summary: This pattern repeats one verb as dictionary form ＋に＋ its potential negative to say the speaker is unable to do it despite wanting to: 言うに言えない = can't bring myself to say it, 引くに引けない = can't back out now. It portrays a bind — the will is there but circumstances block the action. The verbs are limited to ones that form this pair naturally (言う, 引く, 泣く, 帰る, etc.).
pitfalls: The same verb appears twice: dictionary form, then its potential negative (言う→言えない, 引く→引けない).
Distinct from 〜ようにも〜ない, which starts from the volitional (帰ろうにも帰れない); this pattern uses the plain dictionary form plus に.

examples.ja: 途中でやめるわけにもいかず、引くに引けない状況に陥った。
examples.en: I couldn't very well quit partway, and ended up in a situation where I couldn't back out even if I wanted to.
examples.f: ｜途中[とちゅう]でやめるわけにもいかず、｜引[ひ]くに｜引[ひ]けない｜状況[じょうきょう]に｜陥[おちい]った。

examples.ja: 本当のことは、言うに言えない事情があって黙っていた。
examples.en: As for the truth, there were circumstances that made it impossible to say even though I wanted to, so I kept quiet.
examples.f: ｜本当[ほんとう]のことは、｜言[い]うに｜言[い]えない｜事情[じじょう]があって｜黙[だま]っていた。

synonyms.note: ようにも〜ない builds on the volitional (〜ようにも〜れない); 〜に〜ない uses the dictionary form + に + potential negative for the same 'can't, though I want to'.

title: 〜に〜を重ねて
meaning: after piling ~ upon ~; through repeated ~
summary: 〜に〜を重ねて repeats the same noun across に and を to stress that something was accumulated over and over: 努力に努力を重ねて = piling effort upon effort, 失敗に失敗を重ねる = heaping failure upon failure. It emphasizes the sheer repetition or layering of the same experience, usually as the drawn-out process leading to a hard-won result. The register is formal or written.
pitfalls: The same noun must sit on both に and を (苦労に苦労を重ねる); it is the repetition of one thing, not two different ones.
It stresses accumulated repetition over time and belongs to formal, written-style Japanese.

examples.ja: 彼らは失敗に失敗を重ねた末に、ついに新製品を完成させた。
examples.en: After piling failure upon failure, they finally completed the new product.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]らは｜失敗[しっぱい]に｜失敗[しっぱい]を｜重[かさ]ねた｜末[すえ]に、ついに｜新[しん]｜製品[せいひん]を｜完成[かんせい]させた。

examples.ja: 議論に議論を重ねて、ようやく全員が納得する結論に達した。
examples.en: Heaping discussion upon discussion, they at last reached a conclusion everyone could accept.
examples.f: ｜議論[ぎろん]に｜議論[ぎろん]を｜重[かさ]ねて、ようやく｜全員[ぜんいん]が｜納得[なっとく]する｜結論[けつろん]に｜達[たっ]した。

related.note: た末に marks the final outcome after a long process; 〜に〜を重ねて zooms in on the repeated piling-up of the same effort within such a process.

title: 〜にあって
meaning: in; at; under (a particular situation, position, or era)
summary: 〜にあって places the following statement within a special situation, position, or time — 'being in ~, situated in ~'. 非常時にあって = in a time of emergency, その立場にあって = holding that position. It sets up circumstances that are notable or extreme, and the main clause tells what holds true under them. The negative-conditional form にあっても means 'even in ~'. It is a formal, written expression.
pitfalls: Formal and written; in ordinary speech に or で is used instead.
にあって frames a situation or position, not a physical meeting; do not read it as the 〜に会って ('meet ~') of everyday verbs.
にあっても means 'even in ~', shifting the sense from setting a scene to concession.

examples.ja: 危機的な状況にあって、彼は最後まで冷静さを失わなかった。
examples.en: In a critical situation, he kept his composure to the very end.
examples.f: ｜危機[きき]｜的[てき]な｜状況[じょうきょう]にあって、｜彼[かれ]は｜最後[さいご]まで｜冷静[れいせい]さを｜失[うしな]わなかった。

examples.ja: 情報が氾濫する現代にあっては、何を信じるかがかえって難しい。
examples.en: In today's world awash with information, deciding what to believe is, if anything, all the harder.
examples.f: ｜情報[じょうほう]が｜氾濫[はんらん]する｜現代[げんだい]にあっては、｜何[なに]を｜信[しん]じるかがかえって｜難[むずか]しい。

synonyms.note: において neutrally marks a place, time, or field; にあって stresses being placed within a notable or trying situation.

related.note: とあって gives a special circumstance as the reason for what follows; にあって sets the circumstance as a backdrop without asserting cause.

title: 〜に至っては
meaning: when it comes to (this extreme case); as for (of all things)
summary: 〜に至っては singles out the most extreme or worst example among several and comments on it, usually with dismay or criticism. After listing so-so cases, it picks the one that goes furthest — 兄はまだしも、弟に至っては = the older brother is one thing, but as for the younger one. What follows is typically how bad or hopeless that case is. It is a formal expression built on 至る ('to reach').
pitfalls: It highlights the single most extreme case, almost always to criticize or lament — not a neutral 'regarding ~'.
Distinct from the temporal に至って ('upon finally reaching ~'); に至っては picks out an extreme example.

examples.ja: 予算は削られ、人手も足りない。新人の育成に至っては、まったく手つかずのままだ。
examples.en: The budget has been cut and we are short-handed; as for training the new hires, that has been left completely untouched.
examples.f: ｜予算[よさん]は｜削[けず]られ、｜人手[ひとで]も｜足[た]りない。｜新人[しんじん]の｜育成[いくせい]に｜至[いた]っては、まったく｜手[て]つかずのままだ。

examples.ja: 上の子はまだ勉強するが、下の子に至っては教科書すら開こうとしない。
examples.en: The older child at least studies, but when it comes to the younger one, they won't even open a textbook.
examples.f: ｜上[うえ]の｜子[こ]はまだ｜勉強[べんきょう]するが、｜下[した]の｜子[こ]に｜至[いた]っては｜教科書[きょうかしょ]すら｜開[ひら]こうとしない。

synonyms.note: となると shifts to 'when it comes to ~' neutrally; に至っては adds that this is the worst, most extreme case.

related.note: に至る is the base verb 'to reach (an extreme point)'; に至っては applies that framing to pick out one glaring example.
に至っても means 'even after reaching (that extreme), still ~'; に至っては instead singles out the extreme case for comment.

title: 〜に至っても
meaning: even when it has come to (this extreme point); even now that ~
summary: 〜に至っても marks that even after a situation has reached an extreme or final stage, the expected change still fails to happen. It stresses that things have gone this far and yet — 締め切り当日に至っても = even when the very day of the deadline arrived. The main clause usually ends in a negative or in stubborn inaction. It is formal and built on 至る ('to reach').
pitfalls: The main clause typically states that the looked-for change did not occur even at this extreme stage; it often ends in 〜ない.
Distinct from に至っては, which singles out an extreme example rather than conceding 'even now'.

examples.ja: 締め切り当日に至っても、彼から原稿は届かなかった。
examples.en: Even when the day of the deadline itself arrived, the manuscript still hadn't come from him.
examples.f: ｜締め切[しめき]り｜当日[とうじつ]に｜至[いた]っても、｜彼[かれ]から｜原稿[げんこう]は｜届[とど]かなかった。

examples.ja: これほど問題が深刻化するに至っても、経営陣は方針を変えようとしない。
examples.en: Even now that the problem has grown this serious, management still refuses to change course.
examples.f: これほど｜問題[もんだい]が｜深刻[しんこく]｜化[か]するに｜至[いた]っても、｜経営[けいえい]｜陣[じん]は｜方針[ほうしん]を｜変[か]えようとしない。

related.note: に至る plainly states 'reaches (an extreme point)'; に至っても adds the concessive 'even having reached it, still ~'.
に至っては picks out the most extreme case to comment on; に至っても concedes that even at the extreme, nothing changed.

title: 〜に至る・〜に至って・〜に至り
kana: にいたる・にいたって・にいたり
romaji: ni itaru / ni itatte / ni itari
meaning: to reach (an extreme point or final state); only when it came to ~
summary: 〜に至る describes finally arriving at an extreme, serious, or final stage after a long process — much weightier than plain なる. 合併するに至る = to reach the point of merging, ここに至る = to come to this pass. The connective 至って marks 'upon finally reaching ~', and 至り appears in formal writing. It stresses that things went all the way to a decisive end. The register is formal and literary.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋に至る／に至って／に至り
Noun＋に至る／に至って／に至り
pitfalls: 至る marks reaching an extreme or grave stage; it is far heavier than a neutral なる and suits weighty outcomes.
It follows a dictionary-form verb: 決断するに至る, not 決断したに至る.

examples.ja: 両社は長い交渉の末、ついに合併するに至った。
examples.en: After long negotiations, the two companies finally reached the point of merging.
examples.f: ｜両社[りょうしゃ]は｜長[なが]い｜交渉[こうしょう]の｜末[すえ]、ついに｜合併[がっぺい]するに｜至[いた]った。

examples.ja: 大きな事故が起こるに至って、ようやく安全対策が見直された。
examples.en: It was only when a major accident occurred that safety measures were finally reviewed.
examples.f: ｜大[おお]きな｜事故[じこ]が｜起[お]こるに｜至[いた]って、ようやく｜安全[あんぜん]｜対策[たいさく]が｜見直[みなお]された。

related.note: に至るまで stresses a range extending even to an extreme endpoint; に至る marks arriving at a final stage after a process.
に至っては singles out one extreme case for comment; に至る simply states reaching an extreme point.
に至っても concedes 'even having reached (that point), still ~'; に至る just marks the reaching itself.

title: 〜に至るまで
meaning: everything up to and including; (extending) even to ~
summary: 〜に至るまで stresses that a range reaches all the way to an extreme, minor, or surprising endpoint — 'from ~ right down to ~'. It commonly pairs with から: 服装から言葉遣いに至るまで = everything from clothing down to word choice. The point is that even the far or trivial end is covered, which plain まで does not emphasize. It is a formal expression.
pitfalls: It emphasizes that the range extends even to an extreme or trivial endpoint; it is stronger than a bare まで.
Most often used as 〜から〜に至るまで to sweep across a whole span.

examples.ja: 彼女は服装から言葉遣いに至るまで、細かく指導された。
examples.en: She was given detailed guidance on everything from her clothing right down to her word choice.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜服装[ふくそう]から｜言葉[ことば]｜遣[づか]いに｜至[いた]るまで、｜細[こま]かく｜指導[しどう]された。

examples.ja: 経営者から現場のアルバイトに至るまで、全員が同じ理念を共有している。
examples.en: From the executives down to the part-timers on the floor, everyone shares the same philosophy.
examples.f: ｜経営[けいえい]｜者[しゃ]から｜現場[げんば]のアルバイトに｜至[いた]るまで、｜全員[ぜんいん]が｜同[おな]じ｜理念[りねん]を｜共有[きょうゆう]している。

related.note: まで marks a plain endpoint; に至るまで adds that the range reaches even an extreme or unexpected far end.
から〜にかけて spans a rough range over time or space; から〜に至るまで stresses that even the extreme endpoint is included.

title: 〜に言わせれば
meaning: if you ask ~; in ~'s opinion (as they would put it)
summary: 〜に言わせれば introduces a person's subjective, often assertive verdict on something — 'the way ~ sees it, if you ask ~'. 私に言わせれば = if you ask me, 専門家に言わせれば = as the experts would put it. It frames what follows as that person's opinion, frequently a pointed or critical one, rather than neutral fact. The person is marked with に.
pitfalls: It presents a subjective, often critical judgment, not objective fact; expect an opinionated statement to follow.
The holder of the opinion takes に: 私に言わせれば, not 私が言わせれば.

examples.ja: 私に言わせれば、彼のやり方は少し強引すぎる。
examples.en: If you ask me, his way of doing things is a bit too forceful.
examples.f: ｜私[わたし]に｜言[い]わせれば、｜彼[かれ]のやり｜方[かた]は｜少[すこ]し｜強引[ごういん]すぎる。

examples.ja: 専門家に言わせれば、この対策は場当たり的なものにすぎないそうだ。
examples.en: According to the experts, this measure is nothing more than a stopgap.
examples.f: ｜専門[せんもん]｜家[か]に｜言[い]わせれば、この｜対策[たいさく]は｜場当[ばあ]たり｜的[てき]なものにすぎないそうだ。

related.note: にしてみれば imagines how a situation feels from someone's standpoint; に言わせれば voices the opinion or verdict they would actually state.
にとって marks 'for ~ / to ~' as the one an evaluation matters to; に言わせれば introduces that person's own spoken judgment.

title: 〜にかかっている
meaning: to depend on; to hinge on; to rest on
summary: 〜にかかっている says that an outcome rests entirely on one deciding factor — 'it all depends on ~, it hinges on ~'. The uncertain result is usually phrased with 〜かどうか or a question word, and the factor it turns on is marked with に: 成功するかどうかは君の努力にかかっている = whether it succeeds depends on your effort. It stresses that everything comes down to that one thing.
structure: Noun／Sentence［〜かどうか］＋は＋Noun＋にかかっている
pitfalls: The thing that is decided is usually a 〜かどうか clause or question phrase; the deciding factor takes に.
It stresses total dependence on one factor — everything comes down to it, not merely 'is related to it'.

examples.ja: 計画が成功するかどうかは、君の努力にかかっている。
examples.en: Whether the plan succeeds hinges on your effort.
examples.f: ｜計画[けいかく]が｜成功[せいこう]するかどうかは、｜君[きみ]の｜努力[どりょく]にかかっている。

examples.ja: 会社の将来は、この新製品が売れるかどうかにかかっていると言ってもいい。
examples.en: You could say the company's future rests on whether this new product sells.
examples.f: ｜会社[かいしゃ]の｜将来[しょうらい]は、この｜新[しん]｜製品[せいひん]が｜売[う]れるかどうかにかかっていると｜言[い]ってもいい。

synonyms.note: 次第だ names the deciding factor formally ('depending on ~'); にかかっている stresses that the whole outcome rests on it.

related.note: によって marks a means or cause; にかかっている frames one factor as the thing an entire outcome hangs on.
にかかっては describes what inevitably happens once a certain person takes charge; にかかっている states that an outcome depends on a factor.

title: 〜にかかっては・〜にかかったら・〜にかかると
kana: にかかっては・にかかったら・にかかると
romaji: ni kakatte wa / ni kakattara / ni kakaru to
meaning: in the hands of ~; once ~ takes it on (things inevitably go a certain way)
summary: 〜にかかっては marks that once a certain formidable or skilled person gets involved, a particular result becomes unavoidable — 'in the hands of ~'. あの弁護士にかかっては = in the hands of that lawyer, どんな難事件も解決してしまう. The person is marked with に, and the main clause states what inevitably happens once they take charge, often with a touch of admiration or resignation. It is conversational.
structure: Noun［person］＋にかかっては／にかかったら／にかかると
pitfalls: It describes an inevitable result once a certain capable or formidable person is on the case — not neutral dependence.
Do not confuse it with にかかっている ('an outcome depends on ~'); these are different patterns despite the shared かかる.

examples.ja: あの弁護士にかかっては、どんな難事件も解決してしまう。
examples.en: In the hands of that lawyer, even the toughest case ends up solved.
examples.f: あの｜弁護士[べんごし]にかかっては、どんな｜難事件[なんじけん]も｜解決[かいけつ]してしまう。

examples.ja: 母にかかったら、私の小さな嘘などすぐに見抜かれてしまう。
examples.en: Once my mother is on the case, my little lies are seen through in no time.
examples.f: ｜母[はは]にかかったら、｜私[わたし]の｜小[ちい]さな｜嘘[うそ]などすぐに｜見抜[みぬ]かれてしまう。

related.note: にかかっている states that an outcome depends on a factor; にかかっては describes what a certain person inevitably brings about.
にかけては praises someone as unmatched in a skill; にかかっては stresses the inevitable result once they take something on.

title: 〜に限ったことではない
kana: にかぎったことではない
meaning: not limited to only ~; not something confined to ~
summary: 〜に限ったことではない denies that a matter is unique to the named case — 'it is not something limited to ~'. 残業が多いのはこの業界に限ったことではない = heavy overtime is not something confined to this industry. It usually implies the phenomenon is in fact more widespread, and often carries a note that it is a broader problem. The noun is marked with に.
structure: Noun＋に限ったことではない
pitfalls: It states the thing is not exclusive to the named case, usually implying 'it happens more widely too'.
Distinct from に限って ('of all things, precisely ~'); this pattern negates exclusivity rather than pinpointing one case.

examples.ja: 残業が多いのは、この業界に限ったことではない。
examples.en: Heavy overtime is not something limited to this industry.
examples.f: ｜残業[ざんぎょう]が｜多[おお]いのは、この｜業界[ぎょうかい]に｜限[かぎ]ったことではない。

examples.ja: 値上げは食品に限ったことではなく、生活全般に及んでいる。
examples.en: Price hikes aren't confined to food; they extend across daily life in general.
examples.f: ｜値上[ねあ]げは｜食品[しょくひん]に｜限[かぎ]ったことではなく、｜生活[せいかつ]｜全般[ぜんぱん]に｜及[およ]んでいる。

synonyms.note: に限らず means 'not just ~ but also (more widely)'; に限ったことではない flatly denies that the matter is exclusive to the named case.

antonyms.note: に限って pinpoints one case as special ('of all times/things, precisely ~'); に限ったことではない denies any such exclusivity.

related.note: のみならず means 'not only ~ but also'; に限ったことではない simply denies that something is unique to one case.

title: 〜にかこつけて
meaning: using ~ as a pretext; on the excuse of ~
summary: 〜にかこつけて marks using something as a convenient pretext to do what one really wanted anyway — 'under the guise of ~, on the excuse of ~'. 出張にかこつけて = using a business trip as a pretext, 病気にかこつけて断る = beg off on the excuse of illness. It implies the stated reason is a cover for a hidden motive. It attaches to a noun and is somewhat formal.
pitfalls: It implies the stated reason is a pretext masking one's real aim, not a genuine cause.
It attaches to a noun; to build a pretext from a clause, nominalize first (〜のにかこつけて / 〜ことにかこつけて).

examples.ja: 彼は出張にかこつけて、地元の旧友と会っていたらしい。
examples.en: He apparently used the business trip as a pretext to meet up with old friends back home.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜出張[しゅっちょう]にかこつけて、｜地元[じもと]の｜旧友[きゅうゆう]と｜会[あ]っていたらしい。

examples.ja: 体調が悪いのにかこつけて、気の進まない集まりを断った。
examples.en: On the excuse of feeling unwell, I turned down a gathering I wasn't keen on.
examples.f: ｜体調[たいちょう]が｜悪[わる]いのにかこつけて、｜気[き]の｜進[すす]まない｜集[あつ]まりを｜断[ことわ]った。

related.note: をいいことに exploits a genuinely favorable circumstance; にかこつけて uses something as a surface excuse to cover a real motive.

title: 〜に難くない
meaning: not hard to (imagine, guess, surmise)
summary: 〜に難くない means that something takes no effort to imagine or infer — 'it is not hard to ~'. In practice it combines with only a few verbs, above all 想像する and 察する: 想像に難くない = not hard to imagine, 察するに難くない = not hard to surmise. It is used to say that a feeling or situation can readily be understood. The register is formal and literary.
pitfalls: It pairs almost exclusively with 想像する and 察する; it is not a general-purpose 'easy to do'.
With 想像 the fixed shape is 想像に難くない (the する drops); do not force it onto arbitrary verbs.
Formal and written — it would sound stiff in casual conversation.

examples.ja: 突然家族を失った彼の悲しみは、想像に難くない。
examples.en: The grief of a man who suddenly lost his family is not hard to imagine.
examples.f: ｜突然[とつぜん]｜家族[かぞく]を｜失[うしな]った｜彼[かれ]の｜悲[かな]しみは、｜想像[そうぞう]に｜難[かた]くない。

examples.ja: 彼女がこの数年どれほど苦労したかは、察するに難くない。
examples.en: It is not hard to surmise how much hardship she has been through these past few years.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]がこの｜数[すう]｜年[ねん]どれほど｜苦労[くろう]したかは、｜察[さっ]するに｜難[かた]くない。

title: 〜にかまけて
meaning: being too absorbed in ~ (and neglecting other things)
summary: 〜にかまけて marks being so preoccupied with one thing that other things get neglected — 'caught up in ~, too taken up with ~'. 仕事にかまけて家庭を顧みない = so absorbed in work that one neglects the family. It is inherently negative: the following clause states what was let slide. It attaches to a noun and belongs to a somewhat formal, self-reflective register.
pitfalls: It is always negative — being wrapped up in one thing causes neglect of another, named in the following clause.
It attaches to a noun (仕事にかまけて, 忙しさにかまけて), not directly to a plain verb.

examples.ja: 仕事にかまけて、家族との時間をずっとおろそかにしてきた。
examples.en: Absorbed in my work, I have long neglected time with my family.
examples.f: ｜仕事[しごと]にかまけて、｜家族[かぞく]との｜時間[じかん]をずっとおろそかにしてきた。

examples.ja: 日々の忙しさにかまけて、健康のことをすっかり忘れていた。
examples.en: Caught up in the busyness of daily life, I had completely forgotten about my health.
examples.f: ｜日々[ひび]の｜忙[いそが]しさにかまけて、｜健康[けんこう]のことをすっかり｜忘[わす]れていた。

related.note: にかこつけて uses something as a deliberate excuse; にかまけて is genuine over-absorption that causes unintended neglect.

title: 〜に先駆けて
meaning: ahead of; before anyone else; taking the lead over ~
summary: 〜に先駆けて marks doing something before others or before the usual time, taking the lead — 'ahead of ~, in advance of ~'. 他社に先駆けて発売する = launch ahead of rival firms, 桜に先駆けて咲く = bloom before the cherry blossoms. It carries a sense of being first or pioneering, not merely earlier. The noun is marked with に, and the register is formal.
pitfalls: It stresses being first — taking the lead over others or over the normal timing — not just 'before' in a neutral sequence.
Compared with に先立って (plain 'prior to ~'), 先駆けて adds the nuance of pioneering or getting a head start.

examples.ja: その企業は他社に先駆けて、電気自動車の量産に踏み切った。
examples.en: That company took the plunge into mass-producing electric cars ahead of its competitors.
examples.f: その｜企業[きぎょう]は｜他社[たしゃ]に｜先駆[さきが]けて、｜電気[でんき]｜自動車[じどうしゃ]の｜量産[りょうさん]に｜踏み切[ふみき]った。

examples.ja: 春の訪れに先駆けて、梅の花が咲き始めた。
examples.en: Ahead of the arrival of spring, the plum blossoms have begun to bloom.
examples.f: ｜春[はる]の｜訪[おとず]れに｜先駆[さきが]けて、｜梅[うめ]の｜花[はな]が｜咲[さ]き｜始[はじ]めた。

related.note: に先立ち neutrally marks 'prior to (an event)', often preparation beforehand; に先駆けて adds being first or pioneering.
を皮切りに marks the first event that kicks off a whole series; に先駆けて marks doing one thing ahead of others.

title: 〜にしたところで・〜としたところで
kana: にしたところで・としたところで
romaji: ni shita tokoro de / to shita tokoro de
meaning: even ~; even for ~; even supposing ~ (it makes no difference)
summary: 〜にしたところで takes up a case and concedes that even it is no exception, or even supposing it, the conclusion still holds — usually that nothing would change. 専門家にしたところで = even the experts (are no different), 急いだとしたところで = even supposing we hurry. にしたところで attaches to a noun ('even ~ too'); としたところで often follows a verb ('even if we suppose ~'). The register is formal.
pitfalls: The conclusion is typically that it makes no difference — even this case does not escape it.
にしたところで takes a noun ('even ~ as well'); としたところで tends to follow a verb and means 'even supposing ~'.

examples.ja: 専門家にしたところで、この現象を完全に説明できるわけではない。
examples.en: Even the experts can't fully explain this phenomenon.
examples.f: ｜専門[せんもん]｜家[か]にしたところで、この｜現象[げんしょう]を｜完全[かんぜん]に｜説明[せつめい]できるわけではない。

examples.ja: 今から急いだとしたところで、開演には間に合わないだろう。
examples.en: Even supposing we hurry now, we won't make it in time for the start of the show.
examples.f: ｜今[いま]から｜急[いそ]いだとしたところで、｜開演[かいえん]には｜間に合[まにあ]わないだろう。

synonyms.note: にしても is the everyday 'even ~ / even if ~'; にしたところで is a heavier, more formal version stressing that it changes nothing.

related.note: にすれば takes a person's standpoint ('from ~'s view'); にしたところで concedes 'even ~ is no exception'.

title: 〜にして
meaning: only at/when (a notable stage); and at the same time; being both ~ and ~
summary: 〜にして is a formal, literary connector with two main senses. One marks a notable stage or degree — 五十歳にして = at (the age of) fifty, 今にして思えば = now that I look back. The other joins two qualities in one subject — 学者にして詩人 = a scholar and at the same time a poet. In both, にして links a noun to what is remarkable about that point or pairing. Context tells the senses apart.
pitfalls: Formal and literary; it would sound archaic or lofty in casual speech.
One sense marks a striking stage or degree ('only at ~'); the other means 'being both A and B' — context disambiguates.
Do not confuse it with にしては ('for ~, considering ~') or にしても ('even ~'); those are different compounds.

examples.ja: 彼は五十歳にして、ようやく自分の天職を見つけた。
examples.en: At fifty, he at last found his true calling.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜五[ご]｜十[じゅう]｜歳[さい]にして、ようやく｜自分[じぶん]の｜天職[てんしょく]を｜見[み]つけた。

examples.ja: 彼女は優れた研究者にして、二児の母でもある。
examples.en: She is an accomplished researcher and, at the same time, a mother of two.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜優[すぐ]れた｜研究[けんきゅう]｜者[しゃ]にして、｜二[に]｜児[じ]の｜母[はは]でもある。

related.note: にしては means 'for ~, considering ~' and judges against a standard; the bare にして marks a notable stage or a pairing of qualities.
こそ singles out and emphasizes a word; にして in its 'only at ~' sense likewise highlights a stage as pivotal, but formally and with a noun.

title: 〜にしてみれば
meaning: from ~'s standpoint; as far as ~ is concerned
summary: 〜にしてみれば takes up a person or group and imagines how things look or feel from their side — 'from ~'s point of view, as far as ~ is concerned'. 親にしてみれば = from a parent's standpoint, 言われた側にしてみれば = from the standpoint of the one it was said to. It typically foregrounds that party's feelings, which may differ from how others see it. The person is marked with に.
pitfalls: It adopts a person's perspective and imagines their feelings; what follows is how things seem to them, not neutral fact.
The one whose viewpoint is taken is marked with に: 私にしてみれば, not 私がしてみれば.

examples.ja: 親にしてみれば、子供はいくつになっても心配なものだ。
examples.en: From a parent's standpoint, a child is a source of worry no matter how old they get.
examples.f: ｜親[おや]にしてみれば、｜子供[こども]はいくつになっても｜心配[しんぱい]なものだ。

examples.ja: 軽い冗談のつもりでも、言われた側にしてみれば傷つくこともある。
examples.en: Even if it's meant as a light joke, from the standpoint of the person it's aimed at, it can hurt.
examples.f: ｜軽[かる]い｜冗談[じょうだん]のつもりでも、｜言[い]われた｜側[がわ]にしてみれば｜傷[きず]つくこともある。

synonyms.note: にすれば is a near-synonym for taking someone's standpoint; にしてみれば leans a little more into imagining how they feel.

related.note: に言わせれば voices the opinion a person would actually state; にしてみれば imagines how a situation feels to them.
にとって marks 'for ~' as the one something matters to; にしてみれば imagines the situation from inside their perspective.

title: 〜に忍びない
meaning: cannot bring oneself to; too painful (out of pity or attachment) to ~
summary: 〜に忍びない expresses that one cannot bring oneself to do something because it is too heartbreaking or pitiful — 'cannot bear to ~'. 捨てるに忍びない = can't bear to throw away, 見るに忍びない = too pitiful to watch. The inability is emotional, springing from compassion or attachment, not from physical impossibility. It follows a dictionary-form verb and is formal and literary.
pitfalls: The 'cannot' is emotional — too pitiful or dear to bear — not physical inability.
It follows a dictionary-form verb (捨てるに忍びない); it is a written, formal expression.

examples.ja: 長年連れ添った道具だと思うと、捨てるに忍びない。
examples.en: When I think of it as a tool that has been with me for years, I can't bring myself to throw it away.
examples.f: ｜長年[ながねん]｜連れ添[つれそ]った｜道具[どうぐ]だと｜思[おも]うと、｜捨[す]てるに｜忍[しの]びない。

examples.ja: 被災地の惨状は、まさに見るに忍びないものだった。
examples.en: The devastation of the disaster area was truly too painful to look at.
examples.f: ｜被災[ひさい]｜地[ち]の｜惨状[さんじょう]は、まさに｜見[み]るに｜忍[しの]びないものだった。

related.note: 見るに耐えない means it is so unpleasant you can't keep watching; 見るに忍びない means it is too pitiful or heartbreaking to watch.

title: 〜に即して
meaning: in accordance with; in line with (facts, reality, rules)
summary: 〜に即して means acting in keeping with a concrete standard such as the facts, reality, law, or one's experience — 'in line with ~, grounded in ~'. 現実に即した対策 = measures grounded in reality, 規則に即して判断する = judge in accordance with the rules. It stresses fitting one's response to how things actually are, not to abstract ideals. The adnominal form is に即した, and the register is formal.
pitfalls: It pairs with concrete standards — 実情・現実・事実・法律・経験 — not with personal wishes or feelings.
Distinguish it from に沿って ('along / following a line, plan, or intention'); 即して means conforming to the actual facts.

examples.ja: 理想論ではなく、現実に即した対策が求められている。
examples.en: What's needed are measures grounded in reality, not idealistic arguments.
examples.f: ｜理想[りそう]｜論[ろん]ではなく、｜現実[げんじつ]に｜即[そく]した｜対策[たいさく]が｜求[もと]められている。

examples.ja: 規則に即して、公平に処分を決めるべきだ。
examples.en: The penalty should be decided fairly, in accordance with the rules.
examples.f: ｜規則[きそく]に｜即[そく]して、｜公平[こうへい]に｜処分[しょぶん]を｜決[き]めるべきだ。

synonyms.note: に照らして checks something against a standard or precedent to judge it; に即して means shaping one's response to fit the actual facts.

related.note: に基づいて uses something as a foundation or grounds to build on; に即して means staying faithful to the concrete facts or rules.
に沿って means following along a line, plan, or wish; に即して means conforming to how things actually are.

title: 〜に耐える・〜に耐えない
kana: にたえる・にたえない
meaning: worth doing / holds up to ~ ; unbearable to ~ ; filled with (emotion)
summary: 〜に耐える means something is solid enough to be worth doing or can withstand scrutiny — 鑑賞に耐える = worth appreciating, 批判に耐える = holds up to criticism. Its negative 〜に耐えない has two uses: with 見る・聞く it means 'too awful to ~' (見るに耐えない = unbearable to watch), and with emotion nouns like 感謝・感慨 it means 'filled with ~' (感謝の念に耐えない). It is formal, and に堪えない is the same word spelled differently.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋に耐える／に耐えない
pitfalls: 〜に耐える = 'worth ~ing / holds up to ~'; 〜に耐えない = 'unbearable to ~' (with 見る・聞く) or 'filled with ~' (with 感謝・感慨).
に堪えない is merely a different spelling of the same expression, not a separate pattern.

examples.ja: この作品は、大人の鑑賞にも耐える完成度だ。
examples.en: This work is polished enough to be worth appreciating even by adults.
examples.f: この｜作品[さくひん]は、｜大人[おとな]の｜鑑賞[かんしょう]にも｜耐[た]える｜完成[かんせい]｜度[ど]だ。

examples.ja: 彼らの口論は、とても聞くに耐えないものだった。
examples.en: Their quarrel was truly unbearable to listen to.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]らの｜口論[こうろん]は、とても｜聞[き]くに｜耐[た]えないものだった。

synonyms.note: に値する means 'is worth / deserves ~' as a positive judgment; に耐える means it is solid enough to hold up to something like appreciation.

related.note: に足りない means 'not worth ~ing / not enough to'; に耐えない means 'unbearable to ~' or 'filled with (emotion)'.
に忍びない is 'too pitiful to bear'; 見るに耐えない is 'too unpleasant to keep watching' — sympathy versus distaste.

title: 〜に足らない・〜に足りない
kana: にたらない・にたりない
meaning: not worth ~ing; not enough to warrant ~
summary: 〜に足りない (also 〜に足らない) says that something does not merit a certain response — 'not worth ~ing'. It often appears in set phrases: 取るに足りない = trivial, not worth taking up; 恐れるに足りない = not worth fearing. It follows a dictionary-form verb, and its affirmative counterpart is 〜に足る ('worth ~ing, enough to'). The register is formal.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋に足りない／に足らない
pitfalls: Common fixed forms are 取るに足りない ('trivial') and 恐れるに足りない ('nothing to fear'); it follows a dictionary-form verb.
The positive counterpart is 〜に足る ('worth ~ing / sufficient to').

examples.ja: そんな根拠のない噂は、取るに足りないものだ。
examples.en: A baseless rumor like that is trivial and not worth taking up.
examples.f: そんな｜根拠[こんきょ]のない｜噂[うわさ]は、｜取[と]るに｜足[た]りないものだ。

examples.ja: 君の実力なら、あの程度の相手など恐れるに足りない。
examples.en: With your ability, an opponent of that level is nothing to be afraid of.
examples.f: ｜君[きみ]の｜実力[じつりょく]なら、あの｜程度[ていど]の｜相手[あいて]など｜恐[おそ]れるに｜足[た]りない。

antonyms.note: に足る is the positive 'worth ~ing / enough to'; に足りない denies it — 'not worth ~ing'.

related.note: に値する means 'is worth / deserves ~'; に足りない says the opposite — it does not merit the response.
に耐えない means 'unbearable to ~' or 'filled with ~'; に足りない means 'not worth ~ing'.

title: 〜に足る・〜に足りる
meaning: worthy of; sufficient to; enough to warrant
summary: 〜に足る marks that something is worth doing or sufficient to justify a response — 信頼するに足る人物 = a person worthy of trust, 満足するに足る成果 = results good enough to be satisfied with. It attaches to a verb in dictionary form (or a noun) and is formal, written Japanese. The negative 〜に足りない ('not worth ~') is very common, especially in the fixed phrase 取るに足りない ('trivial, not worth mentioning').
pitfalls: The negative 〜に足りない means 'not worth ~'; 取るに足りない is a set phrase meaning 'trivial, insignificant'.
Attach it to the dictionary form: 信頼するに足る, not 信頼したに足る.

examples.ja: 彼はこの大役を任せるに足る人物だと思う。
examples.en: I think he is a person worthy of being entrusted with this major role.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]はこの｜大役[たいやく]を｜任[まか]せるに｜足[た]る｜人物[じんぶつ]だと｜思[おも]う。

examples.ja: その程度の失敗は、いちいち気にするに足りない。
examples.en: A failure of that degree isn't worth fretting over one by one.
examples.f: その｜程度[ていど]の｜失敗[しっぱい]は、いちいち｜気[き]にするに｜足[た]りない。

synonyms.note: に値する also means 'worth ~'; に足る is more literary and leans on 'sufficient to warrant'.
に恥じない frames worth as 'living up to (a name/standard)'; に足る frames it as 'good enough to justify (an action)'.

title: 〜に照らして
meaning: in light of; in view of; against (a standard)
summary: 〜に照らして takes an established standard — a law, rule, precedent, common sense, or past experience — and judges something against it. 法律に照らして = in light of the law, 判例に照らして = against precedent. It also appears as 〜に照らし合わせて ('cross-checking against'). This is formal, written Japanese used when weighing a case against a fixed criterion.
pitfalls: The reference must be a standard or criterion (law, rule, common sense, experience), not a literal light source.
に基づいて uses a standard as the foundation to build on; に照らして checks a case against a standard already in place.

examples.ja: これまでの判例に照らして、この訴えは認められないだろう。
examples.en: In light of precedent to date, this claim will likely not be upheld.
examples.f: これまでの｜判例[はんれい]に｜照[て]らして、この｜訴[うった]えは｜認[みと]められないだろう。

examples.ja: 現在の社会通念に照らせば、その発言は差別的だと言わざるを得ない。
examples.en: Judged against present-day social norms, that remark can only be called discriminatory.
examples.f: ｜現在[げんざい]の｜社会[しゃかい]｜通念[つうねん]に｜照[て]らせば、その｜発言[はつげん]は｜差別[さべつ]｜的[てき]だと｜言[い]わざるを｜得[え]ない。

synonyms.note: に基づいて takes a source as the basis to act on; に照らして compares a case against a standard to evaluate it.
に沿って means 'keeping in line with (a policy/wish)'; に照らして means 'evaluated against (a criterion)'.

related.note: に則って means 'following (rules) as one acts'; に照らして means 'checking something against (a standard)'.

title: 〜にとどまらず
meaning: not stopping at; not limited to; not only
summary: 〜にとどまらず says that something does not stop at the first item but extends further, to something larger or wider — 国内にとどまらず海外にも = not limited to the domestic market but reaching abroad too. It attaches to a noun or a plain-form clause, and the second clause typically widens the scope with も, まで, or a comparable marker. This is formal, written Japanese.
pitfalls: The point is that the scope reaches beyond the first item to something broader; the follow-up clause usually carries も／まで.
It stresses spatial or conceptual expansion, unlike a plain 'not only ~ but also' list.

examples.ja: 被害は一つの村にとどまらず、周辺の地域全体に広がった。
examples.en: The damage did not stop at one village but spread across the entire surrounding region.
examples.f: ｜被害[ひがい]は｜一[ひと]つの｜村[むら]にとどまらず、｜周辺[しゅうへん]の｜地域[ちいき]｜全体[ぜんたい]に｜広[ひろ]がった。

examples.ja: 彼の関心は音楽にとどまらず、絵画や文学にまで及んでいる。
examples.en: His interests do not stop at music but extend even to painting and literature.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜関心[かんしん]は｜音楽[おんがく]にとどまらず、｜絵画[かいが]や｜文学[ぶんがく]にまで｜及[およ]んでいる。

synonyms.note: のみならず is a general 'not only ~ but also'; にとどまらず specifically pictures the scope spilling beyond a boundary.
だけでなく is the everyday 'not only ~'; にとどまらず is formal and emphasizes reaching further out.

title: 〜に則って・〜に則り
kana: にのっとって・にのっとり
meaning: in accordance with (rules, tradition, procedure)
summary: 〜に則って means acting in conformity with an established norm — a law, rule, tradition, format, or set procedure. 伝統に則って = in keeping with tradition, 手続きに則り = following the proper procedure. The 〜に則り form is the more written, formal variant. Use it when behavior is deliberately made to conform to a recognized standard or custom.
pitfalls: The object is a norm — a rule, law, tradition, or procedure — not a physical path or line (that role belongs to に沿って).
It is formal, ceremonial language; everyday speech would use 〜どおりに or 〜に従って.

examples.ja: 式は古くからのしきたりに則って執り行われた。
examples.en: The ceremony was conducted in accordance with age-old custom.
examples.f: ｜式[しき]は｜古[ふる]くからのしきたりに｜則[のっと]って｜執り行[とりおこな]われた。

examples.ja: 契約は法律に則り、正式な手続きを踏んで結ばれた。
examples.en: The contract was concluded in accordance with the law, following the proper procedures.
examples.f: ｜契約[けいやく]は｜法律[ほうりつ]に｜則[のっと]り、｜正式[せいしき]な｜手続[てつづ]きを｜踏[ふ]んで｜結[むす]ばれた。

synonyms.note: に基づいて means 'grounded on (a source)'; に則って means 'conforming to (a rule or tradition)'.
に沿って can follow a path, wish, or policy; に則って specifically conforms to formal rules or custom.

title: 〜には当たらない
meaning: there's no need to; it's not worth (praising, being surprised, etc.)
summary: 〜には当たらない says a certain reaction is not warranted — there's no need to be surprised, impressed, or to blame someone. 驚くには当たらない = no need to be surprised, 非難するには当たらない = not something to condemn. It attaches to a dictionary-form verb, most often a verb of emotional reaction, and calmly dismisses that the reaction is called for.
pitfalls: It pairs typically with reaction verbs (驚く・感心する・褒める・非難する) and says the reaction is unwarranted, not that something 'doesn't apply'.
Use the dictionary form: 驚くには当たらない, not 驚いたには当たらない.

examples.ja: 彼が優勝したからといって、驚くには当たらない。実力どおりだ。
examples.en: Just because he won is no reason to be surprised — it's exactly what his ability warranted.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]が｜優勝[ゆうしょう]したからといって、｜驚[おどろ]くには｜当[あ]たらない。｜実力[じつりょく]どおりだ。

examples.ja: あの程度のミスなら、そう責めるには当たらないよ。
examples.en: For a slip of that degree, there's really no need to blame him so harshly.
examples.f: あの｜程度[ていど]のミスなら、そう｜責[せ]めるには｜当[あ]たらないよ。

synonyms.note: には及ばない also means 'no need to', but is a shade more about sparing effort; には当たらない dismisses an emotional reaction as unwarranted.
ことはない is the everyday 'there's no need to ~'; には当たらない is formal and typically follows reaction verbs.

title: 〜には及ばない
meaning: there's no need to; not a match for; falls short of
summary: 〜には及ばない has two senses. After a dictionary-form verb it means 'there's no need to ~' — 心配するには及ばない = no need to worry. After a noun it means 'does not measure up to / is no match for' — 彼の腕には及ばない = not up to his skill.
