Both trace to the core idea of 'not reaching': either the action isn't necessary, or one side falls short of the other.
pitfalls: Two senses: 'no need to' (after a verb) versus 'no match for / falls short of' (after a noun) — context decides which.
In the 'no need' sense it is politely dismissive of trouble or worry, often softening an offer.

examples.ja: わざわざ迎えに来ていただくには及びません。自分で行けますので。
examples.en: There's no need to go out of your way to come pick me up; I can get there myself.
examples.f: わざわざ｜迎[むか]えに｜来[き]ていただくには｜及[およ]びません。｜自分[じぶん]で｜行[い]けますので。

examples.ja: 努力は認めるが、彼の技術はまだ一流には及ばない。
examples.en: I acknowledge the effort, but his skill still doesn't reach the first rank.
examples.f: ｜努力[どりょく]は｜認[みと]めるが、｜彼[かれ]の｜技術[ぎじゅつ]はまだ｜一流[いちりゅう]には｜及[およ]ばない。

synonyms.note: には当たらない says an emotional reaction is unwarranted; には及ばない (no-need sense) says the trouble or worry is unnecessary.
ことはない plainly says 'no need to ~'; には及ばない is more formal and can also mean 'no match for'.

title: 〜に恥じない
meaning: worthy of; living up to (a name or standard)
summary: 〜に恥じない literally means 'not ashamed before ~', and describes conduct or achievement that lives up to a name, title, or standard. プロに恥じない仕事 = work worthy of a professional, 名に恥じない = living up to the name. It attaches to a noun and usually modifies a following noun. This is formal, often used in praise or in statements of resolve.
pitfalls: It measures conduct against a title or standard you should live up to — 'not putting X to shame' — rather than plainly 'not embarrassing'.
It commonly sits before a noun: 王者に恥じない戦い, not a standalone predicate in most uses.

examples.ja: 王者の名に恥じない、堂々とした試合ぶりだった。
examples.en: It was a commanding performance, worthy of the name of champion.
examples.f: ｜王者[おうじゃ]の｜名[な]に｜恥[は]じない、｜堂々[どうどう]とした｜試合[しあい]ぶりだった。

examples.ja: 彼女はプロに恥じない責任感を持って仕事に取り組んでいる。
examples.en: She approaches her work with a sense of responsibility worthy of a professional.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]はプロに｜恥[は]じない｜責任[せきにん]｜感[かん]を｜持[も]って｜仕事[しごと]に｜取り組[とりく]んでいる。

synonyms.note: に足る means 'good enough to justify (an action)'; に恥じない means 'living up to (a name or standard)'.
に値する means 'worth ~, deserving of'; に恥じない frames worth as not disgracing a title one bears.

title: 〜には無理がある
meaning: is a stretch; is unreasonable; is far-fetched
summary: 〜には無理がある points out that a claim, plan, or interpretation is a stretch — it doesn't quite hold up or can't reasonably be pushed through. その説明には無理がある = that explanation is a stretch, 日程には無理がある = the schedule is unworkable. It attaches to a noun (or a nominalized clause with のに) and calmly registers that something is overreaching or forced.
structure: Verb［plain form］＋のには無理がある
pitfalls: It says a reasoning, plan, or interpretation is forced or overreaching — not that a task is physically hard (that would be plain 無理だ).
Often used to gently reject an argument as far-fetched: 〜と考えるには無理がある.

examples.ja: その言い訳には少し無理があるように思う。
examples.en: That excuse strikes me as a bit of a stretch.
examples.f: その｜言い訳[いいわけ]には｜少[すこ]し｜無理[むり]があるように｜思[おも]う。

examples.ja: 短い期間で全部終わらせようという計画には無理があった。
examples.en: The plan to finish everything in such a short span was unreasonable from the start.
examples.f: ｜短[みじか]い｜期間[きかん]で｜全部[ぜんぶ]｜終[お]わらせようという｜計画[けいかく]には｜無理[むり]があった。

title: 〜に引き換え
meaning: in stark contrast to; unlike
summary: 〜に引き換え sets two things side by side and draws a sharp, often evaluative contrast — one side clearly better or worse than the other. 兄に引き換え弟は… = unlike the older brother, the younger one… It attaches to a noun (or なの＋に引き換え after a clause). Unlike the neutral に対して, 〜に引き換え carries the speaker's judgment that the two differ markedly.
pitfalls: It carries a subjective, evaluative tone (one side is better or worse); に対して by contrast is a neutral juxtaposition.
Both compared items should be comparable in kind — two people, two years, two situations.

examples.ja: 去年の記録的な猛暑にひきかえ、今年の夏は驚くほど過ごしやすい。
examples.en: In stark contrast to last year's record heat, this summer is surprisingly pleasant.
examples.f: ｜去年[きょねん]の｜記録[きろく]｜的[てき]な｜猛暑[もうしょ]にひきかえ、｜今年[ことし]の｜夏[なつ]は｜驚[おどろ]くほど｜過[す]ごしやすい。

examples.ja: よく働く姉にひきかえ、弟はいつも遊んでばかりいる。
examples.en: Unlike his hard-working older sister, the younger brother is always just goofing off.
examples.f: よく｜働[はたら]く｜姉[あね]にひきかえ、｜弟[おとうと]はいつも｜遊[あそ]んでばかりいる。

synonyms.note: に反して means 'contrary to (an expectation)'; に引き換え contrasts two comparable things with an evaluative slant.
に対して is a neutral 'whereas / in contrast'; に引き換え adds the speaker's judgment that one side compares poorly.

title: 〜にまつわる
meaning: related to; surrounding; entwined with
summary: 〜にまつわる connects a topic to the stories, legends, troubles, or memories entangled around it. お金にまつわるトラブル = money-related trouble, 神社にまつわる伝説 = a legend surrounding the shrine. It attaches to a noun and modifies a following noun. Richer than a plain について, it suggests things bound up with or clustered around the topic.
pitfalls: It modifies a following noun (にまつわる話・伝説・問題) and suggests things entwined around a topic, not a neutral 'about'.
Typical companions are 話・伝説・エピソード・思い出・争い — nouns for stories or entanglements.

examples.ja: この古い城には、悲しい恋にまつわる伝説が残っている。
examples.en: A legend surrounding a tragic love still clings to this old castle.
examples.f: この｜古[ふる]い｜城[しろ]には、｜悲[かな]しい｜恋[こい]にまつわる｜伝説[でんせつ]が｜残[のこ]っている。

examples.ja: 遺産をめぐって、お金にまつわる争いが親族のあいだで起きた。
examples.en: A money-related dispute over the inheritance broke out among the relatives.
examples.f: ｜遺産[いさん]をめぐって、お｜金[かね]にまつわる｜争[あらそ]いが｜親族[しんぞく]のあいだで｜起[お]きた。

synonyms.note: について is a neutral 'about, concerning'; にまつわる implies stories or troubles entangled around the topic.
に関わる means 'affecting / having a bearing on'; にまつわる means 'associated with, woven around'.

title: 〜にもほどがある
meaning: there's a limit to; ~ goes too far
summary: 〜にもほどがある is a sharp criticism that some behavior has crossed the bounds of what's acceptable — 冗談にもほどがある = there's a limit to joking, 失礼にもほどがある = that's rude beyond all limits. It attaches to a noun, adjective, or plain-form verb. The tone is emotional and reproachful, saying the person has gone well past a reasonable line.
structure: Verb［plain form］／い-adjective／な-adjective＋にもほどがある
pitfalls: It is a pointed rebuke that something is excessive, not a neutral statement that 'there is a limit'.
Common with 冗談・失礼・非常識・勝手 — nouns naming the excess being criticized.

examples.ja: 人の日記を勝手に読むなんて、失礼にもほどがある。
examples.en: Reading someone's diary without permission — there's a limit to how rude you can be.
examples.f: ｜人[ひと]の｜日記[にっき]を｜勝手[かって]に｜読[よ]むなんて、｜失礼[しつれい]にもほどがある。

examples.ja: いくら忙しいからって、何日も連絡しないなんて、ひどいにもほどがある。
examples.en: No matter how busy you are, going days without any contact is awful beyond all reason.
examples.f: いくら｜忙[いそが]しいからって、｜何[なん]｜日[にち]も｜連絡[れんらく]しないなんて、ひどいにもほどがある。

related.note: すぎる plainly marks 'too much'; にもほどがある adds indignation that a line of decency has been crossed.

title: 〜にも増して
meaning: even more than; more than ever
summary: 〜にも増して means 'surpassing even ~' — the current degree exceeds a reference point that was already high. 例年にも増して = even more than in an ordinary year, 以前にも増して = more than before. The set phrase 何にも増して means 'more than anything else'. It attaches to a noun and is formal, written Japanese.
pitfalls: It says the new degree tops an already high benchmark, not a plain 'more than' comparison.
何にも増して is a fixed phrase meaning 'above all else, more than anything'.

examples.ja: 今年は例年にも増して、桜の花が見事に咲いた。
examples.en: This year the cherry blossoms bloomed even more splendidly than in a normal year.
examples.f: ｜今年[ことし]は｜例年[れいねん]にも｜増[ま]して、｜桜[さくら]の｜花[はな]が｜見事[みごと]に｜咲[さ]いた。

examples.ja: 合格の知らせを聞いて、本人にも増して両親が喜んでいた。
examples.en: On hearing the news that he'd passed, his parents were even more delighted than he was.
examples.f: ｜合格[ごうかく]の｜知[し]らせを｜聞[き]いて、｜本人[ほんにん]にも｜増[ま]して｜両親[りょうしん]が｜喜[よろこ]んでいた。

synonyms.note: 以上に means 'more than (a standard), beyond'; にも増して stresses topping a benchmark that was itself already high.
より marks a plain comparison ('than'); にも増して is formal and implies surpassing an already elevated level.

title: 〜によらず
meaning: regardless of; irrespective of; not depending on
summary: 〜によらず means an outcome is not determined by, and holds regardless of, the noun it marks. 年齢によらず = regardless of age, 男女によらず = irrespective of gender. It often appears in the fixed frame 〜のいかんによらず ('whatever the ~ may be'). This is formal, written Japanese, common in rules, policies, and official statements.
pitfalls: It means 'not decided by / regardless of' — close to にかかわらず but stressing that the factor plays no determining role.
The set frame 〜のいかんによらず ('whatever the ~') is very common in formal writing.

examples.ja: 当社では、年齢や性別によらず、実力で評価する。
examples.en: At our company we assess people on ability, regardless of age or gender.
examples.f: ｜当社[とうしゃ]では、｜年齢[ねんれい]や｜性別[せいべつ]によらず、｜実力[じつりょく]で｜評価[ひょうか]する。

examples.ja: 理由のいかんによらず、暴力は決して許されない。
examples.en: Whatever the reason may be, violence is never permissible.
examples.f: ｜理由[りゆう]のいかんによらず、｜暴力[ぼうりょく]は｜決[けっ]して｜許[ゆる]されない。

synonyms.note: にかかわらず is the general 'regardless of'; によらず stresses that the factor does not govern the result.
いかんにかかわらず and のいかんによらず overlap closely; both mean 'whatever the ~ may be' in formal writing.

title: 〜の至り
meaning: the height of; extreme (emotion); the utmost of
summary: 〜の至り expresses that an emotion is felt at its utmost — 光栄の至り = the greatest of honors, 感激の至り = deeply moved beyond words. It attaches to a small set of emotion nouns and belongs to very formal, ceremonial or humble speech. The fixed phrase 若気の至り ('the folly of youth') is a notable exception, naming a rash act driven by youthful impulse.
pitfalls: It attaches to a limited set of emotion nouns (光栄・感激・恐縮・赤面); it is not a freely productive pattern.
若気の至り is a set idiom meaning 'a blunder of youthful impulsiveness', not an emotion at its peak.

examples.ja: このような名誉ある賞をいただき、光栄の至りでございます。
examples.en: To receive such an honorable award is the greatest of honors for me.
examples.f: このような｜名誉[めいよ]ある｜賞[しょう]をいただき、｜光栄[こうえい]の｜至[いた]りでございます。

examples.ja: 若気の至りとはいえ、当時の言動は今思うと恥ずかしい。
examples.en: Though it was the folly of youth, my words and deeds back then are embarrassing to recall now.
examples.f: ｜若気[わかげ]の｜至[いた]りとはいえ、｜当時[とうじ]の｜言動[げんどう]は｜今[いま]｜思[おも]うと｜恥[は]ずかしい。

synonyms.note: の極み marks a state pushed to its limit (贅沢・混乱); の至り is reserved for emotions at their peak in humble set phrases.
限りだ also expresses an emotion at its extreme (うれしい限りだ); の至り is more formal and attaches to emotion nouns.

title: 〜の極み
meaning: the extreme of; the height of; the epitome of
summary: 〜の極み marks a state pushed to its absolute limit — 贅沢の極み = the height of luxury, 疲労の極み = utter exhaustion, 混乱の極み = total chaos. It attaches to a noun naming a condition and says that condition has reached its furthest point. This is formal, written or dramatic Japanese, used for both positive and negative extremes.
pitfalls: It attaches to nouns naming a state or condition (贅沢・混乱・疲労・感激) and pushes it to its limit.
の至り is largely confined to emotions in humble set phrases; の極み ranges more widely, over states good and bad.

examples.ja: 毎晩高級店で食事をするとは、贅沢の極みだ。
examples.en: Dining at high-end restaurants every night is the height of extravagance.
examples.f: ｜毎晩[まいばん]｜高級[こうきゅう]｜店[てん]で｜食事[しょくじ]をするとは、｜贅沢[ぜいたく]の｜極[きわ]みだ。

examples.ja: 準備不足のまま本番を迎え、会場は混乱の極みに達した。
examples.en: Going into the main event underprepared, the venue descended into utter chaos.
examples.f: ｜準備[じゅんび]｜不足[ふそく]のまま｜本番[ほんばん]を｜迎[むか]え、｜会場[かいじょう]は｜混乱[こんらん]の｜極[きわ]みに｜達[たっ]した。

synonyms.note: の至り is limited to peak emotions in humble set phrases; の極み covers a wider range of states, positive or negative.
この上ない means 'nothing surpasses it, the utmost'; の極み names the extreme point of a specific state as a noun.

title: 〜のなんのって
meaning: so ~ that words fail; incredibly ~
summary: 〜のなんのって is a very colloquial way to exaggerate a degree — 寒いのなんのって = it was so unbelievably cold, words can't capture it. It follows an い-adjective or plain-form verb and is usually left trailing, inviting the listener to imagine just how extreme it was. This belongs to casual, spoken Japanese and carries a lively, emphatic tone.
pitfalls: This is casual spoken emphasis; it clashes with the formal register of の極み or の至り.
It often trails off after the exaggeration, leaving the degree to the listener's imagination.

examples.ja: 山頂の風が冷たいのなんのって、じっと立っていられなかった。
examples.en: The wind at the summit was so unbelievably cold I couldn't stand still.
examples.f: ｜山頂[さんちょう]の｜風[かぜ]が｜冷[つめ]たいのなんのって、じっと｜立[た]っていられなかった。

examples.ja: 久しぶりに全力で走ったら、翌日の筋肉痛が痛いのなんのって。
examples.en: After running full-out for the first time in ages, the next day's muscle soreness was something else.
examples.f: ｜久[ひさ]しぶりに｜全力[ぜんりょく]で｜走[はし]ったら、｜翌日[よくじつ]の｜筋肉[きんにく]｜痛[つう]が｜痛[いた]いのなんのって。

synonyms.note: ことか is an emotive 'how ~!' that works in writing; のなんのって is strictly casual, spoken exaggeration.

title: 〜のやら〜のやら
meaning: whether ~ or ~ (I can't tell which)
summary: 〜のやら〜のやら pairs two possibilities — often opposites — to say the speaker can't tell which is the case. 本当なのやら嘘なのやら = whether it's true or a lie, no telling. It joins two plain-form clauses and frequently takes the shape 〜のやら〜ないのやら ('whether ~ or not'). The tone conveys genuine puzzlement or resignation.
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋のやら＋Sentence［plain form］＋のやら
pitfalls: It lines up two (often opposite) possibilities to say which one holds is unknown; a common shape is 〜のやら〜ないのやら.
The overall feeling is puzzlement or resignation, not a neutral 'either A or B' choice.

examples.ja: 彼が本気なのやら冗談なのやら、表情からは全く読み取れない。
examples.en: Whether he's serious or joking I can't tell in the least from his expression.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]が｜本気[ほんき]なのやら｜冗談[じょうだん]なのやら、｜表情[ひょうじょう]からは｜全[まった]く｜読み取[よみと]れない。

examples.ja: 息子は勉強しているのやらしていないのやら、部屋から物音一つしない。
examples.en: Whether my son is studying or not I have no idea — not a single sound comes from his room.
examples.f: ｜息子[むすこ]は｜勉強[べんきょう]しているのやらしていないのやら、｜部屋[へや]から｜物音[ものおと]｜一[ひと]つしない。

synonyms.note: the single 〜のやら／ものやら expresses one unresolved question; the paired 〜のやら〜のやら weighs two possibilities against each other.

title: 〜のやら・〜ものやら・〜ことやら
kana: のやら・ものやら・ことやら
romaji: no yara / mono yara / koto yara
meaning: I wonder; who knows (uncertainty)
summary: 〜のやら, and its variants 〜ものやら and 〜ことやら, attach to an embedded question to express 'who knows / I wonder', with a musing and often faintly worried tone. どうしたものやら = I have no idea what to do, どこにいることやら = who knows where he is. It usually follows a question word such as どう, どこ, いつ, or 何, and belongs to reflective, slightly literary speech.
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋のやら／ものやら／ことやら
pitfalls: It follows a single embedded question and means 'who knows ~'; ものやら・ことやら add a musing or worried undertone.
It typically comes after a question word (どう・どこ・いつ・何) rather than a yes/no clause.

examples.ja: こんな難題を、これからどう解決したものやら見当もつかない。
examples.en: I haven't the faintest idea how I'm going to solve such a hard problem from here.
examples.f: こんな｜難題[なんだい]を、これからどう｜解決[かいけつ]したものやら｜見当[けんとう]もつかない。

examples.ja: 家を出たきりの息子は、今どこで何をしていることやら。
examples.en: My son, who left home and never returned — who knows where he is or what he's doing now.
examples.f: ｜家[いえ]を｜出[で]たきりの｜息子[むすこ]は、｜今[いま]どこで｜何[なに]をしていることやら。

synonyms.note: the paired 〜のやら〜のやら weighs two possibilities; the single 〜のやら／ものやら muses over one open question.
ことか exclaims 'how ~!' with feeling; ことやら wonders aloud with unresolved uncertainty.

title: 〜はおろか
meaning: let alone; not to mention; to say nothing of
summary: 〜はおろか says that not only the greater or more obvious thing but even a more basic one is (typically) not the case. 漢字はおろか、ひらがなも書けない = can't write even hiragana, let alone kanji. It attaches to a noun, and the second, more basic item is usually marked with も, さえ, or すら, in a generally negative sentence. This is formal, written Japanese.
pitfalls: The second item (marked も／さえ／すら) is the more basic case, and the whole sentence is usually negative.
It attaches to nouns; the emphasis is 'even the obvious thing doesn't hold, never mind the harder one'.

examples.ja: 大けがをして、走ることはおろか、歩くことさえままならない。
examples.en: After the serious injury, he can't even walk, let alone run.
examples.f: ｜大[だい]けがをして、｜走[はし]ることはおろか、｜歩[ある]くことさえままならない。

examples.ja: その村には電気はおろか、水道すら引かれていない。
examples.en: That village has no running water, let alone electricity.
examples.f: その｜村[むら]には｜電気[でんき]はおろか、｜水道[すいどう]すら｜引[ひ]かれていない。

synonyms.note: どころか can also reverse an expectation ('far from ~'); はおろか strictly builds a 'not even the basic thing' scale.
のみならず adds 'not only ~ but also' in positive statements; はおろか works in negatives ('let alone').

related.note: さえ ('even') often marks the second, basic item in a はおろか sentence.

title: 〜ばこそ
meaning: precisely because ~; it is only because ~
summary: 〜ばこそ gives the true, emphatic reason behind a result — 'it is precisely because ~ that…'. 君を思えばこそ = it is precisely because I care about you. It attaches to the ば-conditional form (であればこそ after a noun or な-adjective), and the reason is usually a positive or heartfelt one. This is formal, somewhat literary Japanese, more elevated than からこそ.
pitfalls: It highlights the genuine underlying reason for a (usually positive) outcome; it is more formal and emphatic than からこそ.
The reason clause is often followed by のだ／んです, underscoring the explanation.

examples.ja: 君の将来を思えばこそ、あえて厳しいことを言うのだ。
examples.en: It is precisely because I care about your future that I dare to say these harsh things.
examples.f: ｜君[きみ]の｜将来[しょうらい]を｜思[おも]えばこそ、あえて｜厳[きび]しいことを｜言[い]うのだ。

examples.ja: 家族の支えがあればこそ、私は困難を乗り越えられた。
examples.en: It was only because I had my family's support that I could overcome the hardships.
examples.f: ｜家族[かぞく]の｜支[ささ]えがあればこそ、｜私[わたし]は｜困難[こんなん]を｜乗り越[のりこ]えられた。

synonyms.note: からこそ is the everyday emphatic 'precisely because'; ばこそ is more formal and literary.
こそ alone emphasizes a noun ('this very ~'); ばこそ emphasizes a reason clause ('precisely because ~').

title: 〜はさておき
meaning: setting ~ aside; leaving ~ aside for now
summary: 〜はさておき sets one topic aside in order to move on to a more pressing or important one — 'leaving ~ aside, let's get to ~'. 冗談はさておき = joking aside, 建前はさておき = setting the official line aside. It attaches to a noun and is a common way to pivot from a lesser matter to the real point at hand.
pitfalls: It attaches directly to a noun (冗談はさておき), signalling a deliberate pivot to the main issue.
The item set aside is simply postponed as less urgent, not judged; it does not carry the critical 'neglecting' tone of 〜はそっちのけで.

examples.ja: 冗談はさておき、そろそろ本題に入りましょう。
examples.en: Joking aside, let's get down to the main topic.
examples.f: ｜冗談[じょうだん]はさておき、そろそろ｜本題[ほんだい]に｜入[はい]りましょう。

examples.ja: 味はさておき、この店は雰囲気だけは抜群にいい。
examples.en: Taste aside, this restaurant's atmosphere alone is outstanding.
examples.f: ｜味[あじ]はさておき、この｜店[みせ]は｜雰囲気[ふんいき]だけは｜抜群[ばつぐん]にいい。

synonyms.note: はともかく also brackets a matter off; はさておき leans more on 'setting it aside to move on to the main point'.

related.note: はそっちのけで is neglecting a duty to do something else and sounds critical; はさておき is a neutral shift of topic.

title: 〜はそっちのけで・〜をそっちのけで
kana: はそっちのけで・をそっちのけで
romaji: wa socchinoke de; o socchinoke de
meaning: neglecting; ignoring (one thing to do another)
summary: そっちのけ means shoving something off to the side, and 〜はそっちのけで / 〜をそっちのけで marks a person ignoring or neglecting something that deserves attention in order to throw themselves into something else. 宿題はそっちのけで = ignoring the homework. It carries a mildly critical tone toward the person doing the neglecting.
structure: Noun＋はそっちのけで／をそっちのけで
pitfalls: Casual in tone and usually critical: it faults someone for neglecting a duty in favour of something else.
Unlike 〜はさておき (a neutral pivot in topic), そっちのけ implies a responsibility is being wrongly abandoned.

examples.ja: 息子は宿題をそっちのけで、朝からずっとゲームをしている。
examples.en: Ignoring his homework, my son has been playing games all morning.
examples.f: ｜息子[むすこ]は｜宿題[しゅくだい]をそっちのけで、｜朝[あさ]からずっとゲームをしている。

examples.ja: 彼は自分の仕事はそっちのけで、同僚の相談にばかり乗っている。
examples.en: Neglecting his own work, he does nothing but give advice to his colleagues.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜自分[じぶん]の｜仕事[しごと]はそっちのけで、｜同僚[どうりょう]の｜相談[そうだん]にばかり｜乗[の]っている。

synonyms.note: もかまわず is doing something heedless of X; そっちのけ specifically means neglecting X in order to pour oneself into something else.

related.note: はさておき neutrally postpones a topic; はそっちのけで faults someone for abandoning what they should be doing.

title: 〜ばそれまでだ・〜たらそれまでだ
kana: ばそれまでだ・たらそれまでだ
romaji: ba sore made da; tara sore made da
meaning: if ~, then it's all over; if ~, that's the end of it
summary: 〜ばそれまでだ / 〜たらそれまでだ says that if a certain (usually bad) thing happens, that is the end of everything — there is nothing more to be done and any effort so far comes to nothing. 見つかればそれまでだ = if we're found out, it's all over. It stresses that a single event would render everything else pointless.
pitfalls: The condition is typically an undesirable event that would nullify everything; the point is finality, not just 'up until then'.
It is often paired with a preceding 'no matter how much ~' clause to underline that all the effort would be wasted.

examples.ja: どんなに貯金しても、病気で倒れればそれまでだ。
examples.en: No matter how much you save, if you fall ill it's all over.
examples.f: どんなに｜貯金[ちょきん]しても、｜病気[びょうき]で｜倒[たお]れればそれまでだ。

examples.ja: 大事な書類だから、なくしたらそれまでだよ。
examples.en: It's an important document, so if you lose it, that's the end of it.
examples.f: ｜大事[だいじ]な｜書類[しょるい]だから、なくしたらそれまでだよ。

related.note: までだ plays an action down as 'merely ~'; ばそれまでだ declares that a condition would bring everything to a dead end.

title: 〜はどうであれ
meaning: whatever ~ may be; no matter what ~ is
summary: 〜はどうであれ concedes a point — 'whatever X may be, no matter what X is' — and then asserts that the main clause holds regardless. 理由はどうであれ = whatever the reason, 結果はどうであれ = whatever the outcome. であれ is the concessive form of である, and the pattern dismisses the named factor as irrelevant to the conclusion.
pitfalls: Formal in register; であれ is the concessive form of である, not a request.
The main clause states something that stands firm regardless of the factor set aside before はどうであれ.

examples.ja: 理由はどうであれ、暴力は決して許されない。
examples.en: Whatever the reason, violence can never be excused.
examples.f: ｜理由[りゆう]はどうであれ、｜暴力[ぼうりょく]は｜決[けっ]して｜許[ゆる]されない。

examples.ja: 結果はどうであれ、最後まで全力を尽くすつもりだ。
examples.en: Whatever the outcome, I intend to give it my all to the very end.
examples.f: ｜結果[けっか]はどうであれ、｜最後[さいご]まで｜全力[ぜんりょく]を｜尽[つ]くすつもりだ。

synonyms.note: であれ is the general 'whatever/no matter' form; はどうであれ is the fixed frame 'whatever the ~ may be' built on どう.

related.note: ようが・ようと concedes over a verb ('no matter how one does'); はどうであれ concedes over a noun.
にせよ・にしろ means 'even if / whether ~ or'; はどうであれ specifically dismisses a noun as making no difference.

title: 〜羽目になる
meaning: to end up in (an unpleasant situation); to get stuck having to ~
summary: 羽目 is a tight spot, and 〜羽目になる marks ending up forced into an unwelcome situation — usually as a consequence of something one did or that went wrong. 払う羽目になった = ended up having to pay, 歩いて帰る羽目になる = get stuck walking home. The outcome is unwanted and often self-inflicted.
pitfalls: The result is a troublesome predicament you are stuck with, never a welcome outcome.
It attaches to a dictionary-form verb and most often appears in the past as 羽目になった.

examples.ja: 終電を逃して、駅から歩いて帰る羽目になった。
examples.en: I missed the last train and ended up having to walk home from the station.
examples.f: ｜終電[しゅうでん]を｜逃[のが]して、｜駅[えき]から｜歩[ある]いて｜帰[かえ]る｜羽目[はめ]になった。

examples.ja: 安請け合いしたせいで、休日も出勤する羽目になってしまった。
examples.en: Because I agreed too readily, I ended up having to go in to work even on my day off.
examples.f: ｜安請け合[やすうけあ]いしたせいで、｜休日[きゅうじつ]も｜出勤[しゅっきん]する｜羽目[はめ]になってしまった。

synonyms.note: ことになる reports a decision or arrangement neutrally; 羽目になる specifically means being stuck in an unwelcome predicament.

related.note: ざるを得ない focuses on being forced to do an action; 羽目になる describes ending up in the bad situation itself.

title: 〜びる・〜びた
meaning: to take on the look or quality of; -ish
summary: The suffix 〜びる turns a noun into a verb meaning 'to take on the look or quality of ~'. 大人びる = to come to seem grown-up, 古びる = to grow old and worn, 田舎びた = countrified. The 〜びた form modifies a following noun (大人びた顔つき). It describes something genuinely coming to resemble the base noun, often naturally over time.
pitfalls: 〜びる is limited to a small set of established words (大人びる, 古びる); it is not freely attachable to any noun.
It describes genuinely acquiring a quality, without the critical 'putting on airs' nuance of 〜ぶる.

examples.ja: 中学生になった姪は、急に大人びて見えるようになった。
examples.en: Now that she's a middle schooler, my niece has suddenly come to look grown-up.
examples.f: ｜中学生[ちゅうがくせい]になった｜姪[めい]は、｜急[きゅう]に｜大人[おとな]びて｜見[み]えるようになった。

examples.ja: 古びた木の看板が、店の長い歴史を物語っていた。
examples.en: The weathered wooden sign spoke of the shop's long history.
examples.f: ｜古[ふる]びた｜木[き]の｜看板[かんばん]が、｜店[みせ]の｜長[なが]い｜歴史[れきし]を｜物語[ものがた]っていた。

synonyms.note: めく also means 'to show signs of ~' (春めく); びる leans toward settling into a lasting look or quality.
っぽい is a colloquial, freely productive '-ish'; びる is a fixed verb suffix for a small set of words.

related.note: ぶる is to put on the airs of ~ (pretending); びる is to genuinely take on the quality.

title: 〜ぶり・〜っぷり
meaning: the manner or way in which one does something
summary: Attached to a verb stem or noun, 〜ぶり expresses the manner or style in which something is done — 話しぶり = way of speaking, 働きぶり = the way one works. The variant 〜っぷり is more vivid and colloquial, often admiring: 飲みっぷり = the (impressive) way someone drinks, 食べっぷり. It paints how an action is carried out.
pitfalls: This 〜ぶり ('manner of doing') is a different word from the time 〜ぶり meaning 'after an interval of' (三年ぶり = for the first time in three years).
〜っぷり is the emphatic, often admiring variant and stays casual in register.

examples.ja: 彼の堂々とした話しぶりに、聴衆はすっかり引き込まれた。
examples.en: The audience was completely drawn in by his confident manner of speaking.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜堂々[どうどう]とした｜話[はな]しぶりに、｜聴衆[ちょうしゅう]はすっかり｜引き込[ひきこ]まれた。

examples.ja: 見ていて気持ちがいいほどの、見事な飲みっぷりだった。
examples.en: It was such a splendid way of drinking that it felt good just to watch.
examples.f: ｜見[み]ていて｜気持[きも]ちがいいほどの、｜見事[みごと]な｜飲[の]みっぷりだった。

synonyms.note: 方 is the neutral 'how to / way of doing'; ぶり captures the observed style or manner of the doing.

title: 〜ぶる・〜ぶった
meaning: to act like; to put on the airs of; to affect
summary: The suffix 〜ぶる means to behave as though one were ~, to put on the airs of ~ — usually with a critical edge. 偉ぶる = to act self-important, 上品ぶる = to affect refinement, 学者ぶる = to play the scholar. The 〜ぶった form modifies a noun (もったいぶった態度). It implies the person is only pretending, not genuinely so.
pitfalls: 〜ぶる carries a disapproving nuance of putting on airs, unlike the neutral 〜びる ('to genuinely take on a quality').
Compare 大人ぶる (to affectedly act grown-up) with 大人びる (to genuinely seem grown-up).

examples.ja: 彼女は何も知らないくせに、専門家ぶって偉そうに解説を始めた。
examples.en: Though she knows nothing, she started explaining self-importantly, playing the expert.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜何[なに]も｜知[し]らないくせに、｜専門[せんもん]｜家[か]ぶって｜偉[えら]そうに｜解説[かいせつ]を｜始[はじ]めた。

examples.ja: もったいぶらないで、早く結果を教えてよ。
examples.en: Don't be so coy — just tell me the result already.
examples.f: もったいぶらないで、｜早[はや]く｜結果[けっか]を｜教[おし]えてよ。

synonyms.note: ふりをする is to pretend to be/do in a given instance; ぶる is a suffix implying a habitual affectation of character.

related.note: びる is to genuinely acquire a quality; ぶる is to merely put on its airs.
がましい labels something as bordering on / smacking of a (negative) quality; ぶる is deliberately affecting it.

title: 〜べからず・〜べからざる
kana: べからず・べからざる
meaning: must not; do not; prohibited (literary)
summary: 〜べからず is a stiff, literary prohibition — 'must not ~, do not ~' — descending from classical grammar. 立ち入るべからず = no entry, 初心忘るべからず = never forget your original resolve. It follows a dictionary-form verb (する becomes すべからず or するべからず). The attributive 〜べからざる modifies a noun: 許すべからざる行為 = an impermissible act.
pitfalls: Highly formal and dated — found on signs, in proverbs and set phrases, not everyday speech.
With する, both するべからず and the classical すべからず occur. Do not confuse べからず with the unrelated すべからく ('by all means, one ought to').

examples.ja: 「関係者以外、立ち入るべからず」と立て札に書かれていた。
examples.en: "No entry except for authorized persons," read the sign.
examples.f: 「｜関係[かんけい]｜者[しゃ]｜以外[いがい]、｜立ち入[たちい]るべからず」と｜立て札[たてふだ]に｜書[か]かれていた。

examples.ja: それは教育者として、決して許すべからざる行為だ。
examples.en: That is an act utterly impermissible for an educator.
examples.f: それは｜教育[きょういく]｜者[しゃ]として、｜決[けっ]して｜許[ゆる]すべからざる｜行為[こうい]だ。

synonyms.note: な is the blunt spoken 'don't ~'; べからず is the written, formal, archaic equivalent.
てはならない is a formal 'must not' usable in modern prose; べからず is more archaic and sign-like.

related.note: まじき is the literary 'unbecoming of ~' that modifies a noun, much like べからざる.
べきだ states what one should do; べからず is the negative, prohibitive side of the same べし root.

title: 〜べく
meaning: in order to ~; so as to ~ (literary)
summary: 〜べく expresses purpose in a formal, written register — 'in order to ~, so as to ~'. 目標を達成すべく = in order to achieve the goal. It follows a dictionary-form verb (する → すべく or するべく), and the main clause describes a deliberate action taken toward that aim. It is the literary cousin of ように and ために.
pitfalls: Formal and written; it does not appear in casual conversation.
With する, both すべく and するべく occur (すべく is more classical). The main clause should be a deliberate action taken for that purpose, not a spontaneous happening.

examples.ja: 新市場に参入すべく、会社は大規模な調査を開始した。
examples.en: In order to enter the new market, the company launched a large-scale survey.
examples.f: ｜新[しん]｜市場[しじょう]に｜参入[さんにゅう]すべく、｜会社[かいしゃ]は｜大[だい]｜規模[きぼ]な｜調査[ちょうさ]を｜開始[かいし]した。

examples.ja: 事故の原因を究明すべく、専門家チームが結成された。
examples.en: A team of experts was formed in order to determine the cause of the accident.
examples.f: ｜事故[じこ]の｜原因[げんいん]を｜究明[きゅうめい]すべく、｜専門[せんもん]｜家[か]チームが｜結成[けっせい]された。

synonyms.note: ために is the everyday 'in order to'; べく expresses the same purpose in a literary register.

related.note: べくして (as was bound to happen) uses the same べく root but expresses inevitability, not purpose.

title: 〜べくして
meaning: as was bound to happen; inevitably
summary: 〜べくして typically repeats the same verb — VるべくしてVた — to say that an outcome was bound to happen, the natural and inevitable result of the circumstances. 起こるべくして起こった事故 = an accident that was bound to happen. It frames the event as no accident of chance but the logical culmination of what came before.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋べくして＋Verb［same verb, た form］
pitfalls: It is almost always used with the same verb on both sides (勝つべくして勝った, 起こるべくして起こった).
It stresses inevitability given the conditions — the result was destined, not a coincidence.

examples.ja: 日頃の備えがあったからこそ、あのチームは勝つべくして勝ったのだ。
examples.en: It was precisely their everyday preparation that let that team win just as they were bound to.
examples.f: ｜日頃[ひごろ]の｜備[そな]えがあったからこそ、あのチームは｜勝[か]つべくして｜勝[か]ったのだ。

examples.ja: あれだけ無理を重ねれば、起こるべくして起こった不祥事と言えるだろう。
examples.en: With that much strain piled on, you could call it a scandal that was bound to happen.
examples.f: あれだけ｜無理[むり]を｜重[かさ]ねれば、｜起[お]こるべくして｜起[お]こった｜不祥事[ふしょうじ]と｜言[い]えるだろう。

related.note: べく uses the same root to express purpose ('in order to'); べくして expresses inevitability.

title: 〜べくもない
meaning: cannot possibly ~; there is no way to ~
summary: 〜べくもない is a literary way to say something is utterly impossible — 'cannot possibly ~, there is no way to ~'. 知るべくもない = there's no way one could know, 望むべくもない = cannot even be hoped for. It follows a dictionary-form verb and denies even the possibility, more emphatically and elegantly than ことができない.
pitfalls: Formal and literary; it conveys flat impossibility, stronger and more elegant than 〜ことができない.
It tends to attach to verbs of knowing, hoping, or comparing (知る, 望む, 比べる).

examples.ja: 当時の私に、その言葉の本当の意味など知るべくもなかった。
examples.en: There was no way that I, back then, could have known the true meaning of those words.
examples.f: ｜当時[とうじ]の｜私[わたし]に、その｜言葉[ことば]の｜本当[ほんとう]の｜意味[いみ]など｜知[し]るべくもなかった。

examples.ja: 一介の新人に、社長の真意を推し量るべくもない。
examples.en: A mere newcomer has no way of gauging the president's real intentions.
examples.f: ｜一介[いっかい]の｜新人[しんじん]に、｜社長[しゃちょう]の｜真意[しんい]を｜推し量[おしはか]るべくもない。

synonyms.note: ようがない ('there's no way to') is colloquial; べくもない is its literary counterpart.
かねる means one cannot bring oneself to / is unable to do; べくもない denies the very possibility outright.

related.note: べく shares the same root but expresses purpose ('in order to'), not impossibility.

title: 〜ほうがましだ
meaning: would rather ~; ~ is preferable (as the lesser evil)
summary: まし means 'better, less bad', so 〜ほうがましだ picks the lesser of two undesirable options — 'I'd rather ~ (than something even worse)'. 待たされるくらいなら帰ったほうがましだ = I'd rather go home than be kept waiting. Neither choice is good; the one marked with ほうがまし is simply the more bearable.
structure: Verb［dictionary form／た form］＋ほうがましだ
pitfalls: まし is 'the lesser evil', not positively good — do not read ほうがましだ as a happy preference like ほうがいい.
It usually stands against a worse alternative, often introduced by 〜くらいなら or 〜より.

examples.ja: あんな会社で働き続けるくらいなら、辞めたほうがましだ。
examples.en: If it means staying at a company like that, I'd rather quit.
examples.f: あんな｜会社[かいしゃ]で｜働[はたら]き｜続[つづ]けるくらいなら、｜辞[や]めたほうがましだ。

examples.ja: こんなまずい料理を出すなら、何も食べないほうがましだ。
examples.en: If they're going to serve food this bad, I'd rather eat nothing at all.
examples.f: こんなまずい｜料理[りょうり]を｜出[だ]すなら、｜何[なに]も｜食[た]べないほうがましだ。

synonyms.note: くらいなら names the worse option ('rather than ~'); it often pairs with ほうがましだ, which names the lesser evil chosen.

related.note: ほうがいい recommends a genuinely good course; ほうがましだ merely picks the less bad of two poor options.

title: 〜放題
meaning: as much as one likes; freely; unrestrained
summary: 〜放題 marks doing something freely and without limit — as much or as often as one pleases. 食べ放題 = all-you-can-eat, 飲み放題 = all-you-can-drink. Attached to a 〜たい stem it adds a 'to one's heart's content, however one likes' nuance that often turns critical: 言いたい放題 = saying whatever one pleases, 荒れ放題 = left to run wild.
pitfalls: With plain stems it advertises 'unlimited ~' (食べ放題); with 〜たい stems it often turns critical, 'doing as one selfishly pleases' (やりたい放題).
That second flavour implies neglect or excess left unchecked (伸び放題, 荒れ放題).

examples.ja: このプランなら、ドリンクが飲み放題で二時間楽しめる。
examples.en: With this plan, you get two hours with all-you-can-drink beverages.
examples.f: このプランなら、ドリンクが｜飲[の]み｜放題[ほうだい]で｜二[に]｜時間[じかん]｜楽[たの]しめる。

examples.ja: 何年も手入れをしなかった庭は、雑草が伸び放題になっていた。
examples.en: The garden, untended for years, had let its weeds grow completely wild.
examples.f: ｜何[なん]｜年[ねん]も｜手入[てい]れをしなかった｜庭[にわ]は、｜雑草[ざっそう]が｜伸[の]び｜放題[ほうだい]になっていた。

synonyms.note: まくる is doing an action intensely and repeatedly; 放題 is doing it without any restriction or limit.

title: 〜ほどのことではない
meaning: not worth ~ing over; not that serious a matter
summary: 〜ほどのことではない dismisses something as not serious enough to warrant a given reaction — 'it's not worth ~ing over, it's not that big a deal'. 泣くほどのことではない = not worth crying over, 病院に行くほどのことではない = nothing worth going to the hospital over. It plays the matter down as failing to rise to the level implied.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ほどのことではない
pitfalls: The reaction being dismissed is named by the verb before ほど (謝るほどのことではない = not worth apologizing over).
It downplays how serious something is, distinct from 〜までもない, which says an action is unnecessary because the point is obvious.

examples.ja: 少し擦りむいただけだから、病院に行くほどのことではない。
examples.en: It's just a little scrape, nothing worth going to the hospital over.
examples.f: ｜少[すこ]し｜擦[す]りむいただけだから、｜病院[びょういん]に｜行[い]くほどのことではない。

examples.ja: 誰にでもある失敗で、そんなに落ち込むほどのことではないよ。
examples.en: It's a mistake anyone could make — not something to get so down about.
examples.f: ｜誰[だれ]にでもある｜失敗[しっぱい]で、そんなに｜落ち込[おちこ]むほどのことではないよ。

synonyms.note: ことはない says 'there's no need to ~'; ほどのことではない says the matter doesn't rise to that level of seriousness.

related.note: までもない says an action is unneeded because the point is self-evident; ほどのことではない downplays how serious the matter is.

title: 〜まくる
meaning: to do like crazy; to do intensely and nonstop
summary: The suffix 〜まくる attaches to a verb stem and means to do that action intensely, repeatedly, and without restraint — 'to do like crazy, to do nonstop'. 遊びまくる = to party nonstop, 買いまくる = to buy up like mad. It is colloquial and emphasizes the sheer volume or vigour of the action.
pitfalls: Colloquial and emphatic; it suits casual speech, not formal writing.
It stresses doing something to excess or in great quantity with energy, not a single careful action.

examples.ja: 試験前は、とにかく過去問を解きまくるしかない。
examples.en: Before the exam, all you can do is just work through past papers like crazy.
examples.f: ｜試験[しけん]｜前[まえ]は、とにかく｜過去[かこ]｜問[とい]を｜解[と]きまくるしかない。

examples.ja: 旅行中は、珍しい景色を写真に撮りまくった。
examples.en: During the trip, I snapped photo after photo of the unusual scenery.
examples.f: ｜旅行[りょこう]｜中[ちゅう]は、｜珍[めずら]しい｜景色[けしき]を｜写真[しゃしん]に｜撮[と]りまくった。

synonyms.note: 放題 marks doing something freely without limit; まくる marks doing it intensely and over and over.

title: 〜まじき
meaning: unbecoming of; that must not be (literary)
summary: 〜まじき is a literary attributive meaning 'that must not be, unbecoming of' — it modifies a noun to condemn conduct as improper for a given role. 教師にあるまじき言動 = behaviour unbecoming of a teacher, 許すまじき罪 = an unforgivable crime. It descends from classical まじ (the negative of べし) and appears mostly in the set frame 〜にあるまじき.
pitfalls: Literary and largely frozen in 〜にあるまじき (＋ 行為／言動 etc.); it is not freely productive.
It labels conduct as improper for a role or status, so a person or position is usually named with に.

examples.ja: 情報を漏らすとは、公務員にあるまじき行為だ。
examples.en: Leaking information is conduct utterly unbecoming of a public servant.
examples.f: ｜情報[じょうほう]を｜漏[も]らすとは、｜公務員[こうむいん]にあるまじき｜行為[こうい]だ。

examples.ja: それは指導者としてあるまじき、無責任な発言だった。
examples.en: That was an irresponsible remark unworthy of a leader.
examples.f: それは｜指導[しどう]｜者[しゃ]としてあるまじき、｜無責任[むせきにん]な｜発言[はつげん]だった。

synonyms.note: べからず ends a clause as a prohibition; まじき modifies a noun attributively ('unbecoming ~').

related.note: べきだ ('should') is the affirmative; まじき functions as its literary negative counterpart.

title: 〜までだ・〜までのことだ
kana: までだ・までのことだ
romaji: made da; made no koto da
meaning: merely; simply; that's all; nothing more than
summary: 〜までだ / 〜までのことだ plays an action down as nothing more than what is stated. After a dictionary-form verb it expresses calm resolve — 'if it comes to that, I'll simply ~' (だめなら、やり直すまでだ = if it fails, I'll just do it over). After a た-form verb it justifies — 'I merely ~, that's all' (事実を述べたまでだ = I only stated the facts, nothing more).
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋までだ／までのことだ
Verb［た form］＋までだ／までのことだ
pitfalls: Dictionary form gives resolve ('I'll simply ~ if need be'); た-form gives justification ('I merely did ~, no more than that') — pick the form for the sense you want.
It downplays the action as the only, modest option, without exaggeration.

examples.ja: 話し合いで解決しないなら、法に訴えるまでだ。
examples.en: If it can't be settled by talking, then we'll simply take it to court.
examples.f: ｜話し合[はなしあ]いで｜解決[かいけつ]しないなら、｜法[ほう]に｜訴[うった]えるまでだ。

examples.ja: 責めているわけではない。ただ気づいたことを伝えたまでだ。
examples.en: I'm not blaming you; I merely passed on what I noticed, that's all.
examples.f: ｜責[せ]めているわけではない。ただ｜気[き]づいたことを｜伝[つた]えたまでだ。

synonyms.note: のみ is a formal 'only'; までだ frames the action as the sole, modest recourse or as nothing more than stated.

related.note: までもない ('no need to go so far as') is a separate までも construction, not this 'merely ~' までだ.
だけ limits scope to 'only ~'; までだ adds the nuance of a modest, final recourse or a bare justification.

title: 〜までもない・〜までもなく
kana: までもない・までもなく
romaji: made mo nai; made mo naku
meaning: there is no need to go so far as to ~; it goes without saying
summary: 〜までもない says an action isn't worth taking because the matter is too obvious or minor to require it — 'there's no need to go so far as to ~'. 言うまでもない = it goes without saying, わざわざ確認するまでもない = no need to bother checking. The 〜までもなく form links to a following clause: 説明するまでもなく = without even needing to explain.
pitfalls: It marks an action as unnecessary because the point is self-evident or trivial, not that the action is forbidden.
The very common 言うまでもない / 言うまでもなく means 'needless to say'.

examples.ja: こんな簡単な計算は、電卓を使うまでもない。
examples.en: A calculation this simple doesn't call for a calculator.
examples.f: こんな｜簡単[かんたん]な｜計算[けいさん]は、｜電卓[でんたく]を｜使[つか]うまでもない。

examples.ja: 言うまでもなく、締め切りを守ることが何より大切だ。
examples.en: It goes without saying that meeting the deadline matters above all.
examples.f: ｜言[い]うまでもなく、｜締め切[しめき]りを｜守[まも]ることが｜何[なに]より｜大切[たいせつ]だ。

synonyms.note: ことはない says 'there's no need to ~'; までもない adds that it isn't worth going so far because the point is obvious.
ほどのことではない downplays how serious a matter is; までもない says an action is superfluous given how self-evident the point is.

related.note: までだ ('merely ~') is a different までだ construction expressing resolve or justification.

title: 〜まみれ
meaning: covered in; smeared all over with
summary: 〜まみれ marks a surface covered or smeared all over with something — almost always a dirty, wet, or unpleasant substance. 泥まみれ = covered in mud, 汗まみれ = drenched in sweat, 血まみれ = covered in blood. It attaches to a noun and can extend to abstract unpleasantness clinging to someone: 借金まみれ = mired in debt.
pitfalls: The covering substance is typically unpleasant — mud, sweat, blood, dust, debt — not something clean or desirable.
It stresses being smeared all over a surface, unlike だらけ, which stresses 'full of lots of ~' (mistakes, people).

examples.ja: 子供たちは泥まみれになって、夕方まで川で遊んでいた。
examples.en: The children got covered in mud and played in the river until evening.
examples.f: ｜子供[こども]たちは｜泥[どろ]まみれになって、｜夕方[ゆうがた]まで｜川[かわ]で｜遊[あそ]んでいた。

examples.ja: 事業に失敗し、彼は借金まみれの生活を送っていた。
examples.en: Having failed in business, he was living a life mired in debt.
examples.f: ｜事業[じぎょう]に｜失敗[しっぱい]し、｜彼[かれ]は｜借金[しゃっきん]まみれの｜生活[せいかつ]を｜送[おく]っていた。

synonyms.note: だらけ stresses 'full of many ~'; まみれ stresses a substance smeared all over a surface.
ずくめ means 'nothing but ~' and can be positive (黒ずくめ, いいことずくめ); まみれ is always a dirty substance clinging to a surface.

title: まるっきり
meaning: completely; (not) at all; utterly
summary: まるっきり is a colloquial, emphatic adverb. Most often it pairs with a negative to mean 'not in the slightest' — まるっきり分からない = don't understand at all. With an affirmative it means 'completely, utterly', typically stressing total difference or total lack: まるっきり別人 = a completely different person, まるっきりの素人 = a total amateur. It is rougher and more spoken than まったく or まるで, and carries a note of exasperation.
pitfalls: This is casual, spoken language; in formal writing prefer まったく or 全く.
Unlike まるで, まるっきり does not mean 'as if'; it only intensifies (usually a negation or a statement of total difference).

examples.ja: 何度説明を聞いても、この理論はまるっきり理解できない。
examples.en: No matter how many times I hear it explained, I can't understand this theory at all.
examples.f: ｜何[なん]｜度[ど]｜説明[せつめい]を｜聞[き]いても、この｜理論[りろん]はまるっきり｜理解[りかい]できない。

examples.ja: 久しぶりに会った彼は、昔とまるっきり別人になっていた。
examples.en: Meeting him after a long time, he had become a completely different person from before.
examples.f: ｜久[ひさ]しぶりに｜会[あ]った｜彼[かれ]は、｜昔[むかし]とまるっきり｜別人[べつじん]になっていた。

synonyms.note: まるで also intensifies a negative ('not at all'), but additionally means 'as if ~'; まるっきり is purely emphatic and more colloquial.

related.note: とても〜ない says something is impossible/unthinkable; まるっきり〜ない simply denies it totally, without the 'no way could it' nuance.

title: 〜めく・〜めいた
meaning: to show signs of; to take on the air of; -like
summary: The suffix めく attaches to a limited set of nouns to form a verb meaning 'to take on the atmosphere or signs of ~': 春めく = to grow spring-like, 謎めく = to become mysterious, 皮肉めく = to sound sarcastic. The adnominal past form めいた modifies a following noun — 謎めいた話 = a mysterious story, 冗談めいた口調 = a joking tone. It is a somewhat literary way to say something gives off a certain air without fully being that thing.
pitfalls: めく attaches only to a fixed set of nouns (春・謎・皮肉・冗談 etc.); it is not freely productive with any noun.
In front of a noun the past form めいた is used (謎めいた話), not めくた or めく話.

examples.ja: 三月に入り、日差しもようやく春めいてきた。
examples.en: Now that March has arrived, the sunlight has finally taken on a spring-like feel.
examples.f: ｜三月[さんがつ]に｜入[はい]り、｜日差[ひざ]しもようやく｜春[はる]めいてきた。

examples.ja: 彼の謎めいた笑みの意味を、誰も読み取れなかった。
examples.en: No one could read the meaning of his enigmatic smile.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜謎[なぞ]めいた｜笑[え]みの｜意味[いみ]を、｜誰[だれ]も｜読み取[よみと]れなかった。

synonyms.note: らしい says something is typical of or behaves as befits its category; めく says it takes on the outward air of something it is not fully.
っぽい ('-ish') is colloquial and broadly productive; めく is literary and limited to set combinations.

title: 〜もさることながら
meaning: not only ~ but also (and even more so); ~ goes without saying, but
summary: Noun ＋ もさることながら concedes that the first item is indeed remarkable ('~ is of course a given / goes without saying'), then directs attention to a second item as being just as noteworthy or even more so. この店は味もさることながら接客もすばらしい = the food here is excellent, of course, but the service is wonderful too. It is a formal, written-flavored expression used to praise or highlight two points while foregrounding the second.
pitfalls: The weight falls on what comes after; the first item is presented as already understood, and the second is stressed as equally or more important.
It attaches to nouns; it is formal and belongs to careful speech or writing, not casual conversation.

examples.ja: この旅館は料理もさることながら、窓から望む景色が実に見事だ。
examples.en: At this inn the cuisine is superb, of course, but the view from the window is truly magnificent.
examples.f: この｜旅館[りょかん]は｜料理[りょうり]もさることながら、｜窓[まど]から｜望[のぞ]む｜景色[けしき]が｜実[じつ]に｜見事[みごと]だ。

examples.ja: 語学の習得には、才能もさることながら、日々の地道な努力が欠かせない。
examples.en: In mastering a language, talent matters of course, but steady daily effort is indispensable.
examples.f: ｜語学[ごがく]の｜習得[しゅうとく]には、｜才能[さいのう]もさることながら、｜日々[ひび]の｜地道[じみち]な｜努力[どりょく]が｜欠[か]かせない。

synonyms.note: のみならず simply adds 'not only A but also B'; もさることながら additionally treats A as an acknowledged given and spotlights B.
ばかりか adds a further, often surprising item; もさることながら balances two notable points rather than escalating.

title: もしくは
meaning: or; alternatively (formal)
summary: もしくは is a formal conjunction presenting alternatives — 'A or B'. It links nouns or clauses in written and official contexts: 郵送もしくはメールで = by post or by email. It is more formal than the everyday または, and in careful legal or technical writing the two are sometimes used at different levels (または for the larger split, もしくは for a sub-choice within one side). In ordinary speech, plain か or または is more natural.
pitfalls: This is formal/written; in casual speech か or または sounds more natural.
もしくは offers a choice between alternatives; do not confuse it with もし ('if'), which introduces a condition.

examples.ja: 申込書は郵送、もしくはメールでご提出ください。
examples.en: Please submit the application form by post or by email.
examples.f: ｜申込[もうしこみ]｜書[しょ]は｜郵送[ゆうそう]、もしくはメールでご｜提出[ていしゅつ]ください。

examples.ja: 責任者、もしくはその代理の者が対応いたします。
examples.en: The person in charge, or someone acting on their behalf, will attend to it.
examples.f: ｜責任[せきにん]｜者[しゃ]、もしくはその｜代理[だいり]の｜者[もの]が｜対応[たいおう]いたします。

synonyms.note: または is the standard 'or' for alternatives; もしくは is more formal and, in strict legal writing, marks a lower-level sub-choice.

title: 〜もしないで
meaning: without even doing ~
summary: Inserting も into the negative 〜しないで gives 〜もしないで, 'without even doing ~'. The も adds 'even', so it reproaches someone for skipping a basic, expected action: 確認もしないで = without even checking, 聞きもしないで = without even listening. For する-verbs it is Noun ＋ もしないで (確認もしないで); for other verbs it is the verb stem ＋ もしないで (見もしないで, 聞きもしないで). It typically carries criticism or exasperation.
pitfalls: The も adds 'even' and a tone of reproach; plain 〜ないで／〜ずに is neutral 'without doing'.
With する-verbs, split off the noun: 確認もしないで, not 確認しもしないで.

examples.ja: 彼は中身を確認もしないで、書類にサインしてしまった。
examples.en: He signed the document without even checking its contents.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜中身[なかみ]を｜確認[かくにん]もしないで、｜書類[しょるい]にサインしてしまった。

examples.ja: 人の話を聞きもしないで、勝手に結論を出すのはやめてほしい。
examples.en: I wish you'd stop jumping to your own conclusions without even listening to what people say.
examples.f: ｜人[ひと]の｜話[はなし]を｜聞[き]きもしないで、｜勝手[かって]に｜結論[けつろん]を｜出[だ]すのはやめてほしい。

synonyms.note: 〜ないで is neutral 'without doing ~'; 〜もしないで inserts も to mean 'without even ~' and adds reproach.
〜ずに is a more formal 'without doing'; もしないで is emphatic and critical about a skipped basic step.

title: 〜も同然だ
meaning: practically the same as; as good as; virtually
summary: 〜も同然だ states that although something is not literally so, in effect it amounts to the same thing — 'as good as ~, practically ~'. 終わったも同然だ = as good as finished, ないも同然だ = practically nonexistent. It follows a noun or a た-form verb, and 同然 (どうぜん) means 'the same, no different'. Use it to say the difference from the real thing is negligible in practical terms.
pitfalls: It marks near-equivalence in effect, not a literal identity: 死んだも同然 means 'as good as dead', not actually dead.
同然 can also modify a noun directly (親も同然の人 = someone like a parent); the も同然だ pattern here forms the predicate.

examples.ja: 残りはあと一問だけだから、試験はもう終わったも同然だ。
examples.en: There's only one question left, so the exam is as good as over.
examples.f: ｜残[のこ]りはあと｜一[いち]｜問[もん]だけだから、｜試験[しけん]はもう｜終[お]わったも｜同然[どうぜん]だ。

examples.ja: この街では車がないと、足がないも同然で、どこへも行けない。
examples.en: In this town, having no car is practically the same as having no way to get around — you can't go anywhere.
examples.f: この｜街[まち]では｜車[くるま]がないと、｜足[あし]がないも｜同然[どうぜん]で、どこへも｜行[い]けない。

synonyms.note: まるで〜ようだ compares by resemblance ('just like ~'); も同然だ asserts practical equivalence in effect.

title: 〜ものと思う
meaning: to assume; to take it that; to firmly believe that
summary: 〜ものと思う expresses a settled assumption or expectation — 'I take it that ~, I assume that ~'. It is firmer and more formal than a plain と思う, presenting the belief as a reasoned premise rather than a passing thought: 全員が了承したものと思う = I take it everyone has consented. It attaches to a plain-form clause and is common in polite, deliberate speech and writing.
pitfalls: More formal and settled than と思う: it frames the belief as a working premise, not a casual opinion.
The passive 〜ものと思われる is used for a detached, objective 'it is thought that'; ものと思う is the speaker's own assumption.

examples.ja: 参加者は全員、事前に資料に目を通しているものと思う。
examples.en: I assume all the participants have looked through the materials in advance.
examples.f: ｜参加[さんか]｜者[しゃ]は｜全員[ぜんいん]、｜事前[じぜん]に｜資料[しりょう]に｜目[め]を｜通[とお]しているものと｜思[おも]う。

examples.ja: この案でご了承いただけたものと思い、準備を進めております。
examples.en: Taking it that you have approved this proposal, we are proceeding with the preparations.
examples.f: この｜案[あん]でご｜了承[りょうしょう]いただけたものと｜思[おも]い、｜準備[じゅんび]を｜進[すす]めております。

synonyms.note: と思う is the everyday 'I think'; ものと思う is more formal and presents the belief as a firm assumption.
ものと思われる is the objective passive 'it is thought that'; ものと思う states the speaker's own assumption.

related.note: はずだ draws a logical 'ought to be' from grounds; ものと思う states a settled assumption without stressing the reasoning.

title: 〜ものと思っていた
meaning: was under the impression that; had assumed that
summary: The past continuous 〜ものと思っていた describes an assumption the speaker held over some period — 'I was under the impression that ~'. It very often implies that the assumption later turned out to be mistaken: てっきり来るものと思っていた = I was sure he'd come (but he didn't). It attaches to a plain-form clause and is frequently paired with てっきり ('quite certainly').
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ものと思っていた
pitfalls: It usually signals that the belief proved wrong; the following context typically reveals a contrary reality.
The past tense is on 思っていた, not on the embedded clause alone; keep the inner clause in plain form.

examples.ja: てっきり彼も来るものと思っていたが、結局姿を見せなかった。
examples.en: I was quite sure he would come too, but in the end he never showed up.
examples.f: てっきり｜彼[かれ]も｜来[く]るものと｜思[おも]っていたが、｜結局[けっきょく]｜姿[すがた]を｜見[み]せなかった。

examples.ja: この道でまっすぐ駅に着くものと思っていたら、とんだ回り道だった。
examples.en: I was under the impression this road went straight to the station, but it turned out to be a real detour.
examples.f: この｜道[みち]でまっすぐ｜駅[えき]に｜着[つ]くものと｜思[おも]っていたら、とんだ｜回り道[まわりみち]だった。

synonyms.note: ものと思う is a present, still-held assumption; ものと思っていた is a past belief, often one that turned out to be wrong.

related.note: はずだった expresses 'was supposed to be' from expectation; ものと思っていた reports a mistaken impression the speaker carried.

title: 〜ものと思われる・〜ものと見られる
kana: ものとおもわれる・ものとみられる
romaji: mono to omowareru / mono to mirareru
meaning: it is thought that; it is expected/estimated that
summary: 〜ものと思われる and 〜ものと見られる give a detached, objective judgment — 'it is thought / it is believed that ~'. The passive removes any single speaker, so these are staples of news reports, official statements, and academic writing: 原因は漏電によるものと見られる = the cause is believed to be an electrical short. They attach to a plain-form clause and present a cautious, evidence-based inference rather than a personal opinion.
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ものと思われる／ものと見られる
pitfalls: This is formal, written register (news, reports); in conversation と思う or らしい is more natural.
The passive makes the judgment sound objective and impersonal; use ものと思う when you want to own the assumption.

examples.ja: 出火の原因は、電気系統の不具合によるものと見られている。
examples.en: The cause of the fire is believed to be a fault in the electrical system.
examples.f: ｜出火[しゅっか]の｜原因[げんいん]は、｜電気[でんき]｜系統[けいとう]の｜不具合[ふぐあい]によるものと｜見[み]られている。

examples.ja: 今回の合意により、両国の関係は改善に向かうものと思われる。
examples.en: With this agreement, relations between the two countries are expected to move toward improvement.
examples.f: ｜今回[こんかい]の｜合意[ごうい]により、｜両国[りょうこく]の｜関係[かんけい]は｜改善[かいぜん]に｜向[む]かうものと｜思[おも]われる。

synonyms.note: ものと思う states the speaker's own assumption; ものと思われる is the impersonal passive 'it is thought that'.
に違いない is a confident 'must be'; ものと思われる is a cautious, hedged inference typical of reporting.

title: 〜ものとして
meaning: on the assumption that; treating (something) as being the case
summary: 〜ものとして means 'treating ~ as (settled/true)', proceeding on a stated premise even if it is not literally confirmed. 合意したものとして進める = proceed as though agreement has been reached; なかったものとして扱う = treat it as if it never happened. It attaches to a plain-form clause and works adverbially to set the assumption on which the following action is based.
structure: Verb［た form］／Verb［ない form］＋ものとして
pitfalls: This is the premise-setting 'treating as ~ / on the assumption that ~'; do not confuse it with として meaning 'as / in the role of'.
It describes how the following action treats the situation; the declarative 'shall be deemed' is ものとする.

examples.ja: この点については、双方が合意したものとして話を進めます。
examples.en: Regarding this point, we will proceed on the assumption that both sides have agreed.
examples.f: この｜点[てん]については、｜双方[そうほう]が｜合意[ごうい]したものとして｜話[はなし]を｜進[すす]めます。

examples.ja: 先ほどの発言は、なかったものとして扱ってください。
examples.en: Please treat my earlier remark as though it had never been made.
examples.f: ｜先[さき]ほどの｜発言[はつげん]は、なかったものとして｜扱[あつか]ってください。

synonyms.note: ものとする is a declaration ('shall be / is deemed'); ものとして adverbially sets the premise for a following action.

related.note: ものと思う states what the speaker assumes to be true; ものとして proceeds as if it is true, whether or not it actually is.

title: 〜ものとする
meaning: shall; to be deemed; it is stipulated that (legal/formal)
summary: 〜ものとする is the language of rules, contracts, and regulations, laying down what shall be the case or how something is to be deemed — 'shall ~ / is to be regarded as ~'. 書面で通知するものとする = shall give notice in writing; 合意があったものとする = shall be deemed to have agreed. It attaches to a dictionary- or ない-form verb and states a binding stipulation rather than a description of fact.
pitfalls: This belongs to legal and regulatory writing; it is not used in ordinary conversation.
ものとする lays down a rule ('shall'); ものとして sets a working assumption for a following action.

examples.ja: 契約の更新を希望する場合は、満了の前月末までに書面で通知するものとする。
examples.en: A party wishing to renew the contract shall give written notice by the end of the month preceding its expiry.
examples.f: ｜契約[けいやく]の｜更新[こうしん]を｜希望[きぼう]する｜場合[ばあい]は、｜満了[まんりょう]の｜前月[ぜんげつ]｜末[まつ]までに｜書面[しょめん]で｜通知[つうち]するものとする。

examples.ja: 本規約に定めのない事項については、両者が協議のうえ決定するものとする。
examples.en: Matters not provided for in these terms shall be decided through consultation between the two parties.
examples.f: ｜本[ほん]｜規約[きやく]に｜定[さだ]めのない｜事項[じこう]については、｜両者[りょうしゃ]が｜協議[きょうぎ]のうえ｜決定[けってい]するものとする。

synonyms.note: ものとして sets a premise for an action; ものとする issues a binding rule ('shall / is deemed').

title: 〜ものを
meaning: if only ~; and yet (regret or reproach)
summary: 〜ものを expresses regret or reproach that reality turned out differently from what could or should have been. It typically follows a hypothetical (〜ば／〜たら) describing the better outcome that failed to happen: 一言言ってくれればよかったものを = if only you'd said something. The tone is emotional and often faintly accusatory, and the sentence may trail off after ものを, leaving the complaint implied. It is literary and expressive.
pitfalls: It carries regret or reproach about a missed possibility; it is not the neutral のに and not the general ものだ.
The clause before ものを describes what would have been better, and reality fell short of it.

examples.ja: 一言相談してくれれば手を貸せたものを、彼は誰にも言わずに抱え込んでしまった。
examples.en: If only he'd said a word to me, I could have helped, but he kept it all to himself and told no one.
examples.f: ｜一言[ひとこと]｜相談[そうだん]してくれれば｜手[て]を｜貸[か]せたものを、｜彼[かれ]は｜誰[だれ]にも｜言[い]わずに｜抱え込[かかえこ]んでしまった。

examples.ja: 素直に謝れば済んだものを、言い訳ばかりして事を大きくしてしまった。
examples.en: It would have been over if he'd simply apologized, and yet he only made excuses and blew things out of proportion.
examples.f: ｜素直[すなお]に｜謝[あやま]れば｜済[す]んだものを、｜言い訳[いいわけ]ばかりして｜事[こと]を｜大[おお]きくしてしまった。

related.note: くせに reproaches a person for acting against what their situation warrants; ものを laments a better outcome that a hypothetical could have secured.

title: もはや
meaning: already; now; (with a negative) no longer
summary: もはや is a formal, somewhat literary adverb marking that a decisive, often irreversible point has been reached. With an affirmative predicate it means 'now, by this point, already' — もはや手遅れだ = it is already too late, もはや過去のものだ = it is now a thing of the past. With a negative it means 'no longer' — もはや戻れない = we can no longer go back. It is weightier and more formal than the everyday もう.
pitfalls: もはや is formal and emphatic, often conveying a point of no return; もう is the neutral everyday equivalent.
With a negative it means 'no longer' (もはや〜ない), parallel to もう〜ない.

examples.ja: ここまで事態が悪化しては、もはや打つ手がない。
examples.en: With the situation having deteriorated this far, there is no longer anything to be done.
examples.f: ここまで｜事態[じたい]が｜悪化[あっか]しては、もはや｜打つ手[うつて]がない。

examples.ja: 手作業に頼る時代は、もはや過去のものとなりつつある。
examples.en: The age of relying on manual labor is already becoming a thing of the past.
examples.f: ｜手作業[てさぎょう]に｜頼[たよ]る｜時代[じだい]は、もはや｜過去[かこ]のものとなりつつある。

synonyms.note: もう is the everyday 'already / no longer'; もはや is more formal and stresses that an irreversible point has been reached.

title: 〜や否や
meaning: as soon as; the moment that; no sooner ~ than
summary: 〜や否や attaches to a dictionary-form verb to mean 'the instant that ~, no sooner ~ than': ベルが鳴るや否や = the moment the bell rang. The second clause reports what happened immediately and unexpectedly right after. It is a literary, written expression; the following clause states an actual past event, not a plan, request, or command.
pitfalls: It is literary; in ordinary speech 〜とすぐに or 〜たとたん is more natural.
The second clause must be a factual, usually past, occurrence — not a command, request, or the speaker's own intention.

examples.ja: ベルが鳴るや否や、生徒たちは教室を飛び出していった。
examples.en: The moment the bell rang, the students dashed out of the classroom.
examples.f: ベルが｜鳴[な]るや｜否[いな]や、｜生徒[せいと]たちは｜教室[きょうしつ]を｜飛び出[とびだ]していった。

examples.ja: その知らせを聞くや否や、彼女は席を立って部屋を出て行った。
examples.en: No sooner had she heard the news than she rose from her seat and left the room.
examples.f: その｜知[し]らせを｜聞[き]くや｜否[いな]や、｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜席[せき]を｜立[た]って｜部屋[へや]を｜出[で]て｜行[い]った。

synonyms.note: が早いか is likewise literary 'the moment ~', but stresses that the second action began almost before the first was even finished.
たとたん(に) also means 'the moment ~', often with surprise, but is less literary and follows the た-form.
〜なり means 'as soon as ~' where the same subject moves straight into the next action; や否や allows a different subject or an external event to follow.

related.note: と同時に means 'at the same time as ~' (simultaneity); や否や stresses immediate succession right after the first event.

title: 〜やしない
meaning: there's no way ~; definitely doesn't/won't (emphatic negative)
summary: 〜やしない is a colloquial contraction of 〜はしない, used to deny something emphatically — 'there's no way ~, definitely won't ~'. It attaches to the verb stem: 分かりやしない = there's no way anyone understands, できやしない = it just can't be done. The tone is exasperated or dismissive, brushing off a possibility as out of the question. It belongs to casual, spoken language.
pitfalls: It comes from 〜はしない (わ／や sound change) and is casual and emphatic; avoid it in formal contexts.
It rejects a possibility outright with feeling, stronger than a plain 〜ない.

examples.ja: いくら呼んでも、こんな嵐の中では声など届きやしない。
examples.en: No matter how much you call out, in a storm like this your voice won't reach at all.
examples.f: いくら｜呼[よ]んでも、こんな｜嵐[あらし]の｜中[なか]では｜声[こえ]など｜届[とど]きやしない。

examples.ja: あんな無茶な計画、うまくいきやしないと最初から分かっていた。
examples.en: I knew from the start that a reckless plan like that would never work out.
examples.f: あんな｜無茶[むちゃ]な｜計画[けいかく]、うまくいきやしないと｜最初[さいしょ]から｜分[わ]かっていた。

related.note: とても〜ない says something is impossible to do; やしない emphatically denies that it happens or holds at all.

title: やれ〜やれ
meaning: what with ~ and ~ (listing burdens or complaints)
summary: やれ〜やれ〜 lists one troublesome thing after another, usually with a tone of exasperation at how much is piling up: やれ会議だやれ報告書だ = what with meetings and reports and everything. Each item is often a noun + だ, and the string is frequently rounded off with と before a verb like 忙しい. It conveys the speaker's weariness at a barrage of demands, and is colloquial.
pitfalls: Do not confuse this listing construction with the standalone interjection やれやれ ('good grief', a sigh).
It carries a complaining, put-upon tone, listing burdens rather than neutral choices.

examples.ja: 年末はやれ大掃除だ、やれ挨拶回りだと、休む暇もない。
examples.en: At year's end, what with the big clean-up and the rounds of greetings, there's no time to rest.
examples.f: ｜年末[ねんまつ]はやれ｜大[だい]｜掃除[そうじ]だ、やれ｜挨拶[あいさつ]｜回[まわ]りだと、｜休[やす]む｜暇[ひま]もない。

examples.ja: やれ会議だ、やれ報告書だと追われて、自分の仕事が一向に進まない。
examples.en: What with meetings and reports and all, I'm so run off my feet that my own work makes no headway at all.
examples.f: やれ｜会議[かいぎ]だ、やれ｜報告[ほうこく]｜書[しょ]だと｜追[お]われて、｜自分[じぶん]の｜仕事[しごと]が｜一向[いっこう]に｜進[すす]まない。

related.note: なり〜なり lists alternatives to choose from ('either A or B'); やれ〜やれ lists grievances piling up, with a weary tone.

title: ゆえに
meaning: therefore; hence; because of; for the reason that (formal)
summary: ゆえに expresses cause and consequence in formal, literary, or logical language. As a conjunction at the head of a sentence it means 'therefore, hence'. Attached to a noun (＋ゆえ／のゆえに) or a plain clause (＋がゆえに) it means 'owing to ~, because of ~': 経験の浅さゆえに = owing to inexperience. It is the register of reasoned argument and classical style, far more formal than から or ので.
pitfalls: This is formal/literary; in everyday speech から, ので, or だから are the natural choices.
When it attaches to a noun, no の is strictly required (若さゆえ), though のゆえに also occurs.

examples.ja: 彼の判断は、経験の浅さゆえに甘いところがあった。
examples.en: His judgment, owing to his lack of experience, was naive in places.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜判断[はんだん]は、｜経験[けいけん]の｜浅[あさ]さゆえに｜甘[あま]いところがあった。

examples.ja: 前例のない事業である。ゆえに、慎重な検討が求められる。
examples.en: This is an unprecedented undertaking. Therefore, careful examination is called for.
examples.f: ｜前例[ぜんれい]のない｜事業[じぎょう]である。ゆえに、｜慎重[しんちょう]な｜検討[けんとう]が｜求[もと]められる。

synonyms.note: から is the everyday 'because'; ゆえに expresses the same causal link in formal, literary, or logical writing.
ため(に) gives a neutral cause or purpose; ゆえに is more formal and belongs to reasoned or classical style.

related.note: ので softens a reason as objective and polite; ゆえに is markedly formal and literary.

title: 〜ようが〜まいが・〜ようと〜まいと
kana: ようが〜まいが・ようと〜まいと
romaji: you ga mai ga / you to mai to
meaning: whether one does or not; regardless of whether ~
summary: This pattern pairs a volitional (〜よう) with the negative volitional まい to mean 'whether one does ~ or not': 行こうが行くまいが = whether you go or not. The main clause holds true regardless of which side is the case. まい attaches to the dictionary form of godan verbs (行くまい) and to either form of ichidan/する verbs (食べまい／食べるまい, しまい／するまい). It is emphatic and somewhat formal.
structure: Verb［volitional］＋が／と＋（same verb）＋まいが／まいと
pitfalls: Keep the two verbs the same: the affirmative volitional (〜よう) plus its negative counterpart (〜まい).
まい follows the dictionary form for godan verbs (書くまい) and the stem or dictionary form for ichidan verbs (食べまい／食べるまい); for する both するまい and しまい occur, for 来る both 来るまい and 来まい.

examples.ja: 君が信じようが信じまいが、これは紛れもない事実だ。
examples.en: Whether you believe it or not, this is an undeniable fact.
examples.f: ｜君[きみ]が｜信[しん]じようが｜信[しん]じまいが、これは｜紛[まぎ]れもない｜事実[じじつ]だ。

examples.ja: 彼が来ようと来まいと、私の予定は何も変わらない。
examples.en: Whether he comes or not, my plans won't change in the slightest.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]が｜来[こ]ようと｜来[こ]まいと、｜私[わたし]の｜予定[よてい]は｜何[なに]も｜変[か]わらない。

synonyms.note: 〜ようが／ようと (single) means 'no matter (how/what)'; the 〜まい version explicitly spans the do/not-do alternatives.
にかかわらず says 'regardless of ~' about a noun or fixed set; ようが〜まいが frames the two poles as verb alternatives.

related.note: まい on its own is the negative volitional ('probably won't / won't'); here it forms the negative half of the 'whether or not' pair.

title: 〜ようが〜ようが・〜ようと〜ようと
kana: ようが〜ようが・ようと〜ようと
romaji: you ga you ga / you to you to
meaning: whether ~ or ~ (either way, it makes no difference)
summary: Two volitionals in a row — 〜ようが〜ようが or 〜ようと〜ようと — list two contrasting possibilities and declare that neither affects the outcome: 笑おうが泣こうが = whether you laugh or cry. It also works with adjectives via their volitional-style forms (高かろうが安かろうが = whether expensive or cheap). The main clause stands unchanged no matter which of the two holds. It is emphatic and somewhat formal.
structure: い-adjective［かろう］＋が／と＋い-adjective［かろう］＋が／と
pitfalls: Both slots take a volitional form; the two possibilities are usually contrasting (laugh/cry, expensive/cheap).
The main clause must be unaffected by either alternative; it states something that holds either way.

examples.ja: 周りが笑おうが泣こうが、彼は自分の信念を曲げなかった。
examples.en: Whether those around him laughed or cried, he would not bend his convictions.
examples.f: ｜周[まわ]りが｜笑[わら]おうが｜泣[な]こうが、｜彼[かれ]は｜自分[じぶん]の｜信念[しんねん]を｜曲[ま]げなかった。

examples.ja: 値段が高かろうが安かろうが、必要なものは買うしかない。
examples.en: Whether it's expensive or cheap, if it's something you need you have no choice but to buy it.
examples.f: ｜値段[ねだん]が｜高[たか]かろうが｜安[やす]かろうが、｜必要[ひつよう]なものは｜買[か]うしかない。

synonyms.note: ようが〜まいが spans a do/not-do pair; ようが〜ようが lists two positive alternatives, both irrelevant to the outcome.
〜ようが／ようと (single) means 'no matter (what/how)'; doubling it names two specific possibilities.

title: 〜ようが・〜ようと
meaning: no matter what/how; even if; regardless of ~
summary: A single volitional followed by が or と means 'no matter ~ / even if ~': 何を言われようが = no matter what I'm told, どうなろうと = no matter what happens. It concedes any possibility and states that the main clause holds all the same. With adjectives it uses かろう (どんなに苦しかろうと), and with nouns/な-adjectives であろう (誰であろうと). It is emphatic and more formal than ても.
pitfalls: が and と are interchangeable here; both mean 'no matter ~'.
It is emphatic and somewhat formal; plain ても is the more everyday 'even if'.

examples.ja: 周りに何と言われようと、私はこの道を進むと決めている。
examples.en: No matter what people around me say, I've decided to go down this path.
examples.f: ｜周[まわ]りに｜何[なに]と｜言[い]われようと、｜私[わたし]はこの｜道[みち]を｜進[すす]むと｜決[き]めている。

examples.ja: どんなに困難な状況になろうと、最後まで諦めるつもりはない。
examples.en: No matter how difficult the situation becomes, I have no intention of giving up until the very end.
examples.f: どんなに｜困難[こんなん]な｜状況[じょうきょう]になろうと、｜最後[さいご]まで｜諦[あきら]めるつもりはない。

synonyms.note: ても is the everyday 'even if ~'; 〜ようと／ようが is more emphatic and formal, stressing 'no matter what'.
doubling it (ようが〜ようが) lists two specific alternatives; the single form concedes any possibility at all.

related.note: もかまわず means 'without regard for ~ (and acting anyway)'; 〜ようと states that the outcome holds no matter the case.

title: 〜ようにも〜ない
meaning: even if one wanted or tried to, one can't (because circumstances block it)
summary: 〜ようにも〜ない says that even if you had the will to do something, external circumstances make it impossible. The same verb is usually repeated: the volitional form + にも sets up the intention, and its potential negative closes off the possibility. 起きようにも起きられない = I want to get up but can't. The barrier is a real-world obstacle (illness, lack of information, no time), not a lack of desire — the desire is precisely what is being frustrated.
pitfalls: The verb is normally repeated: volitional + にも, then its potential negative — 出かけようにも出かけられない, not 出かけようにない.
The blocking reason is an external circumstance; the will to act is present, which is what makes the impossibility frustrating.

examples.ja: 高熱で、朝は起きようにも起きられなかった。
examples.en: With a high fever, I couldn't get up in the morning even though I wanted to.
examples.f: ｜高熱[こうねつ]で、｜朝[あさ]は｜起[お]きようにも｜起[お]きられなかった。

examples.ja: 必要な情報がなくて、調べようにも調べられなかった。
examples.en: I lacked the information I needed, so I couldn't look it up even though I wanted to.
examples.f: ｜必要[ひつよう]な｜情報[じょうほう]がなくて、｜調[しら]べようにも｜調[しら]べられなかった。

related.note: ようとする describes making the attempt; ようにも〜ない says the attempt is blocked by circumstances so it can't be carried out.

title: ようによっては
meaning: depending on how one does or looks at it
summary: ようによっては is 'manner' よう (verb stem + よう, as in 考えよう・使いよう) followed by によっては 'depending on'. It says that a different — often more favorable — result is possible depending on the way you approach or interpret something. 考えようによっては = depending on how you look at it; 使いようによっては = depending on how you use it. It frequently introduces a reframing that turns a seemingly negative thing into something acceptable.
pitfalls: This よう is the 'way/manner' nominalizer (考えよう, 言いよう), not the volitional; don't read it as ようにも or ようとする.
It usually sets up a positive reframing — 'seen a certain way, it's actually fine' — rather than a neutral list of possibilities.

examples.ja: 考えようによっては、この失敗も貴重な経験だと言える。
examples.en: Depending on how you look at it, even this failure can be called a valuable experience.
examples.f: ｜考[かんが]えようによっては、この｜失敗[しっぱい]も｜貴重[きちょう]な｜経験[けいけん]だと｜言[い]える。

examples.ja: 言いようによっては、相手を傷つけずに断ることもできる。
examples.en: Depending on how you phrase it, you can turn someone down without hurting them.
examples.f: ｜言[い]いようによっては、｜相手[あいて]を｜傷[きず]つけずに｜断[ことわ]ることもできる。

related.note: Both use よう, but ようにも〜ない is the volitional ('even if I try'); ようによっては is the manner noun ('depending on the way').

title: 〜ようものなら
meaning: if one were to (even slightly) do ~, dire consequences would follow
summary: 〜ようものなら takes a volitional-form verb and warns that if that action were so much as attempted, something serious or disastrous would happen. The consequence is heavy and often exaggerated: 少しでも文句を言おうものなら大変なことになる = if you dared to complain even a little, all hell would break loose. It expresses the speaker's sense that the situation is so touchy that the smallest move triggers an outsized reaction.
pitfalls: Distinguish the two ものなら: with the volitional (言おうものなら) it means 'if one were to, with dire results'; with the potential (できるものなら) it means 'if one could'.
The result clause is negative and often hyperbolic — the point is how extreme the reaction to a small act would be.

examples.ja: 彼の前でその話題に触れようものなら、何時間も説教が続くだろう。
examples.en: If you so much as brought up that topic in front of him, the lecture would go on for hours.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜前[まえ]でその｜話題[わだい]に｜触[ふ]れようものなら、｜何[なん]｜時間[じかん]も｜説教[せっきょう]が｜続[つづ]くだろう。

examples.ja: 少しでも手を抜こうものなら、監督にすぐ見抜かれてしまう。
examples.en: If you were to cut corners even a little, the coach would see through it in no time.
examples.f: ｜少[すこ]しでも｜手[て]を｜抜[ぬ]こうものなら、｜監督[かんとく]にすぐ｜見抜[みぬ]かれてしまう。

synonyms.note: The potential-based ものなら (できるものなら) expresses a wish 'if only one could'; ようものなら uses the volitional to warn of dire results.

title: 〜わ
meaning: sentence-final particle adding soft emphasis or feeling (stereotypically feminine)
summary: Sentence-final わ attaches to the plain form and adds a gentle, emotive touch to a statement. Said with a rising intonation it is classic feminine 'role language' — the わ of fiction and older speech — and can sound affected in real modern conversation. A separate, flat or falling わ is gender-neutral and very common in casual and Kansai speech, where it marks a mild self-directed assertion (そろそろ行くわ = 'I'll head off now'). Teach it as expressive softening, and read the intonation to tell the two apart.
pitfalls: The rising, softly emphatic わ is stereotyped feminine role language and can sound theatrical in everyday modern speech.
A flat/falling わ (common in Kansai and casual male speech) simply marks mild assertion and is not gendered; intonation, not the syllable, distinguishes them.

examples.ja: 私、そんなこと一度も言ってないわ。
examples.en: I never said any such thing.
examples.f: ｜私[わたし]、そんなこと｜一[いち]｜度[ど]も｜言[い]ってないわ。

examples.ja: あら、きれいな花が咲いているわ。
examples.en: Oh, look — there are pretty flowers in bloom.
examples.f: あら、きれいな｜花[はな]が｜咲[さ]いているわ。

related.note: Same syllable, different construction: わ〜わで lists a pile-up of (usually bad) events, not a sentence-final softener.

title: 〜わ〜わで
meaning: what with ~ and ~ (a pile-up of, usually, troubles)
summary: 〜わ〜わで lists two or more things — typically mishaps — that pile up at once, and the closing で leads into the resulting (bad) state. Each item ends in わ: 財布は落とすわ、電車は遅れるわで散々だった = what with losing my wallet and the train being late, it was awful. It conveys an exasperated 'one thing after another' feeling and is common in spoken complaints.
pitfalls: The listed items are usually negatives piling up, and the final で introduces the resulting (bad) situation.
This わ is a listing particle, not the sentence-final feminine わ — here it always comes in the paired わ〜わ pattern.

examples.ja: 財布はなくすわ、電車は遅れるわで、今日は本当についていない。
examples.en: What with losing my wallet and the train being delayed, I've had really rotten luck today.
examples.f: ｜財布[さいふ]はなくすわ、｜電車[でんしゃ]は｜遅[おく]れるわで、｜今日[きょう]は｜本当[ほんとう]についていない。

examples.ja: パソコンは壊れるわ、資料は見つからないわで、仕事が全く進まなかった。
examples.en: What with the computer breaking down and the documents going missing, I got no work done at all.
examples.f: パソコンは｜壊[こわ]れるわ、｜資料[しりょう]は｜見[み]つからないわで、｜仕事[しごと]が｜全[まった]く｜進[すす]まなかった。

related.note: Shares the syllable わ but is unrelated: the feminine 〜わ is a single sentence-final softener, not a paired listing of troubles.

title: 訳あり
meaning: having (unspoken) special circumstances
summary: 訳あり literally 'there is a reason' describes someone or something as carrying special circumstances that are deliberately left unstated — often awkward, delicate, or something that lowers value. 訳ありの二人 = a couple with a complicated backstory; 訳あり商品 = goods discounted for some (minor) flaw. It behaves like a noun/na-adjective modifier (訳ありの〜, 訳ありだ) and hints at a story without telling it.
pitfalls: 訳あり implies there is a reason but pointedly leaves it unspoken — usually something awkward, delicate, or that reduces value.
It modifies like a noun/na-adjective (訳ありの関係, 訳あり品); there is no matching 訳なし used the same way.

examples.ja: あの人は、どうやら訳ありの過去を抱えているらしい。
examples.en: That person seems to be carrying some kind of complicated past.
examples.f: あの｜人[ひと]は、どうやら｜訳[わけ]ありの｜過去[かこ]を｜抱[かか]えているらしい。

examples.ja: この店では、訳あり品を安く売っている。
examples.en: This shop sells items with minor defects at a discount.
examples.f: この｜店[みせ]では、｜訳[わけ]あり｜品[ひん]を｜安[やす]く｜売[う]っている。

title: 〜をいいことに
meaning: taking advantage of; exploiting (a favorable situation)
summary: 〜をいいことに marks a favorable circumstance that someone exploits to do something they arguably shouldn't. It carries clear criticism: 親が留守なのをいいことに = taking advantage of the parents being out. A noun takes を directly; a clause is nominalized with の first (いないのをいいことに). The speaker disapproves of the person for seizing on the situation.
pitfalls: Almost always critical — the speaker blames someone for exploiting a situation, so it doesn't fit neutral 'given the chance' contexts.
After a clause, insert の before をいいことに: 先生がいないのをいいことに.

examples.ja: 彼は先生がいないのをいいことに、教室で騒ぎ始めた。
examples.en: Taking advantage of the teacher's absence, he started making a racket in the classroom.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜先生[せんせい]がいないのをいいことに、｜教室[きょうしつ]で｜騒[さわ]ぎ｜始[はじ]めた。

examples.ja: 客が少ないのをいいことに、店員はずっとおしゃべりしていた。
examples.en: Taking advantage of there being few customers, the clerk chatted the entire time.
examples.f: ｜客[きゃく]が｜少[すく]ないのをいいことに、｜店員[てんいん]はずっとおしゃべりしていた。

related.note: をよそに means acting in disregard of others' concerns; をいいことに means actively exploiting a convenient situation for one's own ends.

title: 〜をおいて〜ない
meaning: no one/nothing but; none other than
summary: 〜をおいて〜ない singles out X as the one and only option, ending in a negative: 彼をおいて適任者はいない = there is no one suited but him. The をおいて here means 'setting aside / other than', and ほかに is often inserted (をおいてほかにない). It carries strong positive evaluation, presenting X as uniquely qualified with no real alternative.
pitfalls: The sentence must close in a negative (いない／ない); it singles out X as the sole choice, usually with praise.
This おいて is 'other than / apart from', not the verb 置いて 'placing (something)'.

examples.ja: この難しい役を演じられるのは、彼女をおいてほかにいない。
examples.en: There is no one but her who could play this difficult role.
examples.f: この｜難[むずか]しい｜役[やく]を｜演[えん]じられるのは、｜彼女[かのじょ]をおいてほかにいない。

examples.ja: 会社を立て直せる人物は、あの人をおいて考えられない。
examples.en: The only person who could turn the company around is him — no one else comes to mind.
examples.f: ｜会社[かいしゃ]を｜立て直[たてなお]せる｜人物[じんぶつ]は、あの｜人[ひと]をおいて｜考[かんが]えられない。

synonyms.note: を除いて simply excludes X from a set; をおいて〜ない goes further, saying X is the sole option and nothing else qualifies.

related.note: ならでは also stresses uniqueness ('only X can'), but as a positive attribute of X; をおいて〜ない frames it through a negation of all alternatives.

title: 〜を押して・〜を押し切って
kana: をおして・をおしきって
meaning: doing something despite opposition or one's own poor condition
summary: 〜を押して and 〜を押し切って mean forging ahead despite an obstacle. を押し切って stresses forcibly overriding others' resistance — 周囲の反対を押し切って結婚した = married in the face of everyone's objections. を押して is often used of acting despite one's own condition — 病を押して出席する = attend despite illness. The object is the obstacle being overcome (opposition, illness), not a physical thing.
