pitfalls: を押し切って = force one's way past others' opposition; を押して is typically used of pressing on despite one's own poor condition (熱を押して).
The object is the obstacle (反対・病気), not a literal object; 押す here is figurative 'push through', not physical pushing.

examples.ja: 周囲の反対を押し切って、彼は起業する道を選んだ。
examples.en: Overriding the objections of those around him, he chose the path of starting his own business.
examples.f: ｜周囲[しゅうい]の｜反対[はんたい]を｜押し切[おしき]って、｜彼[かれ]は｜起業[きぎょう]する｜道[みち]を｜選[えら]んだ。

examples.ja: 高熱を押して、彼女は最後まで舞台に立ち続けた。
examples.en: Pushing through a high fever, she stayed on stage right to the end.
examples.f: ｜高熱[こうねつ]を｜押[お]して、｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜最後[さいご]まで｜舞台[ぶたい]に｜立[た]ち｜続[つづ]けた。

related.note: をものともせずに = undaunted by hardship, admiring the resolve; を押し切って highlights the act of forcibly overriding resistance.
を顧みず = without giving thought to danger/consequences; を押して = pressing on despite an obstacle one is clearly aware of.

title: 〜を顧みず・〜も顧みず
kana: をかえりみず・もかえりみず
meaning: without regard for; heedless of
summary: 〜を顧みず means acting without giving thought to something one arguably should heed — danger, one's own body, or one's family. 危険を顧みず火の中へ = plunging into the fire heedless of danger; 家庭を顧みない = neglectful of one's family. 顧みる literally means 'to look back on / pay heed to', so 顧みず is 'without heeding'. It is formal and largely written, and the も variant adds a 'not even' shading (身の危険も顧みず).
pitfalls: Formal and written in register; the object is usually danger, one's own body/family, or consequences one would normally take into account.
顧みず is literary 'without looking back on / heeding' — not the same as merely 'not seeing'.

examples.ja: 消防士たちは危険を顧みず、炎の中へ飛び込んでいった。
examples.en: The firefighters plunged into the flames heedless of the danger.
examples.f: ｜消防[しょうぼう]｜士[し]たちは｜危険[きけん]を｜顧[かえり]みず、｜炎[ほのお]の｜中[なか]へ｜飛び込[とびこ]んでいった。

examples.ja: 彼は自分の体も顧みず、夜遅くまで働き続けた。
examples.en: Without any regard even for his own health, he kept working late into the night.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜自分[じぶん]の｜体[からだ]も｜顧[かえり]みず、｜夜[よる]｜遅[おそ]くまで｜働[はたら]き｜続[つづ]けた。

synonyms.note: をものともせずに praises bravely overcoming a hardship; を顧みず emphasizes simply not giving thought to what one should heed.

related.note: もかまわず = not minding/caring about something; を顧みず specifically frames it as failing to give due heed to danger or one's own welfare.

title: 〜を限りに
meaning: as of (the end of); ~ being the last
summary: 〜を限りに takes a time point or occasion as the final cutoff, after which something stops or changes for good: 今日を限りに = as of today; 本日を限りに閉店 = closing as of today. The following clause typically states an ending — a retirement, a shop's last day, quitting a habit. (A separate fixed idiom 声を限りに / 力の限り means 'to the utmost' and is unrelated to this time-cutoff use.)
pitfalls: Marks a time point as the last one, after which something ends; the main clause is normally an ending or cessation.
Don't confuse it with the fixed phrase 声を限りに ('at the top of one's voice'), which is 'to the utmost', not a time cutoff.

examples.ja: 今シーズンを限りに、彼は現役を引退することを発表した。
examples.en: He announced that he would retire from active play as of the end of this season.
examples.f: ｜今[こん]シーズンを｜限[かぎ]りに、｜彼[かれ]は｜現役[げんえき]を｜引退[いんたい]することを｜発表[はっぴょう]した。

examples.ja: 本日を限りに、この店は五十年の歴史に幕を下ろす。
examples.en: As of today, this shop brings the curtain down on its fifty years of history.
examples.f: ｜本日[ほんじつ]を｜限[かぎ]りに、この｜店[みせ]は｜五[ご]｜十[じゅう]｜年[ねん]の｜歴史[れきし]に｜幕[まく]を｜下[お]ろす。

synonyms.note: をもって is a neutral formal 'as of / with (this)'; を限りに adds the feeling that this is the final time, the last.

related.note: を境に marks a dividing line with a before/after change; を限りに marks a final endpoint after which something simply stops.

title: 〜を兼ねて
meaning: doubling as; also serving the purpose of
summary: 〜を兼ねて names a secondary purpose that a single action also fulfills. 運動を兼ねて歩く = walk, which also serves as exercise; 挨拶を兼ねて訪ねる = visit, partly to pay one's respects. The noun before を兼ねて is the additional aim; the main clause states the primary action that happens to cover it too. It comes from 兼ねる 'to combine two roles'.
pitfalls: The noun before を兼ねて is the secondary purpose; the main clause is the primary action that also fulfills it.
Both purposes are real and compatible — it's one act serving two ends, not choosing one over the other.

examples.ja: 運動を兼ねて、通勤にはできるだけ自転車を使うようにしている。
examples.en: To get some exercise as well, I try to commute by bicycle whenever I can.
examples.f: ｜運動[うんどう]を｜兼[か]ねて、｜通勤[つうきん]にはできるだけ｜自転車[じてんしゃ]を｜使[つか]うようにしている。

examples.ja: 旧友との再会を兼ねて、久しぶりに故郷へ帰った。
examples.en: I went back to my hometown for the first time in ages, which also served as a reunion with old friends.
examples.f: ｜旧友[きゅうゆう]との｜再会[さいかい]を｜兼[か]ねて、｜久[ひさ]しぶりに｜故郷[こきょう]へ｜帰[かえ]った。

title: 〜を皮切りに
meaning: starting with; as the first of an unfolding series
summary: 〜を皮切りに marks X as the first instance from which a series spreads or expands — 東京公演を皮切りに全国ツアーが始まった = starting with the Tokyo show, a nationwide tour began. 皮切り literally means 'the first cut', and the following clause must describe a chain of events or a spreading development that grows out of that opening, not a single isolated act. It is formal and often used of tours, movements, and cascading reactions.
structure: Noun［first event］＋を皮切りに（して）／を皮切りとして
pitfalls: What follows must be a series or spreading development that grows from the first instance — not a single, unconnected event.
The named event is genuinely the chronological start of the chain, giving it a sense of momentum picking up.

examples.ja: 東京公演を皮切りに、全国各地でのツアーが始まった。
examples.en: Starting with the Tokyo performance, a tour across the country got under way.
examples.f: ｜東京[とうきょう]｜公演[こうえん]を｜皮切[かわき]りに、｜全国[ぜんこく]｜各地[かくち]でのツアーが｜始[はじ]まった。

examples.ja: 彼の勇気ある発言を皮切りに、次々と改革を求める声が上がり始めた。
examples.en: Beginning with his courageous remark, calls for reform began to rise one after another.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜勇気[ゆうき]ある｜発言[はつげん]を｜皮切[かわき]りに、｜次々[つぎつぎ]と｜改革[かいかく]を｜求[もと]める｜声[こえ]が｜上[あ]がり｜始[はじ]めた。

synonyms.note: をはじめ lists X as a representative example among others; を皮切りに marks X as the chronological first of a series that unfolds from it.

title: 〜を機に
meaning: taking ~ as the occasion/opportunity (for a change)
summary: 〜を機に treats an event as the occasion that prompts a deliberate new action or change: 結婚を機に転職した = took marriage as the occasion to change jobs; 定年を機に = on the occasion of retirement. It is fairly formal, and the following clause is a chosen action, not an automatic consequence. 機 here is 'opportunity/turning point'.
pitfalls: The following clause is a deliberate action or change taken because of the event, not a spontaneous result.
Fairly formal; for everyday speech, をきっかけに feels more casual.

examples.ja: 定年を機に、夫婦で田舎に移り住むことにした。
examples.en: Taking his retirement as the occasion, the couple decided to move to the countryside.
examples.f: ｜定年[ていねん]を｜機[き]に、｜夫婦[ふうふ]で｜田舎[いなか]に｜移り住[うつりす]むことにした。

examples.ja: 今回の失敗を機に、業務の進め方を一から見直すことにした。
examples.en: Using this failure as a turning point, we decided to review our workflow from scratch.
examples.f: ｜今回[こんかい]の｜失敗[しっぱい]を｜機[き]に、｜業務[ぎょうむ]の｜進め方[すすめかた]を｜一[いち]から｜見直[みなお]すことにした。

synonyms.note: を契機に is near-identical in meaning and slightly more formal/literary; を機に is the shorter everyday equivalent.
をきっかけに is the more colloquial 'triggered by'; を機に is more formal and leans toward a chosen life change.

related.note: を境に stresses a before/after dividing line; を機に stresses seizing the event as an opportunity to act.

title: 〜を禁じ得ない
meaning: cannot suppress (an emotion); can't help feeling
summary: 〜を禁じ得ない takes an emotion noun and says one cannot forbid it welling up: 涙を禁じ得ない = can't hold back tears; 怒りを禁じ得ない = can't suppress anger. 禁じ得ない literally means 'cannot forbid (in oneself)'. It is distinctly formal, appearing in written and formal-spoken contexts, and describes a feeling that arises naturally in the speaker or as a general human reaction.
pitfalls: The object is an emotion noun (涙・怒り・驚き・同情), not an action — you can't say 行くのを禁じ得ない.
Formal register; describes an emotion welling up in oneself, so it isn't used to report someone else's feelings casually.

examples.ja: あまりに理不尽な仕打ちに、怒りを禁じ得なかった。
examples.en: Faced with such an unreasonable act, I could not suppress my anger.
examples.f: あまりに｜理不尽[りふじん]な｜仕打[しう]ちに、｜怒[いか]りを｜禁[きん]じ｜得[え]なかった。

examples.ja: 被災地の惨状を目にして、涙を禁じ得なかった。
examples.en: Seeing the devastation in the disaster area, I could not hold back my tears.
examples.f: ｜被災[ひさい]｜地[ち]の｜惨状[さんじょう]を｜目[め]にして、｜涙[なみだ]を｜禁[きん]じ｜得[え]なかった。

synonyms.note: ざるを得ない = have no choice but to (do an action); を禁じ得ない = cannot suppress (an emotion) — different objects.

related.note: 〜に堪えない (感慨に堪えない) also expresses an overwhelming feeling; を禁じ得ない specifically frames it as an emotion one cannot hold back.

title: 〜を境に
meaning: with ~ as the dividing line/turning point
summary: 〜を境に takes a time point or event as a boundary and marks a clear before/after contrast: あの日を境に彼は変わった = from that day on, as a dividing line, he changed. 境 means 'boundary', so the emphasis is on how noticeably different things are on either side of that point. It often pairs with life-changing events, ages, or seasons.
structure: Noun［time／event］＋を境に（して）／を境として
pitfalls: The emphasis is on a marked before/after contrast around the boundary — not merely that something happened at that time.
Compare を機に, which stresses seizing an occasion to act; を境に stresses the dividing line itself.

examples.ja: 大病を境に、彼は生き方をすっかり変えた。
examples.en: A serious illness marked a turning point, and he completely changed the way he lived.
examples.f: ｜大病[たいびょう]を｜境[さかい]に、｜彼[かれ]は｜生き方[いきかた]をすっかり｜変[か]えた。

examples.ja: 三十歳を境に、体力の衰えを感じるようになった。
examples.en: Around the age of thirty, as a dividing line, I began to feel my strength declining.
examples.f: ｜三[さん]｜十[じゅう]｜歳[さい]を｜境[さかい]に、｜体力[たいりょく]の｜衰[おとろ]えを｜感[かん]じるようになった。

synonyms.note: を機に seizes an event as an opportunity for a chosen action; を境に marks a boundary with a clear before/after change.

related.note: を限りに marks a final endpoint after which something stops; を境に marks a point where things change from one state to another.

title: 〜を前提として・〜を前提に
kana: をぜんていとして・をぜんていに
romaji: o zentei toshite / o zentei ni
meaning: on the premise/assumption of
summary: 〜を前提として / 〜を前提に marks something as a precondition assumed to hold before proceeding: 結婚を前提に付き合う = date with marriage as the premise; 予算の確保を前提とする = premised on securing the budget. A clause is nominalized with こと first (〜ことを前提に). It is formal, common in planning, agreements, and business, and states an assumed basis rather than a mere hope.
structure: Noun＋を前提として／を前提に
pitfalls: For a clause, nominalize first: 〜ことを前提に / 〜という前提で.
It states a precondition taken as given going forward — not a fact already established (compare を踏まえて).

examples.ja: この計画は、必要な予算が確保できることを前提としている。
examples.en: This plan is premised on being able to secure the necessary budget.
examples.f: この｜計画[けいかく]は、｜必要[ひつよう]な｜予算[よさん]が｜確保[かくほ]できることを｜前提[ぜんてい]としている。

examples.ja: 彼らは結婚を前提に、真剣に交際を始めた。
examples.en: They began dating seriously, with marriage as the premise.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]らは｜結婚[けっこん]を｜前提[ぜんてい]に、｜真剣[しんけん]に｜交際[こうさい]を｜始[はじ]めた。

synonyms.note: を踏まえて builds on facts already established; を前提に assumes a condition as given before moving ahead.

related.note: をもとに uses X as source material for making something; を前提に treats X as a condition assumed to hold.

title: 〜を控えて
meaning: with ~ close ahead; on the eve of
summary: 〜を控えて describes a situation in which an important event is imminent, and the main clause tells what is happening in the run-up: 試験を控えて猛勉強する = cram with exams looming; 出発を明日に控えて = with departure the next day. Here 控える means 'have (something) close ahead', temporally (or sometimes spatially). The impending event is usually significant, which colors the preparation or mood.
pitfalls: This 控える means 'have (an event) looming close ahead', not the other sense of 控える 'to refrain from / hold back'.
The event is imminent and usually important; the main clause describes the situation or preparations leading up to it.

examples.ja: 受験を間近に控えて、彼は毎日遅くまで勉強している。
examples.en: With the entrance exams close at hand, he studies late every day.
examples.f: ｜受験[じゅけん]を｜間近[まぢか]に｜控[ひか]えて、｜彼[かれ]は｜毎日[まいにち]｜遅[おそ]くまで｜勉強[べんきょう]している。

examples.ja: 開店を翌日に控えて、店内は準備に追われていた。
examples.en: With the opening the very next day, the shop was rushed off its feet with preparations.
examples.f: ｜開店[かいてん]を｜翌日[よくじつ]に｜控[ひか]えて、｜店内[てんない]は｜準備[じゅんび]に｜追[お]われていた。

related.note: に先立ち = doing something in advance of an event; を控えて = being in the run-up with the event looming ahead.
にあたって marks the occasion of doing something; を控えて sets the scene of an imminent event and what happens before it.

title: 〜を踏まえて
meaning: based on; taking ~ into account
summary: 〜を踏まえて means taking established facts, results, or opinions as the grounds for the next judgment or action: 現状を踏まえて対策を立てる = draw up measures taking the current situation into account; 前回の反省を踏まえて = building on the lessons of last time. 踏まえる means 'to base oneself on', so the reference is something already known and considered, not a future hypothetical. It is formal and common in discussion and policy.
pitfalls: Take X (facts, results, opinions already established) as the basis for a judgment or action — not a future assumption (compare を前提に).
Formal register; typical objects are 現状・結果・意見・事実, things already on the table.

examples.ja: 前回の反省を踏まえて、今年は計画を大幅に見直した。
examples.en: Taking the lessons of last time into account, this year we substantially revised the plan.
examples.f: ｜前回[ぜんかい]の｜反省[はんせい]を｜踏[ふ]まえて、｜今年[ことし]は｜計画[けいかく]を｜大幅[おおはば]に｜見直[みなお]した。

examples.ja: 調査結果を踏まえて、今後の方針を決定する予定だ。
examples.en: We plan to decide our future policy on the basis of the survey results.
examples.f: ｜調査[ちょうさ]｜結果[けっか]を｜踏[ふ]まえて、｜今後[こんご]の｜方針[ほうしん]を｜決定[けってい]する｜予定[よてい]だ。

synonyms.note: をもとに uses X as source material to produce something; を踏まえて takes X into consideration as grounds for a judgment.

related.note: を前提に assumes a condition as given going forward; を踏まえて builds on facts already established.

title: 〜を経て
meaning: via; through; after (a process or interval)
summary: 〜を経て marks passing through a stage, place, or span of time on the way to a result: 長い交渉を経て合意に達した = reached agreement after long negotiations; パリを経てロンドンへ = via Paris to London. 経て is the て-form of 経る 'to pass through'. It is formal and written, emphasizing the intervening process that led to the final state.
pitfalls: Formal and written; marks passing through a stage, place, or period of time on the way to an outcome.
経て is from 経る 'pass through', not 経つ 'time elapses' — the point is the process one goes through.

examples.ja: 長い議論を経て、ようやく全員が納得できる結論に達した。
examples.en: After a long discussion, we finally reached a conclusion everyone could accept.
examples.f: ｜長[なが]い｜議論[ぎろん]を｜経[へ]て、ようやく｜全員[ぜんいん]が｜納得[なっとく]できる｜結論[けつろん]に｜達[たっ]した。

examples.ja: 彼は幾多の困難を経て、今の地位を築き上げた。
examples.en: Through countless hardships, he built up the position he holds today.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜幾多[いくた]の｜困難[こんなん]を｜経[へ]て、｜今[いま]の｜地位[ちい]を｜築き上[きずきあ]げた。

synonyms.note: を通じて = by means of, or throughout a span; を経て = after passing through a stage on the way to a result.

related.note: た末に stresses a final outcome after much effort/trouble; を経て neutrally marks the process or stages passed through.

title: 〜をもって・〜をもちまして
kana: をもって・をもちまして
meaning: with; by means of; as of (a set time or point)
summary: 〜をもって attaches to a noun in two formal senses. As 'by means of / with' it names the means, standard, or quality through which something is done — 誠意をもって対応する (deal with it in good faith), 書面をもって通知する (notify in writing). As 'as of / effective from' it marks a fixed point that draws a line — 本日をもって (as of today), 五時をもって (as of five o'clock) — after which a state ends or begins. をもちまして is the politer form heard in announcements and ceremonies. Both belong to written and formal spoken register, not casual で.
structure: Noun［point in time］＋をもって／をもちまして
pitfalls: Two distinct senses: 'by means of / with' (naming a method or quality) and 'as of / effective from' (a fixed cut-off point). Context tells them apart.
This is formal and written; in everyday speech で ('by means of') is normal, not をもって.
をもちまして is a politeness variant used in announcements, not a separate meaning.

examples.ja: 当店は本日をもちまして閉店させていただきます。
examples.en: As of today, our store will be closing for good.
examples.f: ｜当店[とうてん]は｜本日[ほんじつ]をもちまして｜閉店[へいてん]させていただきます。

examples.ja: 選考の結果は、後日書面をもってお知らせいたします。
examples.en: The results of the selection will be communicated to you in writing at a later date.
examples.f: ｜選考[せんこう]の｜結果[けっか]は、｜後日[ごじつ]｜書面[しょめん]をもってお｜知[し]らせいたします。

synonyms.note: にて is a formal で for means or place; をもって in its 'by means of' sense is even more formal and often names a quality or standard.

related.note: を限りに also sets a final cut-off point in time, but stresses that something ends there; をもって can mark either an ending or a starting boundary.

title: 〜をものともせずに
meaning: undaunted by; in defiance of (a hardship or danger)
summary: 〜をものともせず（に） attaches to a noun naming a difficulty, danger, or setback and says the subject pressed on without being cowed by it — 困難をものともせず (undaunted by hardship), 荒波をものともせず (in defiance of the rough seas). The tone is admiring: it praises someone for bravely facing down an obstacle, so it usually describes other people's courage rather than one's own trivial troubles.
pitfalls: The noun must be a real hardship or danger that the subject overcomes admirably; it does not fit petty inconveniences.
The nuance is praise for bravery, so it is normally used of others, not to describe your own everyday situation.
せず is the classical negative of する; there is no をものともしずに.

examples.ja: 彼女は度重なる失敗をものともせず、研究を続けた。
examples.en: Undaunted by one failure after another, she carried on with her research.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜度重[たびかさ]なる｜失敗[しっぱい]をものともせず、｜研究[けんきゅう]を｜続[つづ]けた。

examples.ja: 選手たちは悪天候をものともせずに、試合を最後まで戦い抜いた。
examples.en: In defiance of the terrible weather, the players fought the match out to the very end.
examples.f: ｜選手[せんしゅ]たちは｜悪天候[あくてんこう]をものともせずに、｜試合[しあい]を｜最後[さいご]まで｜戦[たたか]い｜抜[ぬ]いた。

synonyms.note: にもかかわらず neutrally states 'despite'; をものともせず adds that the subject bravely overpowered the obstacle.

related.note: をよそに also means acting in the face of something, but coolly disregards concern one ought to heed; をものともせず courageously overcomes a hardship.

title: 〜を余儀なくさせる
meaning: to force (a situation); to make (something) unavoidable
summary: 〜を余儀なくさせる is the causative side of this pair: an impersonal cause — a circumstance, event, or condition — is the subject and forces some outcome to happen. The forced outcome is a noun of action (中止, 撤退, 変更) marked with を, and the person pushed into it takes に. 不況が事業の縮小を余儀なくさせた = the recession forced a scaling-back of the business. It is stiff, written register typical of news and reports.
pitfalls: The subject is the impersonal cause that does the forcing; contrast 〜を余儀なくされる, where the affected person is the subject.
The を-noun is normally a する-type action noun such as 中止・変更・撤退, not a concrete object.
Register is formal and written; it rarely appears in casual conversation.

examples.ja: 資金不足が、計画の大幅な見直しを余儀なくさせた。
examples.en: A shortage of funds forced a sweeping revision of the plan.
examples.f: ｜資金[しきん]｜不足[ふそく]が、｜計画[けいかく]の｜大幅[おおはば]な｜見直[みなお]しを｜余儀[よぎ]なくさせた。

examples.ja: 台風の接近は、主催者に大会の中止を余儀なくさせた。
examples.en: The approaching typhoon forced the organizers to call off the tournament.
examples.f: ｜台風[たいふう]の｜接近[せっきん]は、｜主催[しゅさい]｜者[しゃ]に｜大会[たいかい]の｜中止[ちゅうし]を｜余儀[よぎ]なくさせた。

related.note: The passive counterpart: 〜を余儀なくされる puts the forced person in the subject slot, while 〜を余儀なくさせる puts the cause there.

title: 〜を余儀なくされる
meaning: to be forced to; to have no choice but to (undergo)
summary: 〜を余儀なくされる is the passive side of the pair: the person or organization affected is the subject, and outside circumstances leave them no choice but to accept some outcome. The unwanted outcome is an action noun (欠場, 閉鎖, 延期) marked with を. けがで欠場を余儀なくされた = was forced to sit out because of injury. It stresses that the situation was imposed from without, and it belongs to formal, written register.
pitfalls: The affected person is the subject and the を-noun is what they are forced into; contrast 〜を余儀なくさせる, where the cause is the subject.
The を-noun is normally a する-type action noun such as 中止・閉鎖・延期.
It emphasizes that circumstances imposed the outcome, so it carries a sense of reluctance and belongs to formal writing.

examples.ja: 出場予定だった選手は、けがのために欠場を余儀なくされた。
examples.en: The player who had been slated to compete was forced to withdraw because of an injury.
examples.f: ｜出場[しゅつじょう]｜予定[よてい]だった｜選手[せんしゅ]は、けがのために｜欠場[けつじょう]を｜余儀[よぎ]なくされた。

examples.ja: 業績の悪化により、会社は多くの店舗の閉鎖を余儀なくされた。
examples.en: With performance deteriorating, the company had no choice but to close many of its stores.
examples.f: ｜業績[ぎょうせき]の｜悪化[あっか]により、｜会社[かいしゃ]は｜多[おお]くの｜店舗[てんぽ]の｜閉鎖[へいさ]を｜余儀[よぎ]なくされた。

synonyms.note: ざるを得ない attaches to a verb and voices personal, reluctant resignation; を余儀なくされる attaches to an action noun and stresses that external circumstances imposed it.
しかない plainly says 'there is nothing to do but'; を余儀なくされる is far more formal and frames the outcome as forced upon one from outside.

related.note: The causative counterpart: 〜を余儀なくさせる makes the cause the subject, while 〜を余儀なくされる makes the forced person the subject.

title: 〜をよそに
meaning: disregarding; ignoring; without regard to
summary: 〜をよそに attaches to a noun — usually someone's worry, opposition, or concern — and says the subject went ahead as if it were none of their business. 親の心配をよそに (heedless of his parents' worry), 周囲の反対をよそに (ignoring everyone's objections). The nuance is often critical: the subject coolly brushes aside something they really ought to have taken into account. It is written and formal in flavor.
pitfalls: The ignored noun is typically other people's feelings, concern, or opposition, and the tone is frequently disapproving.
Do not confuse it with 〜をものともせず: をよそに coolly disregards what one should heed, while をものともせず bravely overcomes a hardship.

examples.ja: 親の心配をよそに、彼は危険な冒険の旅に出かけていった。
examples.en: Heedless of his parents' worry, he set off on a dangerous adventure.
examples.f: ｜親[おや]の｜心配[しんぱい]をよそに、｜彼[かれ]は｜危険[きけん]な｜冒険[ぼうけん]の｜旅[たび]に｜出[で]かけていった。

examples.ja: 住民の反対をよそに、工事は着々と進められた。
examples.en: Ignoring the residents' opposition, the construction pressed steadily ahead.
examples.f: ｜住民[じゅうみん]の｜反対[はんたい]をよそに、｜工事[こうじ]は｜着々[ちゃくちゃく]と｜進[すす]められた。

related.note: をものともせず admiringly overcomes a hardship; をよそに coolly, often selfishly, disregards concern one ought to weigh.
にもかかわらず neutrally says 'despite the fact that'; をよそに specifically shrugs off others' feelings or objections.

title: 〜んがために
meaning: in order to; for the sake of (literary)
summary: 〜んがために is a literary equivalent of ために that expresses a strong, deliberate purpose — 'in order to ~'. It attaches to the same base as a verb's ない-form: 勝たんがために (in order to win), 生き延びんがために (in order to survive). The subject actively wants the goal, so the following clause states what was done to reach it. Modifying a noun it becomes んがための. This is bookish, formal language; ordinary speech uses ために.
structure: Verb［ない form, drop ない］＋んがために
Verb［ない form, drop ない］＋んがための＋Noun
pitfalls: する becomes せんがために, not しんがために.
There is no ない in the form: 行かんがために, not 行かないがために.
It is literary and written; in everyday speech use ために or ように.

examples.ja: 生き延びんがために、人々はあらゆる手段を講じた。
examples.en: In order to survive, people resorted to every means available.
examples.f: ｜生き延[いきの]びんがために、｜人々[ひとびと]はあらゆる｜手段[しゅだん]を｜講[こう]じた。

examples.ja: それは、真実を明らかにせんがための長い闘いであった。
examples.en: It was a long struggle waged in order to bring the truth to light.
examples.f: それは、｜真実[しんじつ]を｜明[あき]らかにせんがための｜長[なが]い｜闘[たたか]いであった。

synonyms.note: べく is likewise a literary 'in order to'; んがために foregrounds the subject's strong desire for the goal, while べく reads more as a stated objective.
ため(に) is the everyday 'in order to'; んがために is its bookish, emphatic counterpart.

title: 〜んばかりに
meaning: as if about to; almost as though (~ing)
summary: 〜んばかりに vividly describes an appearance or manner that looks on the very verge of an action, though the action itself does not actually occur — 泣き出さんばかりに (as if about to burst into tears), 割れんばかりの拍手 (applause as though to split the hall). It attaches to the same base as a verb's ない-form, and appears as んばかりに (adverbial), んばかりだ (sentence end), or んばかりの before a noun. It is literary and heightens the description with exaggeration.
structure: Verb［ない form, drop ない］＋んばかりに／んばかりだ
Verb［ない form, drop ない］＋んばかりの＋Noun
pitfalls: It describes something that merely looks about to happen; the action itself does not actually take place.
する becomes せんばかり, not しんばかり.
There is no ない in the form: 落ちんばかり, not 落ちないばかり.
It is literary and exaggerated, unsuited to plain everyday description.

examples.ja: 彼女は今にも泣き出さんばかりの表情で、こちらを見つめていた。
examples.en: She was gazing at me with a look as though she were about to burst into tears.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜今[いま]にも｜泣[な]き｜出[だ]さんばかりの｜表情[ひょうじょう]で、こちらを｜見[み]つめていた。

examples.ja: 演奏が終わると、会場は割れんばかりの拍手に包まれた。
examples.en: When the performance ended, the hall was engulfed in applause loud enough to split the walls.
examples.f: ｜演奏[えんそう]が｜終[お]わると、｜会場[かいじょう]は｜割[わ]れんばかりの｜拍手[はくしゅ]に｜包[つつ]まれた。

synonyms.note: とばかりに means 'as if to say ~', capturing an attitude; んばかりに means 'as if about to ~', capturing a state or motion on the verge of happening.

related.note: ように見える plainly states 'looks as if'; んばかりに is a heightened, literary 'as if on the very brink of'.
ほど gives a concrete degree ('to the extent that'); んばかりに paints an exaggerated on-the-verge image rather than a measured degree.
